maelgwn-gwynedd.s: Maelgwn Gwynedd was king of Gwynedd in north-west Wales in the 6th century. The writer Gildas denounced him as Maglocunus, 'dragon of the island', the most powerful of the British kings of his day.

mahmud-ii.s: Mahmud II was Ottoman sultan from 1808 to 1839. He centralised the empire, destroying the Janissary corps in 1826 and breaking the power of provincial notables such as the Bushati pashas of Scutari in 1831.

mahmud-ii-seljuk-sultan.s: Mahmud II was Seljuk sultan of the western lands, centred on Iraq and western Iran, from 1118 to 1131. A son of Muhammad I Tapar, he succeeded as a youth while his uncle Sanjar kept Khurasan as senior sultan, and Sanjar defeated him at Saveh in 1119.

mahmud-shah-durrani.s: Mahmud Shah Durrani was a Sadozai ruler of the Durrani Empire, reigning in Kabul from 1801 to 1803 and again from 1809 to 1818. When the Barakzai brothers took over most of the realm, he withdrew to Herat, which he and his son Kamran Shah held as an independent principality.

mahmud-shah-of-malacca.s: Mahmud Shah of Malacca was the last sultan of Malacca, ruling from 1488 until the Portuguese under Afonso de Albuquerque captured the city in 1511. He fled and kept up resistance from Pahang, Bintan and finally Kampar in Sumatra, where he died in 1528.

makea-takau-ariki.s: Makea Takau Ariki was a high chief of the Te Au o Tonga district of Rarotonga, holding the Makea title from 1871. Foreign governments and visiting ships treated her as queen of Rarotonga.

malayan-emergency.s: The Malayan Emergency was a guerrilla war fought from 1948 to 1960 between the forces of the Federation of Malaya and the British Commonwealth and the armed wing of the Malayan Communist Party. Under the Briggs Plan, hundreds of thousands of rural Chinese were resettled into…

malik-ambar.s: Malik Ambar was an Ethiopian-born soldier, brought to India as a slave, who became regent of the Ahmadnagar Sultanate. From around 1600 he led the Deccan's resistance to Mughal expansion, using light Maratha cavalry in guerrilla warfare.

malik-ashraf.s: Malik Ashraf was a Chupanid ruler who controlled Tabriz and much of north-western Iran after the murder of his brother Hasan Kuchak in 1343. His rule was notorious for cruelty and extortion, driving many scholars and merchants to flee.

malik-sarwar.s: Malik Sarwar was a eunuch noble of the Delhi Sultanate who founded the Jaunpur Sultanate. In 1394 the Tughluq sultan made him governor of the eastern provinces with the title Malik al-Sharq, 'lord of the east'.

mamun-ibn-muhammad.s: Ma'mun ibn Muhammad was the emir of Gurganj in northern Khwarazm who founded the Ma'munid dynasty. In 995 he overthrew and killed the last Afrighid shah of Kath, uniting Khwarazm and taking the title Khwarazmshah.

marco-sanudo.s: Marco Sanudo was a Venetian nobleman, nephew of the doge Enrico Dandolo, who took part in the Fourth Crusade. Around 1207 he led a private expedition that conquered Naxos and other islands of the Cyclades, founding the Duchy of the Archipelago.

marcomannic-wars.s: The Marcomannic Wars were a series of conflicts fought from about 166 to 180 CE between the Roman Empire and Germanic and Sarmatian peoples of the middle Danube, including the Marcomanni, Quadi and Iazyges. They began with invasions that reached northern Italy.

marcus-aurelius.s: Marcus Aurelius was Roman emperor from 161 to 180, ruling jointly with Lucius Verus until 169. His reign was dominated by war with Parthia, the Antonine Plague and, on the Danube, the Marcomannic Wars against the Marcomanni, Quadi and Iazyges.

margaret-of-passavant.s: Margaret of Passavant was a noblewoman of the Principality of Achaea and heiress of the Neuilly barons of Passavant. In the 1270s she claimed the barony of Akova through her mother's family, and the lawsuit before the prince's court, recorded in the Chronicle of the Morea,…

marie-louise-duchess-of-parma.s: Marie Louise was an Austrian archduchess, daughter of Emperor Francis I, who married Napoleon in 1810 and bore his son, Napoleon II. After Napoleon's fall the Congress of Vienna gave her the Duchy of Parma, Piacenza and Guastalla for life.

mariano-paredes.s: Mariano Paredes y Arrillaga was a Mexican general and conservative who seized power in a coup in January 1846 and became president. His government refused to negotiate with the United States over Texas, and the Mexican–American War began during his rule.

marib-dam.s: The Marib Dam was an ancient dam across the Wadi Adhanah near Marib in Yemen, built to capture seasonal floods and irrigate two large oases. Its earliest works date to the kingdom of Saba in the early 1st millennium BCE, and later rulers repeatedly repaired it, including the…

marie-of-enghien.s: Marie of Enghien was the heiress of the Lordship of Argos and Nauplia in the Peloponnese, which she inherited from her father Guy of Enghien in the 1370s. Pressed by the Byzantine Despotate of the Morea and the Ottomans, she sold the lordship to Venice in 1388.

marquis-of-pombal.s: The Marquis of Pombal, Sebastião José de Carvalho e Melo, was chief minister of Portugal under King Joseph I from 1750 to 1777. He led the rebuilding of Lisbon after the 1755 earthquake and pursued sweeping reforms, expelling the Jesuits in 1759.

martand-singh.s: Martand Singh was the last ruling maharaja of Rewa in central India, succeeding his father in 1946. After independence he served as Rajpramukh of the union of Vindhya Pradesh, and he later sat in India's parliament.

martin-luther.s: Martin Luther was a German theologian and monk whose Ninety-five Theses of 1517 began the Protestant Reformation. Born at Eisleben in the County of Mansfeld, he refused to recant before Emperor Charles V at the Diet of Worms in 1521.

massif-central.s: The Massif Central is an upland region of south-central France made up of plateaus, old volcanoes and mountains. In the Iron Age it was home to Gallic peoples such as the Arverni, Lemovices and Gabali, several of whom joined Vercingetorix against Caesar in 52 BCE.

mataafa-iosefo.s: Mataʻafa Iosefo was a Samoan high chief and claimant to the kingship of Samoa in the late 19th century. His rivalry with Malietoa Laupepa and later Malietoa Tanumafili I led to wars in which Germany, Britain and the United States intervened.

matilda-of-tuscany.s: Matilda of Canossa was margravine of Tuscany and ruler of wide lands in northern Italy, including Modena, Reggio, Mantua and Ferrara. A firm supporter of the papacy in the Investiture Controversy, she hosted the meeting at Canossa in 1077 where Emperor Henry IV did penance…

matthew-iii-csak.s: Matthew III Csák was a Hungarian magnate who built a vast domain in the north-west of the kingdom, largely in present-day Slovakia, as royal power collapsed around 1300. From his seat at Trenčín he ruled almost as an independent prince.

matyas-rakosi.s: Mátyás Rákosi was the leader of the Hungarian communists who dominated Hungary after the Second World War. Using the police and 'salami tactics' to break up rival parties, he established the Hungarian People's Republic in 1949 and ruled as a Stalinist dictator, with show…

melchor-pacheco.s: Melchor Pacheco was a Spanish conquistador who, with his kinsman Gaspar Pacheco, led the conquest of the eastern provinces of Yucatán in 1544. Their campaigns against Uaymil, Cochuah and Chetumal were notorious for their cruelty, and the region was largely depopulated.

mem-de-sa.s: Mem de Sá was the third governor-general of Portuguese Brazil, serving from 1557 until his death in 1572. With Jesuit support he attacked France Antarctique in Guanabara Bay in 1560 and fought the Tamoio.

meng-chang.s: Meng Chang was the second and last emperor of Later Shu, one of the Ten Kingdoms, reigning from 934 to 965. Under his long and peaceful rule Sichuan prospered, and his court at Chengdu became a centre of culture and printing.

mesa-del-nayar.s: The Mesa del Nayar is a mountain plateau in the Sierra Madre Occidental, in the present-day Mexican state of Nayarit. It was the stronghold of the Cora people, who kept their independence from Spanish rule for almost two centuries after the conquest.

middle-elamite-period.s: The Middle Elamite period, from about 1500 to 1100 BCE, was the phase of Elamite history in which kings ruling from Susa styled themselves kings of Anshan and Susa. Under rulers such as Untash-Napirisha, builder of the ziggurat of Chogha Zanbil, and Shutruk-Nahhunte, who…

middle-march-al-andalus.s: The Middle March was the central frontier district of al-Andalus facing the Christian kingdoms of northern Iberia, with its capital first at Toledo and from 946 at Medinaceli. Under the Umayyads of Córdoba it was held by military governors and frontier lords.

milos-obrenovic.s: Miloš Obrenović was the leader of the Second Serbian Uprising against the Ottomans, launched at Takovo in 1815. Combining fighting with negotiation, he won recognition as hereditary prince of an autonomous Principality of Serbia, confirmed in 1830.

min-saw-mon.s: Min Saw Mon was the last king of the Launggyet period of Arakan and the founder of the Mrauk U kingdom. Driven into exile in Bengal by forces of the Ava kingdom in 1406, he regained his throne in 1429 with an army from the Bengal Sultanate.

ming-sheng.s: Ming Sheng was the second and last ruler of Ming Xia, a state in Sichuan founded by his father Ming Yuzhen during the collapse of the Yuan dynasty. He succeeded as a child in 1366 under regents.

mir-muhanna.s: Mir Muhanna was the ruler of Bandar Rig, a small port on the Persian coast of the Gulf, in the mid 18th century. Notorious for piracy and violence, he attacked shipping and in 1766 seized Kharg island from the Dutch East India Company.

miracles-of-saint-demetrius.s: The Miracles of Saint Demetrius is a Byzantine Greek collection of stories about the patron saint of Thessalonica, compiled in two main books in the 7th century. It describes the sieges of the city by Avars and Slavs and names Slavic groups such as the Drougoubitai,…

mirza-isa-tarkhan.s: Mirza Isa Tarkhan was the founder of the Tarkhan dynasty of lower Sindh. An officer of the Arghun dynasty from a Mongol military family, he seized Thatta in 1554 as Arghun authority collapsed.

mixteca-alta.s: The Mixteca Alta is the highland part of the Mixtec region of western Oaxaca, Mexico. From around 900 it was divided into small kingdoms such as Tilantongo, Teozacoalco and Coixtlahuaca, whose ruling families are recorded in painted deerskin codices.

mohammad-daoud-khan.s: Mohammad Daoud Khan was an Afghan prince and politician who served as prime minister under his cousin King Zahir Shah from 1953 to 1963. In 1973 he overthrew the monarchy and founded the Republic of Afghanistan, ruling as its president.

mohammed-abdullah-hassan.s: Mohammed Abdullah Hassan was a Somali religious leader of the Salihiyya Sufi order who founded the Dervish movement in the 1890s. For two decades his Dervish State fought British, Italian and Ethiopian forces in the Somali lands from forts such as Taleh.

montgenevre-pass.s: The Montgenèvre Pass is a high pass in the Cottian Alps linking the upper Durance valley in France with the Susa valley in Italy. In antiquity it carried a main Roman road from Italy into Gaul, through lands ruled by the Alpine king Cottius and his father Donnus.

moulay-ismail.s: Moulay Ismail was sultan of Morocco from 1672 to 1727, the second ruler of the Alaouite dynasty. He made Meknes a vast imperial city and built the Abid al-Bukhari, an army of enslaved black soldiers.

mount-cameroon.s: Mount Cameroon is an active volcano near the coast of south-western Cameroon and the highest mountain in West and Central Africa. Under German rule its fertile volcanic slopes were turned into plantations worked by forced and recruited labour.

mount-lebanon.s: Mount Lebanon is a mountain range running parallel to the Mediterranean coast of Lebanon, and the name of the historic region in its highlands. Its valleys gave refuge to many communities, notably the Maronite Christians and the Druze.

mount-mycale.s: Mount Mycale is a mountain on the west coast of Anatolia, opposite the island of Samos. On its slopes stood the Panionion, the shrine of Poseidon Helikonios where the Ionian League met, and the city of Priene lay at its foot.

mount-parnassus.s: Mount Parnassus is a limestone mountain in central Greece, above the Gulf of Corinth. On its southern slopes lay the sanctuary of Delphi, home of the oracle of Apollo, and in Greek myth it was sacred to Apollo and the Muses.

mount-tambora.s: Mount Tambora is a volcano on the island of Sumbawa in Indonesia. Its eruption in April 1815, the largest in recorded history, destroyed the kingdoms of Tambora and Pekat and killed tens of thousands of people on Sumbawa and nearby islands.

mountainous-republic-of-the-northern-cau.n: Mountainous Republic of the Northern Caucasus
mountainous-republic-of-the-northern-cau.s: The Mountainous Republic of the Northern Caucasus was a state formed by the mountain peoples of the North Caucasus, including Chechens, Ingush, Dagestanis and Circassians, after the Russian Revolution. It declared independence in May 1918 and sought Ottoman support.

mstislav-of-tmutarakan.s: Mstislav of Tmutarakan was a son of Vladimir the Great who ruled the principality of Tmutarakan on the Taman peninsula. In 1024 he defeated his brother Yaroslav the Wise at Listven, after which they divided the Rus' lands along the Dnieper, with Mstislav ruling the east from…

muhammad-ahmad.s: Muhammad Ahmad was a Sudanese Sufi teacher who in 1881 declared himself the Mahdi and led a revolt against Turco-Egyptian rule in the Sudan. His followers destroyed Egyptian armies and in January 1885 took Khartoum, killing Charles Gordon.

muhammad-al-shaykh-al-wattasi.s: Muhammad al-Shaykh al-Wattasi was the founder of the Wattasid sultanate of Morocco. Of a family that had served the Marinids as viziers, he lost Arzila to Portugal in 1471 and captured Fez in 1472, proclaiming himself sultan.

mohammed-al-shaykh.s: Mohammed al-Shaykh was the Saadi sultan who united Morocco under his dynasty. He captured Agadir from the Portuguese in 1541 and took Fez from the Wattasid Sultanate in 1549, ruling the whole country from then until 1557.

muhammad-amin-naib-of-shamil.s: Muhammad Amin was an Avar religious leader sent by Imam Shamil in 1848 as his naib, or deputy, to the Circassians of the north-western Caucasus. Among the Abadzekhs he built a more centralised Islamic administration with courts, taxes and a standing force.

muhammad-amin-of-kazan.s: Muhammad Amin of Kazan was khan of Kazan three times between 1484 and 1518. Brought to power with the support of Moscow, he ruled at first as a client of Ivan III.

muhammad-ibn-saud.s: Muhammad ibn Saud was emir of Diriyah in Najd from 1727 and the founder of the first Saudi state. In 1744 he made a pact with the religious reformer Muhammad ibn Abd al-Wahhab, joining political power to the Wahhabi movement.

muhammad-ibn-sulayman-al-katib.s: Muhammad ibn Sulayman al-Katib was an Abbasid commander who ended the Tulunid dynasty in Egypt. In 904 and 905 he led a campaign through Syria into Egypt, taking Fustat in January 905.

muhammad-ibn-sulayman-emir-of-tlemcen.s: Muhammad ibn Sulayman was the founder of the Sulaymanid dynasty of Tlemcen in western Algeria in the early 9th century. A son of Sulayman ibn Abd Allah, brother of Idris I, he received Tlemcen from his cousin Idris II around 814.

mukunda-sen.s: Mukunda Sen was a ruler of the Sen dynasty of Palpa in the hills of western Nepal in the 16th century. He is said to have campaigned as far as the Kathmandu Valley.

mungo-park.s: Mungo Park was a Scottish surgeon and explorer who made two journeys into West Africa in search of the course of the Niger. On the first, from 1795 to 1797, he travelled up the Gambia through Wuli and reached the Niger at Segou.

muqrin-ibn-zamil.s: Muqrin ibn Zamil was a ruler of the Jabrid dynasty of eastern Arabia, which held al-Ahsa and the islands of Bahrain. In 1521 a Portuguese and Hormuzi force under Antonio Correia attacked Bahrain; Muqrin was defeated and mortally wounded.

murad-beg-of-kunduz.s: Murad Beg was the Qataghan Uzbek chief who built a powerful state from Kunduz in northern Afghanistan in the early 19th century. He took Balkh, Badakhshan and neighbouring Tajik districts and was notorious for slave raiding.

murong-chao.s: Murong Chao was the second and last emperor of Southern Yan, ruling Shandong from 405 to 410. A nephew of the founder Murong De, he alienated his court and raided the Eastern Jin to seize captives as court musicians.

murong-de.s: Murong De was a Xianbei prince, younger brother of Murong Chui of Later Yan, and founder of Southern Yan. When Northern Wei took the Later Yan capital Zhongshan in 397, he led followers south, proclaimed himself King of Yan in 398 and later emperor, ruling from Guanggu in…

murong-xi.s: Murong Xi was the last emperor of Later Yan, ruling from Longcheng in Liaoning from 401 to 407. He was remembered as extravagant and cruel, wasting resources on palaces and campaigns.

musa-khan-of-bengal.s: Musa Khan was a leader of the Baro-Bhuyans, the confederacy of landholders in eastern Bengal who resisted Mughal expansion. Son of Isa Khan, he took over the resistance after his father's death in 1599.

musa-molo.s: Musa Molo was the ruler of Fuladu, the Fula kingdom of the upper Casamance founded by his father Alfa Molo after the fall of Kaabu. He helped conquer Kantora and other Mandinka lands and played Britain and France against each other.

mustafa-khan-of-shirvan.s: Mustafa Khan was the last khan of Shirvan, ruling from 1792. He reunited the khanate after a period of domination by Quba and built a mountain stronghold at Fit-dagh, balancing between Persia and Russia.

mutesa-ii-of-buganda.s: Mutesa II was kabaka of Buganda from 1939. The British exiled him from 1953 to 1955 after he opposed plans for East African federation, a crisis that strengthened Ganda loyalty.

mohamed-amin-didi.s: Mohamed Amin Didi was a Maldivian politician who became the first president of the Maldives when the sultanate was abolished and a republic proclaimed on 1 January 1953. As prime minister and president he pursued modernising reforms, including the expansion of education and…

mahapadma-nanda.s: Mahapadma Nanda was the founder of the Nanda dynasty of Magadha, who around 345 BCE overthrew the last Shishunaga king. Tradition describes him as a man of low birth, and the Puranas call him a destroyer of the old Kshatriya dynasties.

massacre-of-najran.s: The Massacre of Najran was the killing of the Christian community of Najran, in south-western Arabia, in 523 by the Himyarite king Yusuf As'ar Yath'ar, known in Arab tradition as Dhu Nuwas, who had adopted Judaism. Reports of the martyrs reached Byzantium and Aksum, and in 525…

matilda-i-countess-of-boulogne.s: Matilda I, Countess of Boulogne, held the county in her own right from 1125 and, as wife of Stephen of Blois, was queen of England from 1135. During the civil war known as the Anarchy she defended her husband's cause, raising troops in Kent and securing his release after his…

maximilian-ii-holy-roman-emperor.s: Maximilian II, Holy Roman Emperor, of the Habsburg dynasty, reigned from 1564 to 1576. Sympathetic to Protestantism, he granted religious concessions to the Austrian nobility and sought peace within the Empire, while fighting the Ottomans in Hungary.

ma-zhongying.s: Ma Zhongying was a Hui Muslim warlord of the Ma clique in north-western China. He intervened in the Kumul rebellion of 1931 in Xinjiang against the governor Jin Shuren and fought the governor Sheng Shicai, who called in Soviet help.

maba-diakhou-ba.s: Maba Diakhou Ba was a Muslim cleric and leader of a jihad in the Senegambia region in the 1860s. From his base in Rip he conquered much of the Kingdom of Saloum and spread Islam among the Wolof and Serer, resisting both traditional rulers and the French.

mac-cuu.s: Mạc Cửu was a Chinese merchant and Ming loyalist from Guangdong who settled at Peam, a Cambodian coastal town on the Gulf of Thailand, in the late 17th century. He developed it into the trading port of Hà Tiên, with gambling dens and markets that drew merchants from across the…

mac-dang-dung.s: Mạc Đăng Dung was a Vietnamese general who usurped the throne of the Later Lê dynasty in 1527, founding the Mạc dynasty. A fisherman's son who rose to command the palace guard, he exploited the weakness of the Lê court.

mac-giolla-phadraig.s: Mac Giolla Phádraig, later anglicised as FitzPatrick, was the ruling dynasty of the Irish kingdom of Osraige, named after Giolla Phádraig, a 10th-century king. After the Anglo-Norman invasion they lost the lowlands of Kilkenny but kept lordship in upper Osraige.

mac-kinh-cung.s: Mạc Kính Cung was a member of the Mạc dynasty who proclaimed himself emperor in 1593, after the Trịnh lords retook Thăng Long and executed Mạc Mậu Hợp. He led the Mạc remnant in the mountains of Cao Bằng near the Chinese border, where Ming pressure on the restored Lê court let…

mac-kinh-vu.s: Mạc Kính Vũ was the last ruler of the Mạc dynasty's enclave at Cao Bằng in northern Vietnam. After the Mạc supported the Revolt of the Three Feudatories in China, the Qing withdrew their protection, and in 1677 Trịnh forces conquered Cao Bằng.

macario-sakay.s: Macario Sakay was a Filipino revolutionary and member of the Katipunan who refused to accept American rule after the United States declared the Philippine-American War over in 1902. He revived the Tagalog Republic, or Republic of Katagalugan, and led guerrilla resistance in…

madakari-nayaka-v.s: Madakari Nayaka V was the last of the Nayaka rulers of Chitradurga in central Karnataka, reigning from 1758. He made shifting alliances with Mysore, the Marathas and others.

madan-gopal.s: Madan Gopal was the founder of Sonepur State in western Odisha. A younger son of the Chauhan ruling house of Patna (Patnagarh), he received in 1556 the territory around the confluence of the Mahanadi and Tel rivers, and his descendants ruled Sonepur as a separate Chauhan line…

madan-singh-of-jhalawar.s: Madan Singh was the first ruler of Jhalawar State in Rajputana, reigning from 1838 to 1845. He was the grandson of Zalim Singh, the powerful regent of Kota, and the British created Jhalawar for him out of Kota territory to end the long rivalry between the regent's family and…

madhavaraja-ii.s: Madhavaraja II was the most powerful king of the Shailodbhava dynasty of Kongoda on the coast of Odisha in the 7th century. He began as a feudatory of Shashanka of Gauda and declared his independence after Shashanka's death, issuing land grants in his own name.

madhavavarma-ii.s: Madhavavarma II was the most celebrated king of the Vishnukundina dynasty of the eastern Deccan in the 5th century. His inscriptions credit him with many Vedic sacrifices, including horse sacrifices, which proclaimed his imperial status.

madho-singh-of-kota.s: Madho Singh was the first ruler of Kota State in Rajputana, reigning from 1631 to 1648. A son of Rao Ratan Singh of Bundi, he received Kota as a separate principality from the Mughal emperor Shah Jahan as a reward for military service.

madina-mayurqa.s: Madina Mayurqa was the Arabic name of the city now called Palma, capital of Majorca under Muslim rule from 903 to 1229. It served as the seat of the Taifa of Majorca after 1076 and was sacked by a Pisan and Catalan fleet in 1115.

madinat-al-zahra.s: Madinat al-Zahra was the fortified palace city built from 936 by Abd al-Rahman III a few kilometres west of Córdoba as the seat of the Caliphate of Córdoba. It housed the court, mint and administration in terraced halls and gardens.

madras-state.s: Madras State was the successor of the Madras Presidency in independent India, a province from 1947 and a state of the Republic from 1950. It lost its Telugu districts to Andhra State in 1953 and Malabar to Kerala in 1956, while gaining the Tamil-speaking southern taluks of…

maeda-toshiie.s: Maeda Toshiie was a Japanese warlord of the Sengoku period and founder of the Kaga domain. A companion of Oda Nobunaga and later a leading general of Toyotomi Hideyoshi, he received northern Kaga in 1583 and made Kanazawa his castle town.

maeda-tsunanori.s: Maeda Tsunanori was the fifth lord of the Kaga domain, ruling from Kanazawa for most of the later 17th century. He was a noted patron of scholarship who collected and copied old books and documents, and he encouraged the crafts that made Kanazawa famous, including gold leaf,…

mael-sechnaill-mac-domnaill.s: Máel Sechnaill mac Domnaill was King of Mide and High King of Ireland from 980 to 1002 and again from 1014 to 1022. He defeated the Norse of Dublin at Tara in 980 and took Dublin, but in 1002 submitted to Brian Boru.

maghan-kon-fatta.s: Maghan Kon Fatta is the king of the Manding town of Niani remembered in the oral epic of Sundiata as the father of Sundiata Keita. According to the griots, a prophecy led him to marry the hunchbacked Sogolon, who bore Sundiata.

magna-graecia.s: Magna Graecia, Latin for Great Greece, was the name given to the coastal areas of southern Italy settled by Greek colonists from the 8th century BCE. Cities such as Croton, Sybaris, Taras, Locri and Kaulonia grew rich from farming and trade, produced fine coinage and hosted…

magnus-olafsson.s: Magnus Olafsson was the last king of Mann and the Isles of the Crovan dynasty, reigning from 1254 to 1265. He supported Haakon IV of Norway in the campaign that ended at the Battle of Largs in 1263, then submitted to Alexander III of Scotland.

mahabat-khanji-iii.s: Mahabat Khanji III was the last ruling Nawab of Junagadh, from 1911 to 1948. He is remembered for keeping hundreds of dogs and for protecting the last Asiatic lions in the Gir forest.

mahadji-scindia.s: Mahadji Scindia was the Maratha ruler of Gwalior and the most powerful Indian chief of the late 18th century. Surviving the Maratha defeat at Panipat in 1761, he rebuilt his family's power with a European-trained army under French officers.

mahakam-river.s: The Mahakam River is the main river of East Kalimantan on Borneo, flowing about 900 kilometres from the interior highlands to the Makassar Strait. Its valley was the home of the early kingdom of Kutai, whose Sanskrit yupa inscriptions at Muara Kaman are among the oldest in…

mahamuni-buddha.s: The Mahamuni Buddha is a seated bronze image of the Buddha, the most revered statue in Myanmar. Arakanese tradition says it was cast in the Buddha's lifetime for King Chandrasuriya of Dhanyawadi, and it was the palladium of Arakanese kingdoms for centuries.

maharaja-sukarama.s: Maharaja Sukarama was a king of Negara Daha in southern Borneo known from the Hikayat Banjar chronicle. He named his grandson Raden Samudera as heir, but his son Pangeran Tumenggung seized the throne.

maharana-pratap.s: Maharana Pratap was the Rajput ruler of Mewar from 1572 to 1597. He refused to submit to the Mughal emperor Akbar and fought a Mughal army led by Man Singh I at the Battle of Haldighati in 1576.

mahashivagupta-balarjuna.s: Mahashivagupta Balarjuna was the most famous king of the Panduvamshi dynasty of Dakshina Kosala, ruling from Sirpur in present-day Chhattisgarh for about sixty years in the 7th century. A devotee of Shiva, he also endowed Buddhist monasteries.

mahecor-diouf.s: Mahecor Diouf was the last Maad a Sinig, king of the Serer kingdom of Sine in present-day Senegal. He reigned from 1924, when the kingdom was already under French colonial rule and its kings acted as chiefs.

mahmud-begada.s: Mahmud Begada was Sultan of Gujarat from 1458 to 1511, the greatest ruler of the Muzaffarid dynasty. He conquered Junagadh and Champaner, which he made a new capital.

mahmud-khalji.s: Mahmud Khalji was Sultan of Malwa from 1436 to 1469 and founder of its Khalji dynasty. He seized the throne from the Ghurid line of Hoshang Shah and made Malwa a major power, fighting Mewar, Gujarat, the Bahmani Sultanate and the Delhi Sultanate.

makino-tadanari.s: Makino Tadanari was a Japanese daimyo of the early Edo period and the first Makino lord of Nagaoka. The Tokugawa shogunate moved him to Nagaoka in Echigo province in 1618 with about 74,000 koku, and he built the castle town.

maktoum-bin-butti.s: Maktoum bin Butti was the founder of the Al Maktoum dynasty of Dubai, ruling from 1833 to 1852. In 1833 he led about 800 members of the Al Bu Falasah section of the Bani Yas from Abu Dhabi to settle at Dubai Creek.

malatesta-da-verucchio.s: Malatesta da Verucchio was the founder of the Malatesta lordship of Rimini. As leader of the city's Guelph party, he drove out the Ghibelline Parcitadi family in 1295 and ruled Rimini until his death at about a hundred.

malatesta-family.s: The Malatesta were an Italian noble family who ruled Rimini from 1295 and at times Pesaro, Fano, Cesena and other towns of Romagna and the Marche as lords and papal vicars. Their best-known members include Malatesta da Verucchio and Sigismondo Pandolfo Malatesta, patron of the…

malay-annals.s: The Malay Annals are a Malay literary chronicle of the rulers of Malacca, tracing them from Sang Nila Utama's founding of Singapura to the Portuguese conquest of Malacca in 1511. The best-known version was edited in 1612 at the court of Johor.

malhar-rao-holkar.s: Malhar Rao Holkar was the founder of the Holkar dynasty of Indore. The son of a shepherd, he rose as a cavalry commander under Peshwa Baji Rao I and received lands in Malwa from about 1731.

mali-federation.s: The Mali Federation was a union of Senegal and the Sudanese Republic, the former French Sudan, formed in 1959 within the French Community. It became independent on 20 June 1960 with Dakar as capital, but disputes between Léopold Sédar Senghor and Modibo Keïta led Senegal to…

malietoa-laupepa.s: Malietoa Laupepa was a Samoan paramount chief recognised as King of Samoa for much of the late 19th century. His rule was contested by rival chiefs such as Tupua Tamasese and Mataʻafa Iosefo, each backed by Germany, Britain or the United States.

malik-raja-faruqi.s: Malik Raja Faruqi was the founder of the Faruqi dynasty of Khandesh in the Tapti valley. Granted lands there by Firuz Shah Tughluq of the Delhi Sultanate, he became effectively independent around 1382 as Delhi's authority declined.

malik-shawish.s: Malik Shawish was a king of the Shaigiya, a warlike Arab people of the Nile bend in northern Sudan. In November 1820 he led their cavalry against the Egyptian army of Ismail Pasha, son of Muhammad Ali, at Korti, where the Shaigiya horsemen were defeated by firearms.

malik-sy.s: Malik Sy was a Torodbe Muslim cleric from Futa Toro who founded the state of Bundu in the upper Senegal valley around 1690. He obtained land from the ruler of Gajaaga and attracted settlers to his religious community, ruling with the title almamy.

mallam-ishaku.s: Mallam Ishaku was the Fulani commander who took Daura during the jihad of Usman dan Fodio around 1806 and became its first Fulani emir. The Hausa ruling house fled north and kept a rival court at Zango.

mallam-musa.s: Mallam Musa was a Fulani scholar and follower of Usman dan Fodio who led the jihad forces that captured Zaria, capital of the Hausa kingdom of Zazzau, in 1808. He became the first emir of Zaria under the Sokoto Caliphate and ruled until 1821.

malojirao-nimbalkar.s: Malojirao Nimbalkar was the last ruling Raja of Phaltan, a Maratha princely state in the Deccan, from 1917 until it merged with India in 1948. He had been active in the state's administration and in the movement for responsible government, and after the merger he served as a…

malolos-constitution.s: The Malolos Constitution was the constitution of the First Philippine Republic, drafted by a revolutionary congress at Barasoain church in Malolos, Bulacan, from September 1898 and promulgated in January 1899. Drawing on Spanish and Latin American models, it created a republic…

mamadi-kandia.s: Mamadi Kandia was the last king of Kaarta, the Bambara state of the Massassi dynasty in the western Sahel. In 1854 the Tijani jihad leader Umar Tall conquered Kaarta, took its capital Nioro and executed him.

mammad-amin-rasulzade.s: Mammad Amin Rasulzade was an Azerbaijani politician and writer, leader of the Musavat party and chairman of the national council that proclaimed the Azerbaijan Democratic Republic in 1918, the first parliamentary republic in the Muslim world. After the Red Army overthrew the…

man-singh-ii-of-jaipur.s: Man Singh II was the last ruling Maharaja of Jaipur, from 1922 to 1949. He merged his state into Greater Rajasthan in 1949, with Jaipur as capital, and served as Rajpramukh of Rajasthan until 1956.

man-singh-tomar.s: Man Singh Tomar was the Tomara ruler of Gwalior from 1486 to 1516 and the most celebrated of his line. He resisted repeated attacks by the Lodi sultans of Delhi and built the Man Mandir palace in Gwalior fort, known for its blue tile work.

manabendra-shah.s: Manabendra Shah was the last Maharaja of Tehri Garhwal, ruling from 1946 to 1949. After a popular movement ended the monarchy's authority, he acceded to India and Tehri Garhwal was merged into Uttar Pradesh in 1949.

manaw-gododdin.s: Manaw Gododdin was a district of the Brittonic kingdom of the Gododdin around the head of the Firth of Forth in early medieval Scotland. Its name survives in Clackmannan and Slamannan.

manco-capac.s: Manco Capac is the legendary founder of the Inca dynasty and of the city of Cusco. Inca tradition says he emerged with his siblings from Lake Titicaca or from the cave of Pacaritambo and led his people to the Cusco valley, where his golden staff sank into the earth.

mangkunegara-iv.s: Mangkunegara IV was prince of the Mangkunegaran principality in Surakarta, Java, from 1853 to 1881. He made the house wealthy by building sugar mills and coffee estates and reforming its finances.

mangkunegara-vii.s: Mangkunegara VII was prince of the Mangkunegaran principality in Surakarta from 1916 to 1944. Educated partly in the Netherlands, he supported Javanese cultural nationalism and was a celebrated patron of dance, gamelan music and wayang.

mangrai.s: Mangrai was the founder of the northern Thai kingdom of Lan Na. Ruler of Ngoenyang from about 1259, he founded Chiang Rai in 1262, conquered the Mon kingdom of Hariphunchai in 1292 and founded Chiang Mai as his capital in 1296.

manrique-perez-de-lara.s: Manrique Pérez de Lara was a Castilian magnate of the House of Lara and the first lord of Molina. He held Molina under Castilian overlordship and in 1154 granted it a fuero, a charter of rights for settlers.

mansur-khan.s: Mansur Khan was a Chagatai khan of eastern Moghulistan who ruled from Turpan in the first half of the 16th century. The son of Sultan Ahmad Khan, he waged repeated wars with the Ming dynasty over Hami and campaigned against the Oirats.

mansur-shah-of-malacca.s: Mansur Shah was Sultan of Malacca from 1459 to 1477, the period of the sultanate's greatest expansion. With his bendahara Tun Perak he brought Pahang, Kampar, Siak and other lands on both sides of the Strait of Malacca under Malaccan control.

manuel-amador-guerrero.s: Manuel Amador Guerrero was a Panamanian physician and politician who led the movement for Panama's separation from Colombia in 1903, with the support of the United States. He became the first president of the Republic of Panama, serving from 1904 to 1908, while the United…

manuel-azana.s: Manuel Azaña was a Spanish writer and politician, prime minister of the Second Spanish Republic in 1931 to 1933 and again in 1936, and its president from 1936 to 1939. His governments pursued army reform, land reform, Catalan autonomy and separation of Church and state.

manuel-belgrano.s: Manuel Belgrano was an Argentine economist, politician and general of the wars of independence. A member of the first junta of Buenos Aires in 1810, he led an expedition to Paraguay that was defeated in 1811.

manuel-de-carvalho-pais-de-andrade.n: Manuel de Carvalho Pais de Andrade
manuel-de-carvalho-pais-de-andrade.s: Manuel de Carvalho Pais de Andrade was a Brazilian politician from Pernambuco and president of its provincial government. Opposed to the centralising constitution imposed by Emperor Pedro I, he proclaimed the Confederation of the Equator in Recife on 2 July 1824.

manuel-i-of-portugal.s: Manuel I was King of Portugal from 1495 to 1521, known as the Fortunate. His reign saw Vasco da Gama's voyage to India, Cabral's landing in Brazil and the building of a Portuguese empire in the Indian Ocean, as well as fortified posts on the Atlantic coast of Morocco.

manuel-kantakouzenos.s: Manuel Kantakouzenos was the first despot of the Morea, the Byzantine province in the Peloponnese, ruling from Mystras from 1349 to 1380. Appointed by his father, Emperor John VI Kantakouzenos, he gave the province a permanent ruler, restored order among its quarrelling…

manuel-lobo.s: Manuel Lobo was a Portuguese soldier and colonial governor who founded Colônia do Santíssimo Sacramento in January 1680 on the northern bank of the River Plate, opposite Spanish Buenos Aires. Spanish forces captured the settlement later that year and took him prisoner, and he…

manuel-namuncura.s: Manuel Namuncurá was a Mapuche leader who succeeded his father Juan Calfucurá as head of the Salinas Grandes confederation on the Argentine pampas in 1873. He fought Argentine frontier forces until Julio Argentino Roca's Conquest of the Desert broke his power, and he…

manuel-roxas.s: Manuel Roxas was the first president of the independent Republic of the Philippines, taking office in 1946 after serving as the last president of the Commonwealth. He led reconstruction after the Second World War and signed agreements giving the United States trade privileges…

maqsud-shah.s: Maqsud Shah was the last khan of Kumul (Hami) in eastern Xinjiang, ruling from 1882 under Qing and then Chinese republican overlordship. After his death in 1930 the Xinjiang governor Jin Shuren abolished the khanate and imposed direct rule and new taxes, provoking the Kumul…

marcelo-molina.s: Marcelo Molina was a liberal politician of Quetzaltenango and head of the government of the State of Los Altos, which broke away from Guatemala within the Central American Federation in 1838. The new state was dominated by Ladino liberals ruling a K'iche' and Mam Maya majority.

march-first-movement.s: The March First Movement was a nationwide Korean protest against Japanese colonial rule that began on 1 March 1919 with the reading of a Declaration of Independence in Seoul. Hundreds of thousands joined peaceful demonstrations, which the Japanese authorities suppressed with…

marco-aurelio-soto.s: Marco Aurelio Soto was a liberal president of Honduras from 1876 to 1883. He carried out a programme of liberal reform, issuing new legal codes, separating Church and state, promoting mining and foreign investment and expanding schools.

marco-gradenigo.s: Marco Gradenigo was a Venetian noble settled in Crete and one of the leaders of the Revolt of Saint Titus in 1363. The colonists, angered by taxes and their exclusion from power in Venice, imprisoned the Venetian duke and proclaimed an independent republic under Crete's patron…

marcus-claudius-marcellus.s: Marcus Claudius Marcellus was a Roman general, five times consul, who won the spolia opima in 222 BCE by killing a Gallic king in single combat. In the Second Punic War he besieged Syracuse from 214 BCE and took it in 212 BCE, when Archimedes was killed and the city's art was…

marcus-claudius-marcellus-consul-166-bce.s: Marcus Claudius Marcellus, grandson of the conqueror of Syracuse, was a Roman general who was consul three times, in 166, 155 and 152 BCE. As governor in Hispania he founded Corduba, the later Córdoba, which became the seat of the governors of Hispania Ulterior, and he…

marcus-fulvius-flaccus-consul-125-bce.s: Marcus Fulvius Flaccus was a Roman politician and ally of the Gracchi. As consul in 125 BCE he answered Massalia's appeal and began the Roman campaigns against the Salyes and Vocontii, the first step in the conquest of Transalpine Gaul, celebrating a triumph in 123 BCE.

marcus-fulvius-nobilior.s: Marcus Fulvius Nobilior was a Roman general and consul in 189 BCE. As praetor in Hispania Ulterior he defeated the Carpetani and their allies near Toletum in 193 BCE and took the town in 192 BCE.

marcus-julius-cottius.s: Marcus Julius Cottius was a king of the Ligurian peoples of the western Alps around Segusio (Susa). Rather than resist Augustus's conquest of the Alps, he made peace and was confirmed as ruler with the title of prefect.

marcus-julius-cottius-ii.s: Marcus Julius Cottius II was the last king of the Cottian Alps, a son of Marcus Julius Cottius. The emperor Claudius restored the royal title to him in 44 CE and enlarged his territory.

marcus-lollius.s: Marcus Lollius was a Roman politician and general, consul in 21 BCE and a close associate of Augustus. In 16 BCE, as governor in Gaul, he was defeated by the Sugambri, Usipetes and Tencteri, who captured the eagle of the Fifth Legion, a disaster known as the clades Lolliana.

marcus-perperna-vento.s: Marcus Perperna Vento was a Roman politician of the popular party who joined Quintus Sertorius in Hispania in 77 BCE with the remnants of Lepidus's army. Jealous of his leader, he had Sertorius murdered at a banquet in 73 or 72 BCE and took command, but was quickly defeated by…

margaret-i-of-denmark.s: Margaret I was the ruler of Denmark, Norway and Sweden. Daughter of Valdemar IV of Denmark and widow of Haakon VI of Norway, she governed Denmark from 1375 and Norway from 1380, and won Sweden by defeating King Albert of Mecklenburg in 1389.

margaret-maultasch.s: Margaret Maultasch was Countess of Tyrol from 1335 to 1363, the last of the Meinhardiner line. She expelled her first husband, John Henry of Luxembourg, and married Louis of Bavaria without an annulment, causing a European scandal.

margaret-of-austria-duchess-of-savoy.n: Margaret of Austria, Duchess of Savoy
margaret-of-austria-duchess-of-savoy.s: Margaret of Austria was a daughter of Maximilian I and Mary of Burgundy who governed the Habsburg Netherlands from 1507 to 1515 and from 1519 to 1530 for her nephew Charles V. Her court at Mechelen was a centre of Renaissance art, music and learning.

marghuz-buyruk.s: Marghuz Buyruk was a khan of the Keraites, a Turko-Mongol people of central Mongolia, in the early 12th century. He fought the Tatars, Naimans and Merkits, and was captured by the Tatars and handed over to the Jin dynasty, which put him to death.

maria-ii-of-portugal.s: Maria II was Queen of Portugal from 1826 to 1828 and from 1834 to 1853. Daughter of Pedro I of Brazil, she became queen when her father abdicated the Portuguese throne, but her uncle Miguel usurped it in 1828.

mariano-galvez.s: Mariano Gálvez was a Guatemalan lawyer and liberal politician, head of state of Guatemala within the Central American Federation from 1831 to 1838. He introduced civil marriage, the Livingston penal codes, secular education and land grants to foreign colonists.

mariano-iv-of-arborea.s: Mariano IV was judge (ruler) of Arborea in Sardinia from 1347 to 1376. At first an ally of the Crown of Aragon, he turned against it in 1353 and fought to drive the Aragonese from Sardinia, bringing most of the island under his control.

mariano-ospina-rodriguez.s: Mariano Ospina Rodríguez was a Colombian politician, co-founder of the Conservative Party in 1849 and president from 1857 to 1861. The federal constitution of 1858, adopted under his government, created the Granadine Confederation.

marie-of-montpellier.s: Marie of Montpellier was the heiress of the lordship of Montpellier and Queen of Aragon. In 1204 she married Peter II of Aragon, bringing Montpellier to the Crown of Aragon, and in 1208 she gave birth there to the future James I of Aragon.

mario-lago.s: Mario Lago was an Italian diplomat and governor of the Italian Islands of the Aegean, the Dodecanese, from 1922 to 1936. He invested in roads, farming, archaeology and public buildings, restoring the Palace of the Grand Master in Rhodes and sponsoring Italian rationalist…

marmaduke-grove.s: Marmaduke Grove was a Chilean air force officer and socialist politician. On 4 June 1932 he led the coup that overthrew President Juan Esteban Montero and proclaimed the Socialist Republic of Chile, which lasted only twelve days before a rival coup exiled him.

maroboduus.s: Maroboduus was a king of the Marcomanni who built the first large Germanic kingdom known by name. Raised partly in Rome, he led his people into Bohemia around 9 BCE and drilled an army on Roman lines.

marquis-wen-of-wei.s: Marquis Wen of Wei was the founding ruler of the state of Wei, recognised as a state by the Zhou king in 403 BCE after the partition of Jin. He made Wei the leading power of the early Warring States period through the legal reforms of Li Kui, the irrigation works of Ximen Bao…

marquis-yi-of-zeng.s: Marquis Yi of Zeng was a ruler of the small Zhou state of Zeng, identified with Sui, in present-day Hubei. His tomb at Leigudun near Suizhou, excavated in 1978, held a set of 65 bronze bells, lacquerware, weapons and bamboo-slip writings.

marquis-zhao-of-cai.s: Marquis Zhao of Cai was a ruler of the Zhou state of Cai during the Spring and Autumn period. Pressed by Chu, he allied with Wu and moved his capital to Zhoulai, near Shouxian in Anhui, where he was assassinated in 491 BCE.

marshall-islands.s: The Marshall Islands are two chains of coral atolls in the central Pacific, the Ratak and Ralik chains, home to Marshallese navigators for some two thousand years. They became a German protectorate in 1885, were occupied by Japan in 1914 and by the United States in 1944.

martanda-bhairava-thondaiman.s: Martanda Bhairava Thondaiman was Raja of Pudukkottai, a princely state in Tamil Nadu, from 1886 to 1928. He spent much of his reign in Europe and Australia, and his marriage to the Australian Molly Fink in 1915 caused friction with the British authorities.

marthas-vineyard.s: Martha's Vineyard is an island off the south coast of Cape Cod in Massachusetts, the Wampanoag land of Noepe. English settlers under Thomas Mayhew arrived in the 1640s, and many of the island's Wampanoag became Christian converts.

marthinus-prinsloo.s: Marthinus Prinsloo was a frontier Boer leader in the Graaff-Reinet district of the Cape Colony. In 1795, with Adriaan van Jaarsveld, he led the burghers who expelled the Dutch East India Company's landdrost Honoratus Maynier and declared the short-lived Graaff-Reinet Republic.

marthinus-wessel-pretorius.s: Marthinus Wessel Pretorius was a Boer leader, the son of Andries Pretorius. He was the first president of the South African Republic, from 1857 to 1871, uniting the separate Transvaal communities under the constitution of 1858 and making Pretoria the capital.

martim-afonso-de-sousa.s: Martim Afonso de Sousa was a Portuguese nobleman and naval commander who led the first official colonising expedition to Brazil in 1530 to 1533. In 1532 he founded São Vicente, the first permanent Portuguese town in Brazil, and was granted the captaincy of São Vicente.

martin-de-alarcon.s: Martín de Alarcón was a Spanish soldier and governor of Texas. Sent to strengthen the missions of east Texas against French influence from Louisiana, in 1718 he founded the presidio of San Antonio de Béxar and the mission of San Antonio de Valero, later known as the Alamo, the…

martin-mutschmann.s: Martin Mutschmann was a German textile manufacturer and Nazi official, Gauleiter of Saxony from 1925 and Reich governor of Saxony from 1933 to 1945. He controlled the state government, persecuted political opponents and Jews and failed to prepare Dresden's air-raid defences.

martino-zaccaria.s: Martino Zaccaria was a Genoese lord of Chios from 1314 to 1329. He built a fleet that fought Turkish pirates successfully, struck his own coins and took the title King and Despot of Asia Minor from the Latin claimants to the Byzantine throne.

marwan-ibn-abd-al-aziz.s: Marwan ibn Abd al-Aziz was the qadi, chief judge, of Valencia, whom the city's notables recognised as ruler in 1145 after expelling the Almoravid governor. His brief rule was part of the wave of urban revolts that ended Almoravid power in eastern al-Andalus and created the…

mary-of-burgundy.s: Mary of Burgundy was the only child of Charles the Bold and heiress of the Burgundian State. When her father died in 1477, Louis XI of France seized the duchy of Burgundy, and she married Maximilian of Austria to defend the rest.

mary-of-jever.s: Mary of Jever was the ruler of the lordship of Jever in Frisia from 1517 to 1575, the last of her family. To defend her small land against East Frisia she placed it under Habsburg protection as a fief of Brabant.

masinissa.s: Masinissa was the first king of united Numidia. Son of Gaia of the Massylii, he fought for Carthage in Spain but went over to Rome in 206 BCE, defeated Syphax and led the Numidian cavalry at Zama in 202 BCE.

mateo-de-toro-zambrano.s: Mateo de Toro Zambrano, Count of La Conquista, was a Chilean-born merchant and soldier who served as interim governor of Chile in 1810. On 18 September 1810 a cabildo in Santiago made him president of the First Government Junta, ruling in the name of the captive Ferdinand VII,…

matsudaira-harusato.s: Matsudaira Harusato was the seventh lord of the Matsue domain in Izumo, better known by his tea name Fumai. With his ministers he restored the domain's finances through land reform, flood control and ginseng production.

matsudaira-katamori.s: Matsudaira Katamori was the last lord of the Aizu domain. In 1862 he became Protector of Kyoto, policing the capital with the Shinsengumi and supporting the shogunate against Choshu radicals.

matsudaira-naomasa.s: Matsudaira Naomasa was a Japanese daimyo of the early Edo period, a grandson of Tokugawa Ieyasu and son of Yuki Hideyasu. After holding smaller fiefs, he received the Matsue domain in Izumo in 1638 with about 186,000 koku.

matsudaira-sadaaki.s: Matsudaira Sadaaki was the last lord of the Kuwana domain. As Kyoto deputy from 1864 he worked alongside his elder brother Matsudaira Katamori of Aizu to defend the shogunate's position in the capital.

matsudaira-tadanao.s: Matsudaira Tadanao was the second lord of the Fukui domain in Echizen, a grandson of Tokugawa Ieyasu and son of Yuki Hideyasu. He fought at the siege of Osaka in 1615 but became resentful of his treatment by the shogunate.

matsudaira-yorishige.s: Matsudaira Yorishige was the first lord of the Takamatsu domain in Sanuki, a son of Tokugawa Yorifusa of Mito and elder brother of Tokugawa Mitsukuni. In 1642 he received eastern Sanuki with 120,000 koku, and his line ruled Takamatsu until the Meiji Restoration as close kin of…

matsudaira-yoritaka.s: Matsudaira Yoritaka was a lord of the Takamatsu domain in Sanuki in the mid-18th century. He promoted new industries to repair the domain's finances, especially sugar cane, which led to the fine wasanbon sugar for which the region became famous.

matsudaira-yoshinaga.s: Matsudaira Yoshinaga, known as Shungaku, was lord of the Fukui domain and a leading reformer of the late Edo period. He employed Hashimoto Sanai and Yokoi Shonan and promoted Western learning, medicine and trade.

matthew-orsini.s: Matthew Orsini was the founder of the Orsini county palatine of Cephalonia and Zakynthos in the Ionian Sea. Of an Apulian family, he held the islands by about 1195 and established a hereditary lordship, placing himself in turn under the protection of the Pope, Venice and the…

matthias-von-jagow.s: Matthias von Jagow was the last Catholic Bishop of Brandenburg, from 1526 to 1544. When Elector Joachim II introduced the Lutheran Reformation in Brandenburg in 1539, the bishop accepted the change and took communion in both kinds.

mau-mau-rebellion.s: The Mau Mau rebellion was an armed uprising in colonial Kenya, mainly among the Kikuyu, against British rule and European settlement on African land. The British declared a state of emergency in 1952, detained tens of thousands in camps and killed many thousands of suspected…

maulana-hasanuddin.s: Maulana Hasanuddin was the first ruler of the Banten Sultanate in western Java. Son of Sunan Gunung Jati, he helped take the port of Banten from the Sunda Kingdom around 1527 and became its ruler, spreading Islam and building up the pepper trade.

maulana-yusuf.s: Maulana Yusuf was the second Sultan of Banten in western Java, ruling from 1570 to 1580. In 1579 he captured Pakuan Pajajaran, capital of the Hindu Sunda Kingdom, ending that kingdom and bringing its lands under Banten.

maumoon-abdul-gayoom.s: Maumoon Abdul Gayoom was president of the Maldives from 1978 to 2008, the longest-serving leader in the country's history. His government developed tourism and fisheries and survived a coup attempt by Sri Lankan mercenaries in 1988, defeated with Indian help, but restricted…

maurice-elector-of-saxony.s: Maurice was Duke and then Elector of Saxony of the Albertine line. Though Lutheran, he sided with Emperor Charles V in the Schmalkaldic War and in 1547 received the electoral title taken from his Ernestine cousin.

maurice-duke-of-saxe-zeitz.s: Maurice was the first Duke of Saxe-Zeitz, a younger son of Elector John George I of Saxony. Under his father's will he received Zeitz in 1657 with the secularised bishopric of Naumburg and lands in the Vogtland, founding a Saxon secundogeniture.

maurice-bishop.s: Maurice Bishop was a Grenadian lawyer and leader of the New Jewel Movement, which overthrew Eric Gairy on 13 March 1979. As prime minister of the People's Revolutionary Government he pursued socialist policies and close ties with Cuba.

maurice-fitzthomas-fitzgerald-1st-earl-o.n: Maurice FitzThomas FitzGerald, 1st Earl of Desmond
maurice-fitzthomas-fitzgerald-1st-earl-o.s: Maurice FitzThomas FitzGerald was an Anglo-Norman magnate in Munster, created Earl of Desmond in 1329 with palatine rights over Kerry. He repeatedly clashed with the English administration in Dublin and was imprisoned for rebellion, but was later restored and served as…

maurice-landgrave-of-hesse-kassel.s: Maurice the Learned was Landgrave of Hesse-Kassel from 1592 to 1627. A scholar, composer and patron of the arts, he founded a court school, supported Heinrich Schütz and built the Ottoneum in Kassel, the first permanent theatre in Germany.

maurice-yameogo.s: Maurice Yaméogo was the first president of Upper Volta, now Burkina Faso, leading the territory to independence on 5 August 1960. He established a one-party state under his Voltaic Democratic Union.

mausolus.s: Mausolus was the Hecatomnid ruler of Caria from 377 to 353 BCE, formally a Persian satrap but in practice an independent dynast. He moved his capital to Halicarnassus, which he enlarged and fortified, and extended his power over Lycia and the nearby Greek islands.

mawla-ali.s: Mawla Ali was the son of Muhammad ibn Falah, founder of the Musha'sha movement in Khuzestan. Holding extreme Shia beliefs, he proclaimed that Ali ibn Abi Talib was divine and in 1453 led his followers to sack Najaf, including the shrine of Ali.

maximilian-ii-emanuel-elector-of-bavaria.n: Maximilian II Emanuel, Elector of Bavaria
maximilian-ii-emanuel-elector-of-bavaria.s: Max Emanuel was Elector of Bavaria from 1679 to 1726. He won fame fighting the Ottomans, storming Belgrade in 1688, and governed the Spanish Netherlands from 1692.

maximiliano-hernandez-martinez.s: Maximiliano Hernández Martínez was a Salvadoran general and dictator, president of El Salvador from 1931 to 1944. In 1932 his regime crushed a peasant uprising in western El Salvador in La Matanza, killing thousands, many of them indigenous Pipil.

may-coup-serbia.s: The May Coup was the assassination of King Alexander Obrenović of Serbia and his wife Draga by army officers in Belgrade in June 1903 (May by the Julian calendar). The conspirators, many later linked to the Black Hand, brought Peter I Karađorđević to the throne, ending the…

may-coup-poland.s: The May Coup was the seizure of power in Poland by Marshal Józef Piłsudski from 12 to 14 May 1926. After fighting in Warsaw that killed several hundred people, the government and president resigned.

maysa-wali.s: Maysa Wali is remembered as the first Guelowar king of Sine, a Serer kingdom in present-day Senegal, in the 14th century. Tradition says the Guelowar came from Kaabu, and that he was chosen as king for his wisdom.

mayta-capac.s: Mayta Capac was the fourth ruler of the Kingdom of Cusco in Inca tradition, the son of Lloque Yupanqui. The chronicles describe him as a strong warrior who fought the neighbouring Alcabizas and other peoples of the Cusco valley.

mayurdhwajsinhji-meghrajji-iii.s: Mayurdhwajsinhji Meghrajji III was the last ruling Maharaja of Dhrangadhra, a Jhala Rajput princely state in Kathiawar, from 1942. He acceded to India in 1947, and in 1948 Dhrangadhra was merged into the United State of Saurashtra.

mbegan-ndour.s: Mbegan Ndour was the founder of the Serer kingdom of Saloum in present-day Senegal, around 1494. A warrior linked through his mother to the Guelowar of the Kingdom of Sine, he is said in tradition to have killed Eli Bana, the Muslim cleric who then ruled the region.

mbomou-river.s: The Mbomou River in central Africa forms much of the border between the Central African Republic and the Democratic Republic of the Congo, and joins the Uele to form the Ubangi. In the 19th century its banks were home to Zande and Nzakara sultanates such as Bangassou and…

meguejin-seultue.s: Megüjin Seultü was a chief of the Tatars of eastern Mongolia. In 1196 the Jin dynasty, which had turned against its former Tatar allies, sent an army against him, joined by Temüjin, the future Genghis Khan, and the Keraite ruler Toghrul.

mehdi-frasheri.s: Mehdi Frashëri was an Albanian politician who served as prime minister in 1935 to 1936. After the German occupation of Albania in 1943 he headed the High Regency Council of the nominally independent Albanian state, seeking to protect the country while working with the Germans.

mehdi-ii-of-tarki.s: Mehdi II was shamkhal of Tarki, ruler of the Kumyk principality on the Caspian coast of Dagestan, in the early 19th century. He accepted Russian protection in 1806, received high Russian military rank and remained a loyal ally of the Russian Empire against the Muslim…

mehdi-qoli-khan.s: Mehdi Qoli Khan was the last khan of Karabakh, succeeding his father Ibrahim Khalil Khan in 1806 under Russian overlordship. Fearing loss of power, he fled to Persia in 1822, after which the Russian Empire abolished the khanate and made it a province.

mehmed-pasha-bushati.s: Mehmed Pasha Bushati was an Ottoman Albanian governor, from a powerful family of Shkodër, who was appointed governor of the sanjak of Scutari in 1757. He made the post hereditary in practice and founded the semi-independent Pashalik of Scutari, which his son Kara Mahmud Pasha…

melvin-evans.s: Melvin Evans was a physician and politician from the United States Virgin Islands. Appointed governor in 1969, he became the territory's first elected governor in 1970 and served until 1975.

meng-zhixiang.s: Meng Zhixiang was the founder of Later Shu, one of the Ten Kingdoms of tenth-century China. A general of the Later Tang, he was appointed military governor at Chengdu after the conquest of Former Shu in 925, gradually made himself independent, and in 934 declared himself emperor.

mengujek-gazi.s: Mengujek Gazi was a Turkmen commander who founded the Mengujekid principality in eastern Anatolia after the Battle of Manzikert in 1071. He took Erzincan, Kemah, Divriği and Şebinkarahisar on the upper Euphrates.

menteshe-bey.s: Menteshe Bey was a Turkmen leader who, in the 1260s and 1270s, led raiders into the Byzantine coastlands of Caria in south-western Anatolia, taking the country around Milas, Pechin and Miletus. He founded the beylik that bore his name, one of the first Turkish maritime…

merksha-zarkovic.s: Merksha Žarković was a Serbian nobleman who ruled the Principality of Valona (Vlorë) in southern Albania from about 1396 until his death in 1414. He gained the city and Kanina through his marriage to Ruđina, daughter of Balša II, and held them against growing Ottoman pressure.

merodach-baladan-ii.s: Merodach-baladan II (Marduk-apla-iddina II) was a Chaldean chief of Bit-Yakin who seized the throne of Babylon in 721 BCE with Elamite support and held it until Sargon II of Assyria drove him out in 710 BCE. He briefly regained the city in 703 BCE before Sennacherib expelled…

meryibre-khety.s: Meryibre Khety, often counted as Khety I, was the founder of the Ninth Dynasty of Egypt, ruling from Herakleopolis Magna in the First Intermediate Period. His family, remembered as the House of Khety, held Middle Egypt and the Delta and later contested the south with the…

mesa-vouno.s: Mesa Vouno is a limestone ridge on the south-east of Santorini, between Kamari and Perissa, that carried the ancient city of Thera. Dorian settlers from Laconia founded the town there in the early Iron Age, and its remains include temples, an agora, a theatre and some of the…

mesalim-of-kish.s: Mesalim of Kish was an Early Dynastic king of Kish who reigned around 2600 BCE and claimed authority over other Sumerian cities. Inscriptions from Lagash record that he arbitrated the border dispute between Lagash and Umma over the Gu-edena plain and set up a boundary stone.

mestwin-ii.s: Mestwin II (Mściwój II) was the last duke of Pomerelia from the native Samborides dynasty, ruling the whole of Gdańsk Pomerania from 1271 to 1294. Lacking sons, he named Przemysł II of Greater Poland his heir in the Treaty of Kępno of 1282.

mian-nur-muhammad-kalhoro.s: Mian Nur Muhammad Kalhoro was the most powerful ruler of the Kalhora dynasty of Sindh, governing from 1719 until his death in 1755. He extended Kalhora control over almost all of the lower Indus valley but had to submit to Nader Shah of Persia in 1739 and later paid tribute to…

mian-yar-muhammad-kalhoro.s: Mian Yar Muhammad Kalhoro was the founder of Kalhora rule in Sindh. Head of a family of hereditary Sufi leaders with an armed following, he was recognised by the Mughal Empire around 1701 as governor of parts of northern Sindh, with the title Khuda Yar Khan.

miangul-abdul-wadud.s: Miangul Abdul Wadud, known as Badshah Sahib, was the founder of the princely state of Swat. A grandson of the Akhund of Swat, he was chosen ruler in 1917, united the valley by force and diplomacy and was recognised by Britain as Wali in 1926.

miangul-jahanzeb.s: Miangul Jahanzeb was the second and last Wali of Swat, ruling from 1949 until the state was merged into Pakistan in 1969. The son of Miangul Abdul Wadud, he spent much of the state's revenue on schools, hospitals and colleges centred on Saidu Sharif, and Swat became known for…

michael-i-of-romania.s: Michael I of Romania was the last king of Romania, reigning as a child from 1927 to 1930 and again from 1940 to 1947. In August 1944 he led the coup that removed the dictator Ion Antonescu and took Romania over to the Allies.

michael-of-russia.s: Michael of Russia (Mikhail Fyodorovich Romanov) was the first tsar of the Romanov dynasty, elected by an assembly of the land in 1613 to end the Time of Troubles; the news reached him at the Ipatiev Monastery near Kostroma. His reign, guided at first by his father Patriarch…

michael-ii-komnenos-doukas.s: Michael II Komnenos Doukas was ruler of the Despotate of Epirus from about 1230 until his death around 1268. He restored Epirote power from Arta and contested the Byzantine inheritance with the Empire of Nicaea, allying with Manfred of Sicily and the Prince of Achaea, but…

michael-joseph-savage.s: Michael Joseph Savage was the first Labour prime minister of New Zealand, serving from 1935 until his death in 1940. Born in Australia, he led a government that built state housing, guaranteed prices for dairy farmers and passed the Social Security Act of 1938, laying the…

michael-obrenovic.s: Michael Obrenović (Mihailo Obrenović III) was prince of Serbia from 1839 to 1842 and again from 1860 until his assassination in 1868. In his second reign he modernised the army and administration and worked for a Balkan alliance against the Ottomans.

michael-somare.s: Michael Somare was the founding prime minister of Papua New Guinea. He helped found the Pangu Party in 1967, which pressed for self-government, became chief minister in 1972 and led the territory to self-government in 1973 and independence on 16 September 1975.

michael-the-brave.s: Michael the Brave (Mihai Viteazul) was prince of Wallachia from 1593 to 1601. He rebelled against Ottoman overlordship, winning at Călugăreni in 1595, and in 1599 and 1600 took control of Transylvania and Moldavia, briefly uniting the three principalities under one ruler.

michel-micombero.s: Michel Micombero was a Burundian army officer who became the country's first president. As prime minister he deposed the young king Ntare V in November 1966 and proclaimed the Republic of Burundi, ruling through the Tutsi-dominated army and the UPRONA party.

mieszko-iii-the-old.s: Mieszko III the Old was a Piast duke of Greater Poland, which he received under the testament of his father Bolesław III Wrymouth in 1138. He was also high duke of Poland, ruling from Kraków several times between 1173 and his death in 1202, but his harsh rule provoked revolts.

mieszko-iv-tanglefoot.s: Mieszko IV Tanglefoot was a Piast duke of Silesia, son of Władysław II the Exile. In 1172 he received a duchy around Racibórz, and in 1202 he added Opole, creating the Duchy of Opole and Racibórz, the core of Upper Silesia.

miguel-diaz-canel.s: Miguel Díaz-Canel is a Cuban politician who succeeded Raúl Castro as president in 2018, the first leader since the revolution from outside the Castro family. He also became first secretary of the Communist Party in 2021.

miguel-tacon.s: Miguel Tacón was a Spanish general who served as captain-general of Cuba from 1834 to 1838. He ruled with near-absolute powers, suppressed crime and dissent in Havana and carried out major public works, including a prison, roads, markets and the Tacón Theatre.

mihail-gerdzhikov.s: Mihail Gerdzhikov was a Bulgarian revolutionary of anarchist sympathies and a leader of the Internal Macedonian-Adrianople Revolutionary Organisation. During the Ilinden-Preobrazhenie uprising of August 1903 he led the insurgents in the Strandzha mountains, where they set up a…

mihajlo-visevic.s: Mihajlo Višević was ruler of Zachlumia (Hum), between the Neretva and Dubrovnik, in the early 10th century. An ally of Simeon I of Bulgaria, he captured the Serbian prince Peter Gojniković and handed him to the Bulgarians in 917.

mihira-bhoja.s: Mihira Bhoja (Bhoja I) was the most powerful king of the Gurjara-Pratihara dynasty, ruling from Kannauj from about 836 to 885. He rebuilt Pratihara power after earlier defeats and ruled an empire from Punjab to the borders of Bengal, contending with the Pala and Rashtrakuta…

mikhail-andreyevich-of-vereya.s: Mikhail Andreyevich of Vereya was a Russian appanage prince, son of Andrei of Mozhaysk, who ruled Vereya together with Beloozero from 1432. Unlike his brother Ivan of Mozhaysk he stayed loyal to Vasily II of Moscow during the civil war of the mid-15th century.

mikhail-ermolaevich.s: Mikhail Ermolaevich was a prince of Great Perm, the Komi land on the upper Kama, in the 15th century. A baptised ruler who served the Grand Duchy of Moscow while governing the local communities, he was taken prisoner when Ivan III sent an army that captured Cherdyn in 1472.

mikhail-of-tver.s: Mikhail of Tver (Mikhail Yaroslavich) was prince of Tver from 1285 and grand prince of Vladimir from 1305. His rivalry with Yury of Moscow for the favour of the Golden Horde led to war; he defeated Yury in 1317 but was summoned to the Horde, tried and executed in 1318.

mikheil-saakashvili.s: Mikheil Saakashvili is a Georgian politician who led the Rose Revolution of 2003 and was president of Georgia from 2004 to 2013. His government fought corruption, rebuilt the police and sought membership of NATO and the European Union, and his term included the 2008 war with…

milan-acimovic.s: Milan Aćimović was a Serbian police official and politician who served as interior minister of Yugoslavia in 1939. After the German conquest of 1941 he headed the Commissioner Government in occupied Serbia, which proved unable to contain the uprising of that summer.

milan-cathedral.s: Milan Cathedral is the Gothic cathedral of Milan, begun in 1386 under Gian Galeazzo Visconti and completed only in the 19th and 20th centuries. Built largely of pinkish-white Candoglia marble and crowned with a forest of spires, it is among the largest churches in the world.

milo-dukanovic.s: Milo Đukanović is a Montenegrin politician who dominated the country for three decades, serving several times as prime minister from 1991 and as president in 1998–2002 and 2018–2023. In the late 1990s he broke with Slobodan Milošević and adopted the Deutsche Mark and later the…

milton-margai.s: Milton Margai was a physician and the first prime minister of Sierra Leone. A founder of the Sierra Leone People's Party in 1951, he led the colonial government under the constitutional reforms of the 1950s, negotiated independence and became prime minister when Sierra Leone…

milton-obote.s: Milton Obote was Uganda's first prime minister at independence in 1962 and later its president. In 1966 he suspended the constitution and sent troops against the palace of the kabaka of Buganda, Mutesa II, and in 1967 he abolished the kingdoms.

mir-fateh-ali-khan-talpur.s: Mir Fateh Ali Khan Talpur was the founder of Talpur rule in Sindh. A Baloch chief whose family had served the Kalhora dynasty, he defeated the last Kalhora ruler at the Battle of Halani in 1783 and was recognised as ruler of Sindh by the Durrani Empire.

mir-muhammad-kor.s: Mir Muhammad Kor ('the one-eyed') was emir of Soran from about 1814 to 1836. Ruling from Rawanduz in the mountains of northern Iraq, he expanded the emirate across much of southern Kurdistan, set up a cannon foundry and armoury and struck his own coins.

mir-mustafa-khan.s: Mir Mustafa Khan was khan of Talysh, on the south-western coast of the Caspian, from 1786 until his death in 1814. Threatened by Qajar Iran, he sought Russian protection and sided with Russia in the Russo-Persian War of 1804–1813.

mir-nasir-of-bandar-rig.s: Mir Nasir of Bandar Rig was the Arab lord of the port of Bandar Rig on the Persian shore of the Gulf in the mid-18th century. A member of the Za'ab family, he governed the town independently after central authority collapsed on the death of Nader Shah in 1747, and dealt with…

mir-osman-ali-khan.s: Mir Osman Ali Khan was the seventh and last Nizam of Hyderabad, ruling from 1911 to 1948. Reputed the richest man in the world, he founded Osmania University in 1918 with Urdu as its medium of instruction and funded railways, hospitals and public buildings.

mircea-the-elder.s: Mircea the Elder was prince of Wallachia from 1386 to 1418, with a short interruption in the 1390s. He extended his rule over Dobruja and the lower Danube, fought the Ottomans at Rovine in 1395, where Marko Kraljević fell on the Ottoman side, and joined the Crusade of…

mirza-jani-beg-tarkhan.s: Mirza Jani Beg Tarkhan was the last independent ruler of the Tarkhan dynasty of Sindh, reigning from Thatta from 1585. In 1591 he was defeated by Akbar's general Abdul Rahim Khan-i-Khanan and submitted to the Mughal Empire.

mitinti-of-ashdod.s: Mitinti of Ashdod was king of the Philistine city of Ashdod around 700 BCE. He appears in the annals of Sennacherib of Assyria among the western rulers who brought tribute during the campaign of 701 BCE.

miyoshi-nagayoshi.s: Miyoshi Nagayoshi was a Japanese warlord of the Sengoku period who dominated Kyoto and the home provinces in the 1550s. A retainer of the Hosokawa deputy shoguns, he turned against Hosokawa Harumoto in 1549, defeated him at Eguchi and drove the shogun Ashikaga Yoshiteru from…

moch-couoh.s: Moch Couoh was the Maya lord of Champotón on the western coast of the Yucatán Peninsula. In 1517 his warriors attacked the Spanish expedition of Francisco Hernández de Córdoba when it landed for water, killing many men and mortally wounding its leader.

modibbo-adama.s: Modibbo Adama was a Fulani scholar who founded the Adamawa Emirate, the largest emirate of the Sokoto Caliphate. Around 1806 or 1809 he received a flag from Usman dan Fodio to spread the jihad in Fombina, the southern lands, and conquered or absorbed many peoples across what…

mohamed-el-mokrani.s: Mohamed El Mokrani was an Algerian noble of the Mokrani family, lords of the Medjana and heirs of the Kingdom of Ait Abbas, who had served the French as local chiefs. In March 1871 he launched the largest uprising against French rule in Algeria since the conquest, joined by…

mohamed-nasheed.s: Mohamed Nasheed is a Maldivian politician who became the country's first democratically elected president in 2008, under a new multiparty constitution, ending the thirty-year rule of Maumoon Abdul Gayoom. He gained international attention for his climate campaigning on behalf…

mohammad-mosaddegh.s: Mohammad Mosaddegh was an Iranian nationalist who served as prime minister from 1951 to 1953. He led the nationalisation of the Anglo-Iranian Oil Company in 1951, provoking a British boycott of Iranian oil.

mohammad-nadir-shah.s: Mohammad Nadir Shah was king of Afghanistan from 1929 to 1933. A general from the Musahiban branch of the royal family, he overthrew the Saqqawist ruler Habibullah Kalakani in 1929 and took the throne.

mohammad-najibullah.s: Mohammad Najibullah was leader of the Democratic Republic of Afghanistan from 1986 to 1992, having earlier headed the KHAD secret police. He promoted a policy of national reconciliation and renamed the state the Republic of Afghanistan.

mohammad-reza-pahlavi.s: Mohammad Reza Pahlavi was the last shah of Iran, reigning from 1941, when the Anglo-Soviet invasion forced his father Reza Shah to abdicate, until 1979. Restored to full power by the 1953 coup against Mohammad Mosaddegh, he launched the White Revolution of land reform and…

mohammad-zahir-shah.s: Mohammad Zahir Shah was the last king of Afghanistan, reigning from 1933, after the assassination of his father Mohammad Nadir Shah, until 1973. For two decades power lay with his uncles and then his cousin Mohammad Daoud Khan, but the 1964 constitution introduced a…

mohammed-el-kebir.s: Mohammed el-Kebir was bey of the Beylik of the West, the western province of the Regency of Algiers, from 1779 to 1797. He besieged Spanish-held Oran and took possession of it in 1792, after Spain agreed to leave following the earthquake of 1790, and made it his capital.

mohammed-v-of-morocco.s: Mohammed V of Morocco was sultan from 1927 and the first king of independent Morocco. He supported the nationalist movement against the French protectorate, and his deposition and exile by France in 1953 provoked widespread unrest.

mohammed-vi-of-morocco.s: Mohammed VI of Morocco has been king since 1999, succeeding his father Hassan II. He reformed family law in 2004, extending women's rights, and after the protests of 2011 approved a new constitution that gave more power to parliament while keeping wide royal authority.

molopo-river.s: The Molopo River is a mostly dry river of southern Africa that rises near Mahikeng and flows west towards the Orange River. In 1885 Britain made it the dividing line between the Crown colony of British Bechuanaland to the south and the Bechuanaland Protectorate to the north,…

molotov-ribbentrop-pact.s: The Molotov–Ribbentrop Pact was the non-aggression treaty signed by Nazi Germany and the Soviet Union in Moscow on 23 August 1939. Its secret protocols divided eastern Europe into spheres of influence, opening the way to the joint invasion of Poland and to the Soviet…

mona-passage.s: The Mona Passage is the strait between Hispaniola and Puerto Rico, linking the Atlantic Ocean with the Caribbean Sea. About 130 km wide and broken by the islands of Mona, Monito and Desecheo, it was crossed by Taíno canoes long before Spanish contact, connecting the chiefdom…

moncef-bey.s: Moncef Bey (Muhammad VII al-Munsif) was bey of Tunis from June 1942 to May 1943. Sympathetic to the nationalists, he asserted his authority against the French resident-general and appointed a government without French approval.

mongol-oirat-code.s: The Mongol-Oirat Code was a law code agreed in 1640 at an assembly of Oirat and Khalkha Mongol princes, at which Erdeni Batur of the Dzungars played a leading part. Aimed at uniting the Mongols against outside threats, it regulated relations between princes, military duties,…

monks-mound.s: Monks Mound is the largest earthwork at Cahokia, near modern St Louis, and the largest prehistoric earthen structure in the Americas. Built in stages from about 950 to 1100, it rises in terraces to about 30 metres and covers some 6 hectares at its base.

mont-sainte-odile.s: Mont Sainte-Odile is a sandstone mountain of about 764 metres in the Vosges above Obernai in Alsace. In the late 7th century Odile, daughter of the Alsatian duke Adalric, founded the convent of Hohenburg on its summit, and as patron saint of Alsace she made it the region's…

monte-cassino.s: Monte Cassino is a hill above Cassino in southern Italy where Benedict of Nursia founded his monastery around 529, the cradle of the Benedictine order. Sacked by the Lombards around 577 and by Arab raiders in 883, it was rebuilt and became a great centre of learning and…

monte-cavo.s: Monte Cavo is the second-highest peak of the Alban Hills south-east of Rome, rising to about 950 metres above Lake Albano. In antiquity, as Mons Albanus, it carried the sanctuary of Jupiter Latiaris, where the Latin peoples and later the Roman consuls celebrated the annual…

moravian-church.s: The Moravian Church, or Unitas Fratrum, is a Protestant church descended from the Bohemian Brethren of the 15th century. Refugees from Moravia renewed it in 1722 at Herrnhut in Saxony, on the estate of Count Nicolaus von Zinzendorf.

moray-firth.s: The Moray Firth is a large inlet of the North Sea in north-eastern Scotland, reaching inland to Inverness. Its fertile coastal lowlands formed the heart of the Pictish kingdom of Fortriu and later of the medieval kingdom or mormaerdom of Moray, whose rulers, including Macbeth,…

moroka-ii.s: Moroka II was chief of the Seleka branch of the Barolong, a Tswana people, until his death in 1880. In 1833, with Wesleyan missionaries, he led his people from Platberg on the Vaal to Thaba Nchu, where a large town grew up.

morro-castle-havana.s: Morro Castle (Castillo de los Tres Reyes Magos del Morro) is the fortress guarding the entrance to Havana harbour, built by the Spanish from 1589 to about 1630. In 1762 a British army besieged it for weeks; its commander Luis Vicente de Velasco was mortally wounded when it was…

moti-singh-of-poonch.s: Moti Singh of Poonch was the first raja of Poonch, a hill principality in the western Pir Panjal subordinate to Jammu and Kashmir. A son of Dhian Singh, minister of the Sikh Empire at Lahore, and nephew of Maharaja Gulab Singh, he received Poonch from Gulab Singh in 1850 as a…
