She acted as regent for her sons and was a leading literary patron, for whom Chrétien de Troyes wrote his Lancelot and Andreas…

montmedy.s: Montmédy is a small town in the Meuse department of north-eastern France, near the Belgian border, dominated by a fortified citadel on a hill. Founded by the counts of Chiny in the 13th century, it later belonged to Luxembourg and the Spanish Netherlands until France took it…

mondego.s: The Mondego is the longest river lying entirely within Portugal, about 230 kilometres long, rising in the Serra da Estrela and flowing past Coimbra to the Atlantic at Figueira da Foz. In the 9th to 11th centuries it marked the shifting frontier between the Christian north and…

margaret-countess-of-comminges.s: Margaret was countess of Comminges from childhood until her death in 1443, the last of the line of counts. Her three marriages, the third to Mathieu de Foix, led to long disputes over her inheritance, and she spent many years imprisoned by her last husband.

minden.s: Minden is a city on the Weser in North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany, just north of where the river breaks through the hills at the Porta Westfalica. Charlemagne founded a bishopric there around 800, and its prince-bishops ruled a territory along the Weser until it passed to…

medinaceli.s: Medinaceli is a small hilltop town in the province of Soria, Castile, Spain, above the Jalón valley. It keeps a Roman triumphal arch and was a key fortress of al-Andalus, the base of its Middle March against the Christian kingdoms; the chamberlain al-Mansur died there in 1002.

montbrison.s: Montbrison is a town in the Loire department of central France, on the plain of Forez. It grew around a castle of the counts of Forez and was their capital, with the collegiate church of Notre-Dame-d'Espérance founded in 1223.

muri-abbey.s: Muri Abbey is a former Benedictine monastery at Muri in the Swiss canton of Aargau, founded in 1027 by Ita of Lorraine and Count Radbot as the family monastery of the early Habsburgs. Its monks helped found Engelberg Abbey in 1120.

mons.s: Mons is a city in southern Belgium, capital of the Walloon province of Hainaut. It grew around a castle and the abbey of Saint Waltrude and was the seat of the counts of Hainaut for centuries.

meiningen.s: Meiningen is a town in southern Thuringia, Germany, on the Werra between the Thuringian Forest and the Rhön. Held by the bishops of Würzburg and then the counts of Henneberg, it passed to the Saxon Wettins and from 1680 was the capital of the Duchy of Saxe-Meiningen.

mark-sittich-von-hohenems-altemps.s: Mark Sittich von Hohenems (1533–1595), known in Italy as Marco Sittico Altemps, was a cardinal and a nephew of Pope Pius IV, who raised him to the cardinalate in 1561. He served as papal legate at the Council of Trent and as Bishop of Constance, and in Rome he acquired the…

maximilian-friedrich-von-konigsegg-rothe.s: Maximilian Friedrich von Königsegg-Rothenfels (1708–1784) was Archbishop-Elector of Cologne from 1761 and Prince-Bishop of Münster from 1762 until his death. An Enlightenment ruler guided by his minister Caspar Anton von Belderbusch, he reformed schools and administration from…

maximilian-of-egmond.s: Maximilian of Egmond (1509–1548), Count of Buren, was a general and stadtholder of Friesland in the service of Emperor Charles V. He led an army from the Netherlands to join the emperor in the Schmalkaldic War of 1546–1547 and received the county of Lingen, confiscated from…

maximin-of-trier.s: Maximin of Trier (died c. 346) was Bishop of Trier from about 329 and is venerated as a saint.

macon.s: Mâcon is a city in Burgundy, eastern France, on the Saône, prefecture of the Saône-et-Loire department. A Gallic and Roman town (Matisco), it was the seat of a bishopric and of the counts of the Mâconnais, whose county was sold to Louis IX in 1239.

monzon-de-campos.s: Monzón de Campos is a village in the province of Palencia, Castile and León, Spain, on the Carrión in the Tierra de Campos. Its castle was the seat of the County of Monzón, created around 943 by Ramiro II of León for Assur Fernández and ruled by the Ansúrez family.

monzon.s: Monzón is a town in the province of Huesca, Aragon, Spain, on the Cinca. Its castle, taken from the Muslims in 1089, later belonged to the Knights Templar, who brought up the young King James I there.

monastery-of-sant-joan-de-les-abadesses.n: Monastery of Sant Joan de les Abadesses
monastery-of-sant-joan-de-les-abadesses.s: The Monastery of Sant Joan de les Abadesses is a religious house in the Ripollès district of Catalonia, founded around 887 by Wilfred the Hairy for his daughter Emma, its first abbess. One of the earliest nunneries in Catalonia, it anchored the resettlement of the Pyrenean…

monastery-of-santa-maria-de-ripoll.n: Monastery of Santa Maria de Ripoll
monastery-of-santa-maria-de-ripoll.s: The Monastery of Santa Maria de Ripoll is a Benedictine abbey in the Catalan Pyrenees, founded around 880 by Wilfred the Hairy, who was buried there. Under Abbot Oliba in the 11th century its scriptorium and library made it one of Europe's leading centres of learning, where…

monastery-of-santa-maria-de-gerri.n: Monastery of Santa Maria de Gerri
monastery-of-santa-maria-de-gerri.s: The Monastery of Santa Maria de Gerri is a Benedictine abbey at Gerri de la Sal in the Noguera Pallaresa valley of the Catalan Pyrenees. Founded in the early 9th century, it became one of the leading religious houses of the county of Pallars, and its abbots held lordship over…

mortagne-au-perche.s: Mortagne-au-Perche is a town in the Orne department of Normandy, historic capital of the Perche. Its lords, who also held Nogent, became counts of Perche in the 11th century and ruled the county until their line ended in 1226.

minho-river.s: The Minho is a river of the north-western Iberian Peninsula, rising in Galicia and forming the last stretch of the border between Spain and Portugal before reaching the Atlantic. In the Middle Ages the land between the Minho and the Douro formed the core of the County of…

mozarabs.s: The Mozarabs were Christians who lived under Muslim rule in al-Andalus, adopting Arabic language and culture while keeping their faith. Many migrated north to the Christian kingdoms from the 9th century, where they helped resettle frontier lands in León, Castile and Portugal.

mumadona-dias.s: Mumadona Dias was a Galician-Portuguese noblewoman who governed the County of Portugal in the mid-10th century after the death of her husband, Count Hermenegildo Gonçalves. She founded a monastery at Guimarães and built a castle to protect it from Norse and Muslim raiders, the…

marienstatt-abbey.s: Marienstatt Abbey is a Cistercian monastery in the Westerwald near Hachenburg, Rhineland-Palatinate. Founded in the early 13th century under the patronage of the counts of Sayn, it has an early Gothic church, one of the first Gothic buildings east of the Rhine.

mecklenburg-vorpommern.s: Mecklenburg-Vorpommern is a state in north-eastern Germany on the Baltic coast, with Schwerin as its capital and Rostock as its largest city. It unites the historic lands of Mecklenburg with the western part of Pomerania left in Germany after 1945, including the island of Rügen.

merano.s: Merano is a spa town in South Tyrol, northern Italy, on the Passer near its junction with the Adige. Lying below Tyrol Castle, it was the chief town of the county of Tyrol until the princes moved their residence to Innsbruck in the 15th century.

meisenheim.s: Meisenheim is a small town on the Glan in Rhineland-Palatinate, with a well-preserved medieval centre. It was a residence of the counts of Veldenz and later of the dukes of Palatinate-Zweibrücken, whose Gothic Schlosskirche holds their tombs.

mennonites.s: The Mennonites are Anabaptist Christians named after Menno Simons, a Frisian former priest who organised scattered Anabaptist groups in the 1530s and 1540s. Rejecting infant baptism, oaths and military service, they suffered persecution and settled wherever rulers tolerated…

middelburg.s: Middelburg is the capital of the Dutch province of Zeeland, on the former island of Walcheren. It grew around a fortified site and an abbey in the Middle Ages and became a leading trading town, the chief town of the county of Zeeland and later the seat of a chamber of the…

margaritus-of-brindisi.s: Margaritus of Brindisi was an admiral of the Norman Kingdom of Sicily. Commanding the fleet of William II, he seized Cephalonia, Zakynthos and other Ionian islands from Byzantium in 1185 and became their first count palatine.

marcus-antonius-creticus.s: Marcus Antonius Creticus was a Roman praetor given a wide command against Mediterranean pirates in 74 BCE. His attack on Crete, accused of supporting the pirates, ended in a heavy naval defeat near Kydonia around 71 BCE, and he died soon afterwards; the surname Creticus…

menli-i-giray.s: Meñli I Giray was khan of Crimea, with interruptions, from 1468 to 1515. After the Ottomans took the Crimean coast in 1475 he accepted Ottoman overlordship, and in 1502 he destroyed the Great Horde, the last remnant of the Golden Horde.

maciej-sulkiewicz.s: Maciej Sulkiewicz (Suleyman Sulkevich) was a Lithuanian Tatar general of the Russian army. In June 1918, under German occupation, he became head of the Crimean Regional Government, which claimed autonomy and resisted absorption by the Ukrainian State.

myscellus-of-rhypes.s: Myscellus of Rhypes was the legendary founder (oikist) of Croton in southern Italy, around 710 BCE. Ancient writers such as Strabo and Diodorus say that the Delphic oracle sent him, an Achaean from the town of Rhypes, to found the city, and that he would have preferred the…

mustapha-harun.s: Mustapha Harun was a Malaysian politician from Sabah of Suluk and Bajau descent. A leading figure in the negotiations that brought North Borneo into Malaysia in 1963, he became Sabah's first head of state and, as chief minister from 1967 to 1975, dominated the state's politics…

mandvi-kutch.s: Mandvi is a port town in the Kutch district of Gujarat, India, on the Gulf of Kutch at the mouth of the Rukmavati river. For centuries it was the main seaport of Cutch, whose merchants and sailors traded with Arabia, the Persian Gulf and East Africa, and it remains known for…

munich-agreement.s: The Munich Agreement was concluded on 29–30 September 1938 by Germany, Britain, France and Italy, without Czechoslovakia taking part. It required Czechoslovakia to cede the Sudetenland to Nazi Germany, which Hitler had threatened to seize by force.

margiana.s: Margiana was a historical region centred on the oasis of the Murghab river in modern Turkmenistan, around the city of Merv. Home to Bronze Age sites such as Gonur Tepe, it later formed a province of the Achaemenid, Seleucid and Parthian empires and was a key stage on the…

movilla-abbey.s: Movilla Abbey was a monastery at Newtownards in County Down, Northern Ireland, founded around 540 by Saint Finnian of Movilla. It became one of the leading monastic schools of early medieval Ulster and is said to have taught Saint Columba.

masalit-people.s: The Masalit are a people of western Darfur in Sudan and eastern Chad, speaking a language of the Maban family and living mainly as farmers. In the late 19th century they formed the sultanate of Dar Masalit, with its capital at El Geneina, which resisted both Darfur and the…

moel-hiraddug.s: Moel Hiraddug is an Iron Age hillfort near Dyserth in Denbighshire, at the northern end of the Clwydian Range in north-east Wales. Its multiple ramparts enclosed a long hilltop, and finds include a decorated bronze plaque of the late Iron Age.

maimun-palace.s: The Maimun Palace is the palace of the sultans of Deli in Medan, North Sumatra, Indonesia, built between 1888 and 1891 by Sultan Ma'mun Al Rasyid Perkasa Alam. Paid for by the sultanate's tobacco revenues, it mixes Malay, Islamic, Indian and European styles.

mamun-al-rasyid-perkasa-alam.s: Ma'mun Al Rasyid Perkasa Alam was sultan of Deli, on the east coast of Sumatra, from 1873 to 1924. His reign coincided with the boom of the Dutch-supervised tobacco plantations, whose land rents made the sultanate rich.

michael-i-komnenos-doukas.s: Michael I Komnenos Doukas was the founder of the Despotate of Epirus, a Byzantine successor state set up after the Fourth Crusade. A cousin of the emperors Isaac II and Alexios III Angelos, he seized Epirus around 1205 and made Arta his capital, then extended his rule over…

melnik.s: Melnik is a small town in south-western Bulgaria, near the Struma valley, set among sandstone pillars known as the Melnik pyramids. In the 13th century it was the capital of the despot Alexius Slav, and it prospered in later centuries from wine and trade.

manuel-gomes-da-costa.s: Manuel Gomes da Costa was a Portuguese general who launched the military coup of 28 May 1926 that overthrew the First Portuguese Republic. In the First World War he had commanded a division of the Portuguese Expeditionary Corps in Flanders.

modern-revolutionary-party.s: The Modern Revolutionary Party is a political party of the Dominican Republic, founded in 2014 by a breakaway from the Dominican Revolutionary Party. Its candidate Luis Abinader won the presidency in 2020, ending sixteen years of government by the Dominican Liberation Party,…

morlaix.s: Morlaix is a port town in Finistère, north-western Brittany, at the head of a long estuary opening onto the English Channel. In the late Middle Ages and early modern period it prospered from the trade in linen cloth with England and Spain, and in 1522 it was sacked by an…

matvei-platov.s: Matvei Platov was a Cossack general who served as ataman of the Don Cossack Host from 1801 until his death. He fought in Russia's wars against the Ottoman Empire, and in 1812 his Cossacks harried Napoleon's army during its retreat from Moscow, after which he campaigned in…

mal-of-the-drevlians.s: Mal was a prince of the Drevlians, an East Slavic tribe, named in the Primary Chronicle under the year 945. After his people killed Prince Igor of Kiev, he sent envoys to propose marriage to Igor's widow Olga, who had them buried alive and burned and then destroyed the…

melfi.s: Melfi is a town in Basilicata, southern Italy, on a hill near Monte Vulture. Around 1042 the Normans of Apulia made it their first capital, and in 1059 Pope Nicholas II held a synod there at which he invested Robert Guiscard as duke of Apulia and Calabria.

meppen.s: Meppen is a town in Emsland, Lower Saxony, Germany, where the Hase joins the Ems. It belonged to the Prince-Bishopric of Münster until 1803, when it passed to the Duke of Arenberg, and in 1815 it came under the Kingdom of Hanover, with the dukes keeping rights as mediatised…

moulins.s: Moulins is a town on the Allier river in central France, capital of the Allier department. It was the seat of the dukes of Bourbon from the 14th century, and their court made it a centre of the arts; its cathedral holds the triptych of the Master of Moulins, painted around 1500.

moravian-gate.s: The Moravian Gate is a lowland corridor in the eastern Czech Republic between the Carpathians and the Sudetes, linking the valley of the Oder with that of the Bečva, a tributary of the Morava. It has been a natural route between the Baltic and the Danube basin since…

matteo-maria-boiardo.s: Matteo Maria Boiardo was an Italian poet and courtier at Ferrara under Duke Ercole I d'Este. His unfinished chivalric epic Orlando Innamorato, published from the 1480s, combined the Carolingian legends with Arthurian romance and inspired Ariosto's Orlando Furioso.

magdeburg-borde.s: The Magdeburg Börde is a fertile lowland in Saxony-Anhalt, Germany, stretching west of Magdeburg and the Elbe. Its deep black loess soils are among the best farmland in Germany.

masovia.s: Masovia is a historical region of east-central Poland on the middle Vistula, centred first on Płock and later on Warsaw. From 1138 it was a separate Piast duchy, often divided among branches of the dynasty, until it was incorporated into the Kingdom of Poland in 1526.

maria-beatrice-d-este-duchess-of-massa.n: Maria Beatrice d'Este, Duchess of Massa
maria-beatrice-d-este-duchess-of-massa.s: Maria Beatrice d'Este (1750–1829) was heiress of the Duchy of Massa and Carrara through her mother, Maria Teresa Cybo-Malaspina, and of the Este dukes of Modena through her father. In 1771 she married Archduke Ferdinand Karl of Austria, founding the House of Austria-Este.

michelangelo.s: Michelangelo Buonarroti (1475–1564) was a Florentine sculptor, painter, architect and poet, one of the greatest artists of the Italian Renaissance. His works include the marble David in Florence, the ceiling and Last Judgement of the Sistine Chapel in Rome, and the design of…

menumorut.s: Menumorut is a ruler described in the Gesta Hungarorum, written around 1200, as the duke of a land between the Tisza, the Someș and the Igfon forest, with its fortress at Bihar. According to the Gesta he resisted Árpád's Hungarians, but after the siege of Bihar he gave his…

mirandola.s: Mirandola is a town in the province of Modena in Emilia-Romagna, Italy, on the plain north of Modena. From the 14th century it was ruled by the Pico family as a fortified lordship, later a principality and duchy, until it was sold to the Este dukes of Modena in 1710.

mont-saint-michel.s: Mont-Saint-Michel is a tidal island off the coast of Normandy, near the border with Brittany, crowned by a Benedictine abbey dedicated to the Archangel Michael. A sanctuary was founded there in 708 and a Benedictine community in 966 under the dukes of Normandy.

mieszko-ii-the-fat.s: Mieszko II the Fat (c. 1220–1246) was a Piast duke of Opole and Racibórz in Upper Silesia, a son of Casimir I of Opole.

mostar.s: Mostar is the largest city of Herzegovina, in Bosnia and Herzegovina, on the Neretva river. It grew under Ottoman rule around a bridge crossing, and its Old Bridge (Stari Most), completed in 1566, became the symbol of the city.

meiningen-ensemble.s: The Meiningen Ensemble was the theatre company of the court of Saxe-Meiningen, directed by Duke George II with Ludwig Chronegk and Ellen Franz. Between 1874 and 1890 it toured across Europe, staging plays with historically accurate sets and costumes, carefully drilled crowd…

moritzburg-zeitz.s: The Moritzburg is a palace in Zeitz, Saxony-Anhalt, built between 1657 and 1678 for Duke Maurice of Saxe-Zeitz on the site of the old castle of the bishops of Naumburg. It served as the residence of the dukes of Saxe-Zeitz until the line ended in 1718, and its palace church…

maribor.s: Maribor is the second largest city of Slovenia, on the Drava river in Lower Styria. A medieval market town of the Duchy of Styria with a largely German-speaking population, it was secured for the Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes in 1918–1919 by Rudolf Maister's forces.

minnesang.s: Minnesang was the tradition of courtly love poetry and song in medieval Germany, flourishing from the twelfth to the fourteenth century. Its poets, the Minnesänger, were often knights or courtiers who sang of devotion to an idealised noble lady.

marienberg-fortress.s: The Marienberg Fortress stands on a hill above the Main opposite the old town of Würzburg in Bavaria. The Marienkirche on the summit dates from the early eighth century, and from the thirteenth century to 1719 the fortress was the residence of the prince-bishops of Würzburg.

mihailo-i-of-duklja.s: Mihailo I was ruler of Duklja from about 1050 to 1081, son of Stefan Vojislav. He extended his authority over Raška, Travunia and Zachlumia and supported the Bulgarian uprising of 1072.

mount-batten.s: Mount Batten is a small peninsula on the eastern side of Plymouth Sound in Devon, England. Excavations have shown it was a trading port in the late Bronze Age and Iron Age, linking south-west Britain with Brittany and the Atlantic coasts of Europe through the exchange of…

maiden-castle-dorset.s: Maiden Castle is an Iron Age hillfort south-west of Dorchester in Dorset and one of the largest in Europe. It began as a Neolithic enclosure, and in the 1st millennium BCE it was enlarged with several lines of massive ramparts and complex gateways.

mauritsstad.s: Mauritsstad was the planned town built by Johan Maurits of Nassau-Siegen on the island of Antônio Vaz beside Recife, the capital of Dutch Brazil, from the late 1630s. It included his palaces of Vrijburg and Boa Vista, gardens, canals and a bridge linking it to Recife.

malays.s: The Malays are an Austronesian people of the Malay Peninsula, eastern Sumatra, the coasts of Borneo and southern Thailand. Most are Muslims, and Malay culture took shape in sultanates such as Malacca and Johor, whose language became a lingua franca of maritime South-East Asia.

mauritius.s: Mauritius is an island nation in the Indian Ocean, about 2,000 kilometres off the south-east coast of Africa. Uninhabited until the Dutch settled it in 1638, it was ruled by France as Isle de France from 1715 and by Britain from 1810, when sugar plantations worked first by…

marduk-zakir-shumi-i.s: Marduk-zakir-shumi I was king of Babylon from about 855 to 819 BCE. When his brother Marduk-bel-usate revolted, he called on Shalmaneser III of Assyria, who defeated the rebel in 850 BCE; the two kings are shown clasping hands on a throne base from Nimrud.

maurice-fitzgerald-lord-of-lanstephan.s: Maurice FitzGerald was a Cambro-Norman lord, son of Gerald of Windsor and the Welsh princess Nest, who came to Ireland in 1169 as one of the first leaders of the Anglo-Norman invasion. He served Strongbow and Henry II and received lands in Leinster.

magnus-erlendsson.s: Magnus Erlendsson was an Earl of Orkney who shared rule of the islands with his cousin Håkon Paulsson. Their rivalry ended when Håkon had him killed on the island of Egilsay around 1117.

muziris.s: Muziris was an ancient port on the Malabar Coast of south-western India, probably near modern Pattanam in Kerala. In the early centuries CE it was the main harbour of the Chera kingdom and a centre of the pepper trade with Roman Egypt, described in the Periplus of the…

memphis-egypt.s: Memphis was the capital of ancient Egypt for much of its history, founded around 3100 BCE where the Nile valley meets the Delta, south of modern Cairo. Its chief god was Ptah, and its cemeteries, including Saqqara and Giza, hold the pyramids of the Old Kingdom.

mukhalingam.s: Mukhalingam is a village in Srikakulam district of Andhra Pradesh, India, identified with Kalinganagara, the early capital of the Eastern Ganga dynasty. Its temples to Shiva, notably the Madhukeswara temple, are among the finest early examples of the Kalinga style of…

montevideo.s: Montevideo is the capital and largest city of Uruguay, on the northern shore of the Río de la Plata. Founded by the Spanish in the 1720s as a fortress against Portuguese expansion, it became the main naval base of the Viceroyalty of the Río de la Plata.

marcus-aurelius-cotta.s: Marcus Aurelius Cotta was a Roman politician, consul in 74 BCE with Lucius Licinius Lucullus. In the Third Mithridatic War he was defeated by Mithridates VI at Chalcedon, but later besieged Heraclea Pontica and took and sacked it in 70 BCE.

mijares.s: The Mijares (Millars in Valencian) is a river of eastern Spain, rising in the Sierra de Gúdar in the province of Teruel and flowing south-east through the province of Castellón to the Mediterranean between Vila-real and Almassora. In antiquity it is taken to have marked the…

momine-khatun-mausoleum.s: The Momine Khatun Mausoleum is a ten-sided brick tomb tower in Nakhchivan, completed in 1186 by the architect Ajami Nakhchivani for Momine Khatun, wife of the atabeg Eldiguz, on the orders of her son Jahan Pahlavan. Covered in carved geometric ornament, turquoise glaze and…

mount-ida-crete.s: Mount Ida, also called Psiloritis, is the highest mountain of Crete, rising to 2,456 metres in the centre of the island. In Greek myth Zeus was raised in a cave on its slopes, and the Idaean Cave was a major sanctuary from the Minoan period into Roman times.

montlaures.s: Montlaurès is an oppidum, a fortified hilltop settlement, just north of Narbonne in southern France, occupied from about the 6th century BCE. It is usually identified with Naro, the main centre of the Elisyces, an Iberian-influenced people of the coast.

mirador-basin.s: The Mirador Basin is a lowland area of tropical forest in northern Petén, Guatemala, bordering Mexico. It contains a dense cluster of Preclassic Maya cities, including El Mirador, Nakbe and El Tintal, linked by raised causeways, which flourished between about 1000 BCE and 150 CE.

ma-al-aynayn.s: Ma al-Aynayn was a Sufi scholar and political leader of the western Sahara, born in southern Mauritania. From Smara, the town he founded in 1898 with Moroccan support, he called for resistance to French expansion in Mauritania and the Sahara, and his followers opposed the…

mufarraj-ibn-sallam.s: Mufarraj ibn Sallam was the second ruler of the Emirate of Bari in southern Italy, in power in the 850s. He extended Muslim conquests in Apulia, built a congregational mosque in Bari, and sought formal recognition as emir from the Abbasid caliph.

mem-and-zin.s: Mem and Zin is an epic poem in Kurmanji Kurdish written by Ahmad Khani and completed in 1692. Based on a folk tale, it tells of the tragic love of Mem and Zin, a sister of the emir of Bohtan at Cizre, whose union is thwarted by the intrigues of the courtier Bakr.

mutahharten.s: Mutahharten was the ruler of Erzincan in eastern Anatolia in the late 14th and early 15th centuries, after serving as a governor under the Eretnids. He ruled a mixed population of Turks, Armenians and Greeks and survived between the Ottomans, the Turkmen confederations and…

muhammad-i-of-granada.s: Muhammad I of Granada, known as Ibn al-Ahmar, was the founder of the Nasrid dynasty and the Emirate of Granada. A minor noble from Arjona, he proclaimed himself ruler in 1232 amid the collapse of Almohad power and made Granada his capital in 1238.

muhammad-xii-of-granada.s: Muhammad XII, known to the Spanish as Boabdil, was the last Nasrid emir of Granada. He rebelled against his father Abu al-Hasan, was captured by the Castilians at Lucena in 1483 and released as their vassal, and the family's divisions helped Isabella I and Ferdinand II conquer…

masmak-fort.s: Masmak Fort is a clay and mud-brick fortress in the old centre of Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, built in the second half of the 19th century. In January 1902 the young Abd al-Aziz ibn Saud and a small band of followers captured it from the Rashidi governor, a raid that began the…

maan-jordan.s: Ma'an is a city in southern Jordan on the old caravan and pilgrimage route between Syria and the Hejaz, later served by the Hejaz Railway. In November 1920 Abdullah, son of Sharif Husayn of Mecca, arrived there with his followers, the first step towards founding the Emirate of…

muhammad-al-habib-of-trarza.s: Muhammad al-Habib was emir of Trarza in south-western Mauritania from 1827 until 1860. He sought to extend his influence south of the Senegal River, notably by marrying the ruler of Waalo, which alarmed the French at Saint-Louis.

mutsu-province.s: Mutsu Province was an old province of Japan covering most of northern Honshu, the largest in the country. Long a frontier land of the Emishi, it was the setting for the 11th-century wars of the Abe and Kiyohara and for the rule of the Northern Fujiwara from Hiraizumi.

mull-of-kintyre.s: The Mull of Kintyre is the south-western tip of the Kintyre peninsula in Argyll, western Scotland. It lies only about 20 kilometres from the coast of Northern Ireland, across the North Channel, and has long been a crossing point between Scotland and Ireland.

maranhao.s: Maranhão is a state in north-eastern Brazil, on the Atlantic coast between the Amazon and the north-east. Its capital, São Luís, was founded by the French in 1612 and taken by the Portuguese in 1615, and the Dutch occupied it from 1641 to 1644.

menedemus-of-eretria.s: Menedemus of Eretria was a Greek philosopher who founded the Eretrian school, which continued the teaching of Phaedo of Elis and focused on ethics and logic. A citizen of Eretria, he also played a leading part in its politics and served on embassies to the Macedonian kings.

mazaruni.s: The Mazaruni is a river in Guyana, about 560 kilometres long, which rises in the Pakaraima Mountains and joins the Essequibo near Bartica, close to its meeting with the Cuyuni. The early Dutch post of Kyk-over-al stood near the confluence.

mount-aragats.s: Mount Aragats is the highest mountain in Armenia, an extinct volcano rising to 4,090 metres north-west of Yerevan. Its slopes have been settled since prehistoric times and carry the medieval fortress of Amberd and the Byurakan Astrophysical Observatory.

muscogee.s: The Muscogee, or Creek, are a Native American people of the south-eastern United States, whose towns in present-day Alabama and Georgia formed a powerful confederacy in the 18th century. They traded and fought with English, Spanish and French colonists.

monothelitism.s: Monothelitism was the Christian doctrine that Christ had two natures but only one will. Promoted by the emperor Heraclius in his Ecthesis of 638 as a compromise to reconcile opponents of the Council of Chalcedon, it was rejected by the popes and by Maximus the Confessor and…

mushika-dynasty.s: The Mushika dynasty ruled northern Kerala, in the region around Ezhimala and Kannur north of the Chera kingdom, in the early medieval period. Its history is known from inscriptions and from the Mushikavamsa, an 11th-century Sanskrit poem on its kings.

mushikavamsa.s: The Mushikavamsa is a Sanskrit poem composed in the 11th century by the court poet Atula in northern Kerala. It recounts the legendary origins of the Mushika dynasty and lists its kings down to the poet's patron.

monte-cimino.s: Monte Cimino is the highest peak, at about 1,050 metres, of the Monti Cimini, a range of extinct volcanoes near Viterbo in northern Lazio, Italy. In antiquity the range was covered by the dense Ciminian Forest, which the historian Livy described as a feared barrier between…

mankessim.s: Mankessim is a town in the Central Region of Ghana, regarded in tradition as the place where the Fante people settled after migrating to the coast and the seat of their early rulers. Its sacred grove, Nananom Mpow, was an important shrine.

mankessim-constitution.s: The Mankessim Constitution was the written constitution adopted by the Fante Confederacy at Mankessim in the Gold Coast in 1871. It provided for a king-president, an executive council, a representative assembly of kings and chiefs, a poll tax, and programmes for roads,…

misiones-province.s: Misiones is a province of north-eastern Argentina, a narrow territory between Paraguay and Brazil whose name recalls the Jesuit missions founded among the Guaraní in the 17th century, such as San Ignacio Miní. After the Jesuits were expelled in 1767 the region was disputed,…

martin-delgado.s: Martín Delgado was a Filipino general from Iloilo who led the revolution against Spain on Panay in 1898. His forces besieged Iloilo City until the Spanish garrison surrendered on 25 December 1898, and he led revolutionary forces on Panay against the Americans in the…

madinat-ash-shab.s: Madinat ash-Sha'b is a town on the western side of Aden in Yemen, built from 1959 as Al Ittihad, the purpose-built capital of the British-sponsored Federation of Arab Emirates of the South and its successor, the Federation of South Arabia. It housed the federal council and…

malaysian-chinese-association.s: The Malaysian Chinese Association, founded in 1949 as the Malayan Chinese Association under Tan Cheng Lock, is a political party representing ethnic Chinese in Malaysia. It began partly as a welfare body for Chinese moved into new villages during the Malayan Emergency.

malayan-communist-party.s: The Malayan Communist Party was a communist party founded in 1930, drawing its support mainly from the Chinese of Malaya. It led the main resistance to the Japanese occupation and, under Chin Peng, launched an armed revolt in 1948 that the British fought as the Malayan…

malaysian-indian-congress.s: The Malaysian Indian Congress, founded in 1946 as the Malayan Indian Congress, is a political party representing the Indian community of Malaysia, many of them descended from plantation labourers brought in under British rule. It joined the Alliance of the United Malays…

monckton-commission.s: The Monckton Commission was a British advisory commission chaired by Lord Monckton that reviewed the future of the Federation of Rhodesia and Nyasaland in 1960. Its report found deep African hostility to the federation and recommended wider African political representation and…

mamercus-aemilius-mamercinus.s: Mamercus Aemilius Mamercinus was a Roman statesman who was appointed dictator three times, in 437, 434 and 426 BCE. According to Livy, as dictator in 434 BCE he limited the term of the censors to eighteen months, and in 426 BCE he defeated Veii and Fidenae and captured and…

moscow-peace-treaty.s: The Moscow Peace Treaty, signed on 12 March 1940, ended the Winter War between Finland and the Soviet Union. Finland kept its independence but ceded about a tenth of its territory, including the Karelian Isthmus with the city of Viipuri, lands north of Lake Ladoga and part of…

muhammad-amin-bughra.s: Muhammad Amin Bughra was a Uyghur nationalist leader from Khotan in Xinjiang. In 1933 he led a revolt in southern Xinjiang and helped found the short-lived Turkish Islamic Republic of East Turkestan at Kashgar, which was crushed in 1934.

marchand-dessalines.s: Marchand-Dessalines is a town in the Artibonite valley of Haiti that Jean-Jacques Dessalines made the capital of his empire after independence in 1804. He surrounded it with a ring of forts on the hills, such as Fort Fin-du-Monde, as a refuge against any French attempt at…

miguel-malvar.s: Miguel Malvar was a Filipino general from Batangas who fought in the Philippine Revolution against Spain and in the Philippine–American War. After the capture of Emilio Aguinaldo in 1901 he led the continuing resistance as commander of the revolutionary forces, conducting…

mingyi-nyo.s: Mingyi Nyo was the founder of the Toungoo dynasty of Burma, ruler of the small principality of Toungoo on the Sittaung river from 1485. As the kingdom of Ava weakened, he declared independence in 1510 and built Toungoo into a refuge for Burmans fleeing Shan raids in the north.

murong-hui.s: Murong Hui was chief of the Murong Xianbei in western Liaoning from 285 to 333. He settled his people in the Liao valley, encouraged farming and sericulture, and adopted Chinese law and administration, welcoming Chinese refugees from the collapse of the Western Jin.

manetho.s: Manetho was an Egyptian priest of Sebennytos in the Nile Delta who wrote a history of Egypt in Greek, the Aegyptiaca, under the early Ptolemies in the 3rd century BCE. His division of Egyptian kings into thirty dynasties is still the basis of Egyptian chronology.

menton.s: Menton is a town on the French Riviera close to the Italian border, known for its lemons and mild climate. Held by the Grimaldi princes of Monaco from the 14th century, it rebelled in 1848, declared itself a free city with Roquebrune and passed to France in 1861 after a…

martin-schongauer.s: Martin Schongauer was an Alsatian painter and engraver of Colmar, the most important printmaker north of the Alps before Albrecht Dürer. His copper engravings circulated widely across Europe, and his painting the Madonna of the Rose Bower of 1473 survives in Colmar's Dominican…

marienkirche-gelnhausen.s: The Marienkirche in Gelnhausen, Hesse, is a late Romanesque and early Gothic church built mainly in the 12th and 13th centuries. Its unusual group of towers at the east end, its carved rood screen and its rich decoration make it one of the outstanding buildings of the…

marienkirche-reutlingen.s: The Marienkirche in Reutlingen is a Gothic church built between about 1247 and 1343, the city's main church and a symbol of its time as a free imperial city. It was badly damaged in the great town fire of 1726 and restored in the 19th century.

margarete-steiff.s: Margarete Steiff was a German seamstress from Giengen an der Brenz who founded the toy company that bears her name. Partly paralysed by polio from childhood, she began making felt animals in 1880.

moder.s: The Moder is a river in northern Alsace, France, that rises in the northern Vosges and flows south-east through Haguenau to join the Rhine. The Hohenstaufen castle at Haguenau stood on an island in the river.

muhlhausen.s: Mühlhausen is a town on the Unstrut in north-western Thuringia, Germany, which grew around a royal palace and was an imperial city from the late 12th century until 1802. It was a member of the Hanseatic League.

muhlhausen-reichsrechtsbuch.s: The Mühlhausen Reichsrechtsbuch is a law book of the imperial city of Mühlhausen in Thuringia, written down around 1200 to 1230. It records the customary law applied in the town's court and is one of the oldest legal texts written in German prose.

martin-behaim.s: Martin Behaim was a Nuremberg merchant and cosmographer who spent much of his life in Portugal and the Azores. In 1490–1492, back in Nuremberg, he had the Erdapfel made, the oldest surviving terrestrial globe, which shows the world just before Columbus reached America.

matthaus-alber.s: Matthäus Alber was a Lutheran reformer known as the Luther of Swabia. As preacher in Reutlingen from 1521 he led the city into the Reformation, and in 1530 Reutlingen was one of the two cities, with Nuremberg, to sign the Augsburg Confession.

martin-bucer.s: Martin Bucer was a Dominican friar from Sélestat who became the leading reformer of Strasbourg from 1523. He sought agreement between the Lutheran and Swiss reformers, notably in the Wittenberg Concord of 1536, and influenced John Calvin, who worked with him in Strasbourg.

makatea.s: Makatea is a raised coral island in the Tuamotu archipelago of French Polynesia. From 1908 to 1966 a French company mined its rich phosphate deposits, which were for decades among the territory's leading exports and drew labourers from across Polynesia and from Asia.

maximilien-robespierre.s: Maximilien Robespierre was a French lawyer and leading Jacobin of the French Revolution. Elected to the Estates-General in 1789 and to the National Convention in 1792, he joined the Committee of Public Safety in July 1793 and became the most prominent figure of the Terror,…

matanzas-inlet.s: Matanzas Inlet is a channel linking the Matanzas River to the Atlantic Ocean, about 23 km south of St Augustine, Florida. In September and October 1565 Pedro Menéndez de Avilés had Jean Ribault and several hundred shipwrecked French Huguenots executed there, which gave the…

mahe-india.s: Mahé, also called Mayyazhi, is a small town at the mouth of the Mahé River on the Malabar coast of Kerala, India. The French East India Company took it in 1725, and despite several British occupations it remained a French possession until its transfer to India in 1954.

mer-egee.s: Mer-Égée ('Aegean Sea') was a French department created in 1797 from the southern Ionian Islands, formerly Venetian, after the Treaty of Campo Formio. Centred on Zakynthos and including Kythira, it was one of three departments, with Corcyre and Ithaque, into which France…

mississippi-company.s: The Mississippi Company was a French trading company founded in 1717 as the Company of the West and enlarged in 1719 into the Company of the Indies under the financier John Law. It held a monopoly of trade with Louisiana, recruited settlers and enslaved Africans for the…

moktar-ould-daddah.s: Moktar Ould Daddah was the first president of Mauritania, from independence on 28 November 1960 until 1978. A lawyer trained in France, he became head of government in 1957, oversaw the building of Nouakchott as the new capital and later made his People's Party the sole legal…

moruroa.s: Moruroa, also spelled Mururoa, is an atoll in the Tuamotu archipelago of French Polynesia. France conducted most of its nuclear weapons tests there between 1966 and 1996, in the atmosphere until 1974 and then underground, together with nearby Fangataufa.

menalamba-rebellion.s: The Menalamba rebellion was a rising in highland Madagascar against French rule and the collaborating Merina government, which broke out in late 1895 after the French conquest of Antananarivo. The rebels, named after the red-stained shawls they wore, attacked missionaries,…

muhammad-iii-as-sadiq.s: Muhammad III as-Sadiq was bey of Tunis of the Husainid dynasty from 1859 to 1882. In 1861 he promulgated a constitution, the first in the Arab world, but it was suspended in 1864 after a revolt against higher taxes.

moca-dominican-republic.s: Moca is a city in the Cibao valley of the northern Dominican Republic, capital of Espaillat Province. In 1805 Haitian forces retreating from their siege of Santo Domingo under Jean-Jacques Dessalines and Henri Christophe sacked the town and killed many of its inhabitants.

mouride-brotherhood.s: The Mouride brotherhood is a Sufi order founded in Senegal in 1883 by Amadou Bamba, with its holy city at Touba. Its disciples owe obedience and labour to their marabouts, and from the late 19th century they spread groundnut cultivation across the Senegalese interior, becoming…

modibo-keita.s: Modibo Keïta was the first president of Mali, from independence in 1960 until 1968. A teacher educated at the École William Ponty, he led the Sudanese Union–African Democratic Rally, sat in the French National Assembly and briefly headed the Mali Federation with Senegal.

mogho-naba.s: The Mogho Naba ('ruler of the world') is the title of the king of the Mossi kingdom of Ouagadougou in present-day Burkina Faso, the senior of the Mossi states. The office goes back several centuries, and its holder presides over a court of dignitaries and traditional ceremonies.

molise.s: Molise is a region of southern Italy, between Abruzzo, Lazio, Campania and Apulia, with its capital at Campobasso. In antiquity its mountains were the heart of the Samnites, while the Frentani held its coastal hills.

malorix.s: Malorix was a leader of the Frisii in the mid-1st century CE, named by Tacitus with Verritus as ruling the people 'as far as Germans are ruled'. In 58 CE, after the Frisii settled lands near the Rhine reserved for Roman troops, the two went to Rome to plead their case before…

mpongwe.s: The Mpongwe are a Myene-speaking people of the Gabon estuary in western Gabon. From the 18th century their clan chiefs acted as middlemen between European traders and the peoples of the interior, dealing in ivory, timber, rubber and slaves.

masuria.s: Masuria is a lake district in north-eastern Poland, part of the former East Prussia. Its many glacial lakes include Śniardwy and Mamry.

marius-emperor.s: Marius was a Roman usurper who ruled the breakaway Gallic Empire briefly in 269, after the murder of Postumus by his troops. According to later Roman sources he had been a blacksmith before rising in the army.

mandla.s: Mandla is a town on the Narmada river in Madhya Pradesh, India, and the headquarters of Mandla district. It was the later capital of the Gond kingdom of Garha-Mandla, which survived there as a Mughal and then Maratha vassal until the Marathas annexed it in 1781.

murshidabad.s: Murshidabad is a city on the Bhagirathi river in West Bengal, India. Named after Murshid Quli Khan, who moved the provincial revenue office there in the early 18th century, it was the capital of the Nawabs of Bengal for most of that century.

mzila.s: Mzila was king of the Gaza kingdom in southern Mozambique from about 1861 to 1884. A son of the founder Soshangane, he won the long succession war against his brother Mawewe with Portuguese help after their father's death in 1858.

madang.s: Madang is a port town on the north coast of Papua New Guinea. Founded by the Germans as Friedrich-Wilhelmshafen, it was the seat of the German New Guinea Company's administration in the 1890s.

murad-ii.s: Murad II was sultan of the Ottoman Empire from 1421 to 1451, with a brief abdication in 1444 to 1446. He restored Ottoman power after the civil war that followed Timur's victory, inherited the Germiyanid lands in 1429, took Thessalonica from Venice in 1430, and defeated…

merneptah-stele.s: The Merneptah Stele is an inscribed granite slab of the Egyptian pharaoh Merneptah, set up around 1208 BCE and found at Thebes in 1896. It records his victory over the Libyans and their allies and closes with a hymn listing defeated places in Canaan, including Ashkelon, Gezer…

minaret-of-jam.s: The Minaret of Jam is a brick minaret about 65 metres high in a remote valley of Ghor province, Afghanistan, beside the Hari Rud. Built by the Ghurid sultan Ghiyath al-Din Muhammad, probably in the 1190s, it is covered with geometric brickwork and the Qur'anic chapter of Maryam.

maltese-language.s: Maltese is the national language of Malta and an official language of the European Union. It descends from the Siculo-Arabic spoken in Sicily and Malta under Arab rule from the 9th century, and is the only Semitic language written in the Latin script.

machilipatnam.s: Machilipatnam, historically Masulipatnam, is a port town on the Krishna delta in Andhra Pradesh, India. Under the Golconda Sultanate it was the main outlet for Coromandel textiles, and the Dutch (1605), English (1611) and French set up factories there.

magar-people.s: The Magars are one of the largest indigenous peoples of Nepal, living mainly in the western and central hills. Speakers of Tibeto-Burman Magar languages, they formed a large part of the army with which the Gorkha kingdom unified Nepal in the eighteenth century and have long…

milan-nedic.s: Milan Nedić was a Serbian general and politician who headed the German-installed Government of National Salvation in occupied Serbia from 1941 to 1944. A former chief of the Yugoslav general staff and war minister, he collaborated with the occupiers while claiming to shield…

mendoza-argentina.s: Mendoza is a city in western Argentina at the foot of the Andes, the capital of Mendoza Province. Founded from Chile in 1561, it belonged to the Captaincy General of Chile until 1776.

mathildenhohe.s: The Mathildenhöhe is a hill in Darmstadt, Germany, where Grand Duke Ernest Louis of Hesse established the Darmstadt Artists' Colony in 1899. Its artists' houses, exhibition building, Russian Orthodox chapel and Wedding Tower, built largely by Joseph Maria Olbrich, form an…

mindaugas.s: Mindaugas was the first known Grand Duke of Lithuania and its only crowned king. Having united the Lithuanian lands by the 1240s, he accepted Catholic baptism in 1251 to divide his enemies and, with Pope Innocent IV's approval, was crowned king in 1253.

moscow-kremlin.s: The Moscow Kremlin is the fortified complex at the heart of Moscow, on a hill above the Moskva river. From the fourteenth century it was the seat of the grand princes of Moscow and later of the tsars, and under Ivan III Italian architects rebuilt its brick walls, towers and…

mordvins.s: The Mordvins are a Finno-Ugric people of the middle Volga region of Russia, divided into two main groups, the Erzya and the Moksha, each with its own language. Their forest lands bordered the Rus' principalities of Ryazan and Vladimir-Suzdal and Volga Bulgaria, and they came…

mikhail-borisovich-of-tver.s: Mikhail Borisovich was the last Grand Prince of Tver, from 1461 to 1485. The son of Boris Alexandrovich, he at first allied with Moscow, joining Ivan III against Novgorod, but when he sought the support of Casimir IV of Poland-Lithuania, Ivan besieged Tver in 1485.

mikulcice.s: Mikulčice is a village in South Moravia, Czech Republic, near which lies one of the largest fortified centres of Great Moravia, possibly its capital. Excavations since 1954 have uncovered an acropolis with a palace, at least twelve churches and some 2,500 graves, many rich in…

minnesota.s: Minnesota is a state in the upper Midwest of the United States, bordering Canada and Lake Superior, with its capital at Saint Paul. It holds the headwaters of the Mississippi and was the homeland of the Dakota and later also of the Ojibwe.

mongoose-gang.s: The Mongoose Gang was a private militia used by Eric Gairy, Grenada's chief minister and then prime minister, to intimidate and attack his opponents in the 1970s. Its members beat protesters and opposition figures, including New Jewel Movement leaders such as Maurice Bishop.

maurice-bishop-international-airport.s: Maurice Bishop International Airport, formerly Point Salines International Airport, is the main airport of Grenada, at the south-western tip of the island. Its construction under Maurice Bishop's government with Cuban workers was seen by the United States as a possible…

mesolcina.s: The Mesolcina, or Misox in German, is an Italian-speaking valley in the south of Graubünden, Switzerland, running from the San Bernardino Pass towards Bellinzona. Long held by the counts of Sax-Misox, it joined the Grey League in the late 15th century and so became part of the…

mogao-caves.s: The Mogao Caves are a complex of nearly 500 Buddhist cave temples cut into a cliff south-east of Dunhuang in Gansu, China, from the 4th to the 14th century. They hold some of the finest Buddhist murals and sculptures in Asia.

muzaffar-shah-i.s: Muzaffar Shah I, born Zafar Khan, was the founder of the Gujarat Sultanate. Appointed governor of Gujarat by the Tughluq sultan of Delhi in 1391, he declared independence after Timur's sack of Delhi had left the sultanate powerless, taking the title of sultan around 1407.

manaku.s: Manaku was an Indian painter of the Pahari school from Guler in the Himalayan foothills, the elder son of the painter Pandit Seu. Working in the mid-18th century, he is known for large series of illustrations of the Gita Govinda and the Ramayana, painted in a vivid, expressive…

madho-rao-scindia.s: Madho Rao Scindia was Maharaja of Gwalior from 1886 to 1925, succeeding his father Jayajirao Scindia. He modernised the state's administration and promoted railways, industry, schools and irrigation, including the narrow-gauge Gwalior Light Railway.

mansura-sindh.s: Mansura was the capital of the Arab province of Sindh, founded in the 730s by the Umayyad governor Amr ibn Muhammad near the Indus, north-east of modern Hyderabad in Pakistan. From the 850s it was the seat of the Habbari dynasty, and Arab geographers described it as a…

muhammad-i-al-mustansir.s: Muhammad I al-Mustansir was the Hafsid ruler of Ifriqiya from 1249 to 1277 and the first of the dynasty to take the title of caliph, in 1253. His prestige grew after the fall of the Almohads and of Baghdad to the Mongols, and in 1270 he withstood the Eighth Crusade of Louis IX…

murad-i.s: Murad I was the Ottoman sultan from 1362 to 1389 who made the Ottoman state a major power in the Balkans and Anatolia. He took Adrianople, which became the capital as Edirne, defeated the Serbs on the Maritsa in 1371 and expanded in Anatolia by marriage alliances and purchase,…

maitreya.s: Maitreya is the future Buddha of Buddhist tradition, a bodhisattva who will appear on earth to teach the dharma anew when the teaching of Gautama Buddha has been forgotten. He is venerated across Buddhist Asia.

man-dynasty.s: The Ma'n dynasty were Druze chiefs of the Chouf in Mount Lebanon who rose under Ottoman rule in the 16th century. Their most famous member, Fakhr al-Din II, built a large autonomous domain over much of Lebanon and northern Palestine before the Ottomans executed him in 1635.

mahendrapala-i.s: Mahendrapala I was a king of the Gurjara-Pratihara dynasty who ruled from Kannauj from about 885 to 910, succeeding his father Mihira Bhoja. His empire reached its greatest extent, stretching from the Himalaya to the Narmada and from Saurashtra to Bengal, where he took…

maitraka-dynasty.s: The Maitraka dynasty ruled western India from about 475 to 776 from their capital at Valabhi in Saurashtra, now Vala in Gujarat. Founded by Bhatarka, a general of the Gupta Empire, they became independent as Gupta power faded.

mon-people.s: The Mon are a people of Lower Myanmar and central and western Thailand who speak a Mon-Khmer (Austroasiatic) language. They were among the earliest Theravada Buddhist peoples of mainland South-East Asia, associated with the Dvaravati culture and with kingdoms such as Thaton,…

maccabees.s: The Maccabees were the priestly family of Mattathias and his five sons, among them Judas Maccabeus, Jonathan and Simon, who led the Jewish revolt against the Seleucid Empire from 167 BCE. The name comes from Judas's epithet 'Maccabeus' and is often applied to the whole family.

mattathias.s: Mattathias was a Jewish priest of Modein who, according to the First Book of Maccabees, began the revolt against the Seleucid king Antiochus IV in 167 BCE by killing a Jew who sacrificed to the Greek gods and the king's officer who ordered it. He fled to the hills with his…

musa-dagh.s: Musa Dagh is a mountain on the Mediterranean coast of Hatay province, Turkey, south-west of Antakya. In 1915 the Armenians of its villages resisted Ottoman deportation on its slopes for some seven weeks until French warships evacuated about 4,000 of them, an episode retold in…

mac-thien-tu.s: Mạc Thiên Tứ was the second ruler of the Hà Tiên principality on the Gulf of Thailand, succeeding his father Mạc Cửu in 1735 as a vassal of the Nguyễn lords. A patron of letters, he gathered Chinese and Vietnamese poets in a literary society and intervened in Cambodian…

muhammad-bey-abu-al-dhahab.s: Muhammad Bey Abu al-Dhahab was a Mamluk commander in Ottoman Egypt and the protégé of Ali Bey al-Kabir. He crushed the Hawwara of Upper Egypt in 1769 and conquered Damascus for Ali Bey in 1771, but then turned against his master, who was defeated and died in 1773.

mkwawa.s: Mkwawa was chief of the Hehe in the southern highlands of present-day Tanzania from about 1880 to 1898. He made the Hehe the dominant power of the region and destroyed a German column at Lugalo in 1891.

munyigumba.s: Munyigumba was a chief of the Hehe who in the mid-19th century united many small chiefdoms of the southern highlands of present-day Tanzania by conquest and alliance, adapting the military methods of the invading Ngoni. He died in 1879, and his son Mkwawa emerged from the…

metapolitefsi.s: The Metapolitefsi was the transition from military dictatorship to democracy in Greece after the fall of the colonels' junta in July 1974. Konstantinos Karamanlis returned from exile to lead a government of national unity, free elections were held in November 1974, a…

mariandynians.s: The Mariandynians were an Anatolian people of the Black Sea coast between Bithynia and Paphlagonia, around Heraclea Pontica. After Greek colonists from Megara founded Heraclea in the 6th century BCE, many of them were reduced to a dependent rural population working the land,…

memnon-of-heraclea.s: Memnon of Heraclea was a Greek historian, probably of the 1st or 2nd century CE, who wrote a history of his city, Heraclea Pontica. Its books 9 to 16 survive in a summary by the Byzantine patriarch Photius, covering events from the tyranny of Clearchus to the time of Julius…

maharero.s: Maharero, also called Kamaherero, was a Herero leader in central Namibia who freed the Herero from the domination of the Oorlam Afrikaners in a war that began in 1863. Based at Okahandja, he became the most powerful Herero chief, and in 1885 he signed a protection treaty with…

mariamne-i.s: Mariamne I was a Hasmonean princess, granddaughter of both Aristobulus II and Hyrcanus II, and the second wife of Herod the Great, whose claim to rule she strengthened. Suspicious of her and her family, Herod had her executed in 29 BCE, and later also had their sons Alexander…

masada.s: Masada is a rock fortress on a plateau above the Dead Sea in southern Israel, fortified by the Hasmoneans and rebuilt by Herod the Great with palaces and storehouses. In the First Jewish–Roman War it was the last rebel stronghold; according to Josephus its defenders killed…

monterado.s: Monterado is a town in Bengkayang Regency, West Kalimantan, Indonesia, inland from Singkawang. In the 18th and 19th centuries it was a centre of Chinese gold mining in western Borneo and the seat of the Heshun federation of mining kongsis, dominated by the Dagang kongsi, until…

mersin.s: Mersin is a port city on the Mediterranean coast of southern Turkey, capital of Mersin province, which covers the western part of ancient Cilicia. The modern city grew in the 19th century as an outlet for cotton from the Çukurova plain and is now one of Turkey's largest ports.

mefitis.s: Mefitis was an Italic goddess associated with sulphurous springs and vapours, waters and fertility, worshipped especially by the Samnites, Hirpini and Lucanians. Her main sanctuary lay in the Ansanto valley in Irpinia, where poisonous gases rise from a small pool, and another…

monte-testaccio.s: Monte Testaccio is an artificial hill in Rome, about 35 m high, made almost entirely of broken amphorae discarded between the 1st and 3rd centuries CE. Most of them held olive oil imported from Baetica in southern Spain, and their stamps and painted labels are a major source…

munda-people.s: The Munda are an Adivasi people of eastern India, living mainly in Jharkhand, Odisha and West Bengal, who speak Mundari, a language of the Austroasiatic family. Traditionally rice farmers organised in villages under hereditary headmen, they resisted landlords and colonial…

mpangazitha.s: Mpangazitha was a chief of the Hlubi, a Nguni people living near the upper Mzinyathi river in what is now KwaZulu-Natal. Driven from their lands around 1818 by attacks during the upheavals known as the Mfecane, he led a section of the Hlubi onto the highveld, where they raided…

motobu-peninsula.s: The Motobu Peninsula is a hilly peninsula on the north-western coast of Okinawa Island, Japan. In the 14th and early 15th centuries it was the core of Hokuzan, the northern of the three rival kingdoms of Okinawa, ruled from Nakijin Castle.

murray-maclehose.s: Murray MacLehose was a British diplomat who served as governor of Hong Kong from 1971 to 1982, the longest tenure of any governor. He launched a large public housing programme, expanded education and social services, and in 1974 set up the Independent Commission Against…

malnad.s: Malnad is the hilly, forested and rain-soaked region of Karnataka, India, along the Western Ghats, covering parts of districts such as Shivamogga, Chikkamagaluru, Hassan and Kodagu. It is known for coffee, areca nut and spices.

mantaro-valley.s: The Mantaro Valley is a broad, fertile highland valley in the Junín region of central Peru, drained by the Mantaro River, with Huancayo as its main city. After the fall of the Wari Empire it was home to the Huanca and Xauxa peoples, who were conquered by the Incas in the 15th…

mihaly-karolyi.s: Mihály Károlyi was a Hungarian aristocrat and liberal politician who became prime minister after the Aster Revolution of October 1918 and then president of the Hungarian Democratic Republic. His government introduced universal suffrage and began land reform, but resigned in…

miklos-horthy.s: Miklós Horthy was an Austro-Hungarian admiral who led the counter-revolutionary National Army after the fall of the Hungarian Soviet Republic and was elected regent of the Kingdom of Hungary in 1920. He ruled for almost twenty-five years, allying Hungary with Nazi Germany to…

mir-muhammad-jamal-khan.s: Mir Muhammad Jamal Khan was the last ruling Mir of the princely state of Hunza, in what is now Gilgit-Baltistan, Pakistan, from 1945. In 1947 he acceded to Pakistan, and he continued to govern Hunza internally until Zulfikar Ali Bhutto's government abolished the state in 1974.

mir-safdar-ali-khan.s: Safdar Ali Khan was the Mir of Hunza, in the Karakoram, from 1886, after the death of his father Ghazan Khan. His raids on caravans and contacts with Russia and China alarmed the British, who sent a force against Hunza and Nagar in 1891.

mount-philerimos.s: Mount Philerimos is a hill on the north-west coast of Rhodes, Greece, above the site of ancient Ialysos. Its summit held the acropolis of the city, with a temple of Athena and Zeus Polieus.

metulum.s: Metulum was the main stronghold of the Iapydes, an Iron Age people of the north-western Balkans, in what is now Croatia. In 35 BCE Octavian besieged it during his Illyrian campaign and was wounded in the assault.

moroccan-army-of-liberation.s: The Moroccan Army of Liberation was an irregular force formed in 1955 to fight French and Spanish colonial rule in North Africa. After Moroccan independence in 1956 it continued operations in the Spanish-held south, attacking Ifni and Spanish Sahara in the Ifni War of 1957-1958.

muhammad-ibn-tughj-al-ikhshid.s: Muhammad ibn Tughj al-Ikhshid was a Turkic commander of Fergana origin who became governor of Egypt in 935 and founded the Ikhshidid dynasty. In 939 the Abbasid caliph granted him the old Ferghanan princely title of ikhshid.

mandonius.s: Mandonius was a chief of the Ilergetes, an Iberian people of north-eastern Spain, who led them with his brother Indibilis during the Second Punic War. The brothers first served Carthage and then joined Scipio Africanus in 209 BCE.

meskwaki.s: The Meskwaki, called the Fox by the French, are an Algonquian-speaking Indigenous people of the western Great Lakes, closely related to the Sauk. In the early 18th century they fought the Fox Wars against France and its Indigenous allies, including the Illinois, which cost…

michigamea.s: The Michigamea were an Algonquian-speaking people who belonged to the Illinois Confederation. When Marquette and Jolliet descended the Mississippi in 1673 they lived in what is now north-eastern Arkansas, and they later moved north to settle near the Kaskaskia on the middle…

mikawa-province.s: Mikawa Province was an old province of Japan in the eastern part of present-day Aichi Prefecture. It was the home of the Matsudaira family, whose heir Tokugawa Ieyasu spent part of his youth as a hostage of the Imagawa clan, then overlords of the province.

mudaito-dynasty.s: The Mudaito are an Afar clan whose dynasty ruled the Sultanate of Aussa in the lower Awash valley of north-eastern Ethiopia. Around 1734 their leader Kedafu took power in the Aussa oasis after the collapse of the old imamate.

muhammad-al-khalili.s: Muhammad bin Abdullah al-Khalili was the Ibadi Imam of Oman from 1920 until his death in 1954, ruling the interior from Nizwa. Elected after the murder of Imam Salim al-Kharusi, he accepted the Treaty of Seeb of 1920 with the Sultan of Muscat, which left the interior to the…

michel-ney.s: Michel Ney was a French soldier and one of Napoleon's marshals, created Duke of Elchingen in 1808 for his victory there in 1805 and later Prince of the Moskva for his part at Borodino. Famed for his courage in commanding the rearguard on the retreat from Moscow in 1812, he…

mathilde-abbess-of-essen.s: Mathilde was abbess of Essen from 973 until her death in 1011. A granddaughter of Emperor Otto I through his son Liudolf, she made the abbey a centre of Ottonian art and learning, commissioning works such as the Golden Madonna and the Otto-Mathilde Cross and rebuilding its…

machu-picchu.s: Machu Picchu is a 15th-century Inca site on a mountain ridge above the Urubamba valley in Peru. It was probably built as a royal estate for the emperor Pachacuti, with temples, terraces and finely fitted stone buildings, and was abandoned around the time of the Spanish conquest.

menander-i.s: Menander I was the best-known Indo-Greek king, ruling much of the Punjab and Gandhara from Sagala in the mid-2nd century BCE. His coins are found widely in north-western India, and he led campaigns into the Ganges plain.

milindapanha.s: The Milindapanha, or Questions of King Milinda, is a Buddhist text in Pali, probably compiled between the 1st century BCE and the 2nd century CE. It records a dialogue in which the monk Nagasena answers the questions of King Milinda, identified with the Indo-Greek king…

maheshwar.s: Maheshwar is a town on the north bank of the Narmada River in Madhya Pradesh, India. Ahilyabai Holkar made it the seat of the Holkar government in the later 18th century, building its fort, ghats and temples, and encouraged weavers whose Maheshwari saris remain famous.

mathura-lion-capital.s: The Mathura Lion Capital is a sandstone column capital carved with two lions, found at Mathura in northern India and now in the British Museum. Its inscriptions in Kharoshthi record donations to the Buddhist community by the chief queen of the Indo-Scythian satrap Rajuvula and…

maues.s: Maues was the first major Indo-Scythian king in India, ruling in the early 1st century BCE. He established Saka power in Gandhara and took Taxila from the Indo-Greeks, issuing coins that copied Greek types.

madyes.s: Madyes was a Scythian king named by Herodotus as the son of Protothyes. According to Herodotus he defeated the Medes under Cyaxares and the Scythians then dominated Asia for 28 years, until Cyaxares killed their leaders at a banquet.

mohammad-khatami.s: Mohammad Khatami is an Iranian Shia cleric and reformist politician who was President of Iran from 1997 to 2005. Elected in a landslide, he promoted greater press freedom, civil society and a 'dialogue among civilisations' with the West.

muhammad-zia-ul-haq.s: Muhammad Zia-ul-Haq was a Pakistani army general who overthrew Zulfikar Ali Bhutto in 1977 and ruled as military ruler and president until his death. He had Bhutto hanged in 1979, pursued the Islamisation of law and education, and made Pakistan the main base for the Afghan…

marcus-livius-drusus-tribune-91-bce.s: Marcus Livius Drusus was a Roman politician who, as tribune of the plebs in 91 BCE, proposed laws on land, juries and the corn supply, and the grant of Roman citizenship to Rome's Italian allies. The Senate annulled his laws, and he was assassinated at his house later that year.

martin-de-ursua.s: Martín de Ursúa was a Spanish Basque soldier and colonial official, governor of Yucatán. He built a road from Yucatán south into the Petén and on 13 March 1697 stormed Nojpetén, the island capital of the Itza Maya, with troops in a galley built on the lake.

menaka.s: Ménaka is a town in eastern Mali, the capital of the Ménaka region, near the border with Niger. It was a centre of the Iwellemmeden Kel Ataram Tuareg and became a French military post in the colonial period.

michael-manley.s: Michael Manley was Prime Minister of Jamaica from 1972 to 1980 and from 1989 to 1992, and leader of the People's National Party founded by his father Norman Manley. In his first term he pursued democratic socialism, raised the levy on bauxite and drew close to Cuba, amid…

moore-town.s: Moore Town is the main Windward Maroon community of Jamaica, in the Rio Grande valley of the parish of Portland, below the Blue Mountains. It succeeded Nanny Town, the stronghold of the Maroon leader Nanny, and holds her grave.

mapanji-garasakan.s: Mapanji Garasakan was a king in East Java in the mid-11th century, known from inscriptions issued between about 1042 and 1052. He ruled part of the realm of Airlangga after its division and is usually identified as a king of Janggala.

murud-janjira.s: Murud-Janjira is an island fortress off the town of Murud on the Konkan coast of Maharashtra, India. Fortified in stone in the 16th and 17th centuries, it was the stronghold of the Siddis, who ruled the state of Janjira from it.

muharram.s: Muharram is the first month of the Islamic lunar calendar and one of its four sacred months. Its tenth day, Ashura, marks the death of the Prophet's grandson Husayn ibn Ali at the Battle of Karbala in 680.

miri.s: Miri is a city in northern Sarawak, Malaysia, near the border with Brunei. It grew up around the first oil well in Sarawak, drilled by Shell in 1910, and became the centre of the Sarawak oil industry.

malayan-peoples-anti-japanese-army.s: The Malayan Peoples' Anti-Japanese Army was a guerrilla force formed in December 1941 by the Malayan Communist Party to resist the Japanese occupation of Malaya. Mostly ethnic Chinese, it fought from jungle bases and was supplied and trained by the British Force 136.

maha-singh.s: Maha Singh was chief of the Sukerchakia misl, one of the Sikh confederacies of the Punjab, from the early 1770s until his death in 1790. He expanded his territory around Gujranwala through campaigns against rival chiefs.

mehrangarh.s: Mehrangarh is a fort above the city of Jodhpur in Rajasthan, India, founded in 1459 by Rao Jodha of the Rathore dynasty as the new capital of Marwar. Built on a steep rocky hill, it is one of the largest forts in India, with massive walls and palaces of carved sandstone added…

malaspina.s: The Malaspina were a feudal family of Lunigiana in north-western Tuscany, descended from the Obertenghi. Divided into many branches, they held castles in the Apennines, lands in northern Sardinia from the 13th century and later the lordship of Massa and Carrara.

muhammad-sher-khan-babi.s: Muhammad Sher Khan Babi was the founder of the princely state of Junagadh in Kathiawar, India. An officer of Pathan descent in the Mughal administration of Gujarat, he declared himself independent at Junagadh in 1748 as Mughal power collapsed, taking the name Bahadur Khanji.

maibang.s: Maibang is a town in the Dima Hasao district of Assam, India, on the Mahur river. After the Ahoms sacked Dimapur in 1536, it became the capital of the Kachari kingdom until the 18th century.

maeda-toshinaga.s: Maeda Toshinaga was a Japanese daimyo, eldest son of Maeda Toshiie and second lord of the Kaga domain. After his father's death in 1599 he submitted to Tokugawa Ieyasu and fought on his side in the Sekigahara campaign of 1600.

maeda-clan.s: The Maeda clan was a Japanese samurai family that ruled the Kaga domain, the largest domain of the Edo period, assessed at over one million koku. Its founder Maeda Toshiie served Oda Nobunaga and Toyotomi Hideyoshi, and his son Toshinaga backed Tokugawa Ieyasu in 1600.

mount-penanggungan.s: Mount Penanggungan is a dormant volcano in East Java, Indonesia, rising to about 1,650 metres. Its shape, a central peak ringed by smaller summits, recalled the sacred Mount Meru, and from the 10th to the 16th century it became a holy mountain covered with more than a hundred…

mpu-bharada.s: Mpu Bharada was a Buddhist sage of 11th-century Java remembered in the Nagarakretagama and later Javanese tradition. According to these accounts, King Airlangga asked him to divide the kingdom between two sons around 1045, and he marked the boundary between Janggala and…

mpu-kanwa.s: Mpu Kanwa was a court poet of King Airlangga of Kahuripan in East Java in the early 11th century. He wrote the Arjunawiwaha, composed around 1030, one of the earliest and most admired Old Javanese kakawin poems.

motupalli.s: Motupalli is a coastal village in Andhra Pradesh, India, that was a major seaport of the Kakatiya dynasty and later of the Reddi kingdom. Around 1245 King Ganapatideva issued an inscription there guaranteeing fair treatment to foreign merchants, and Marco Polo described the…

mattamayura.s: The Mattamayura order was a Shaiva Siddhanta monastic lineage of medieval central India, named after its first monastic centre. From the 9th century its teachers became royal preceptors and ran monasteries supported by the Kalachuris of Tripuri and other dynasties, such as the…

mantingan-mosque.s: The Mantingan Mosque is a mosque near Jepara on the north coast of Central Java, Indonesia, built in 1559 under the patronage of Ratu Kalinyamat. It is known for its carved stone panels with floral and landscape designs, a blend of Hindu-Javanese and Islamic art.

malang.s: Malang is a city in the highlands of East Java, Indonesia, and the second-largest city in the province. The area holds some of the earliest remains of Javanese kingdoms, including the Dinoyo inscription of 760 and Candi Badut, and later lay at the heart of the Singhasari kingdom.

muhammad-alwali-ii.s: Muhammad Alwali II was the last Hausa king of Kano, ruling from 1781. When the Fulani jihad of Usman dan Fodio spread in the early 1800s, he fought the local jihadist leaders but was defeated and driven from Kano by 1807, and he was killed soon afterwards.

mbuji-mayi-river.s: The Mbuji-Mayi River is a river of the southern Kasai region of the Democratic Republic of the Congo and a tributary of the Lubilash, the upper Sankuru. Rich diamond deposits along its course gave rise to the city of Mbuji-Mayi, named after it.

molla-panah-vagif.s: Molla Panah Vagif was an Azerbaijani poet and statesman who served as vizier of the Karabakh Khanate under Ibrahim Khalil Khan. His lyric poems, written in a simple style close to spoken Azerbaijani, made him one of the founders of modern Azerbaijani poetry.

moynaq.s: Moynaq is a town in Karakalpakstan, Uzbekistan, that was once a fishing port on the southern shore of the Aral Sea. As Soviet irrigation from the Amu Darya shrank the sea from the 1960s, the shoreline retreated far away, destroying its fishing and canning industry.

mysia.s: Mysia is a historical region of north-western Anatolia, lying south of the Sea of Marmara and bordering the Troad, Lydia and Bithynia. In antiquity it included Pergamon, capital of the Attalid kingdom, and later formed part of the Roman province of Asia.

maharaja.s: Maharaja ('great king') is a Sanskrit royal title used across South Asia, originally for major sovereigns and later by many Hindu and Sikh rulers of princely states. Under the Mughals and the British the title was often granted or recognised by the paramount power as a mark of…

martand-sun-temple.s: The Martand Sun Temple is a ruined Hindu temple dedicated to Surya on a plateau near Anantnag in the Kashmir valley. It was built in the 8th century by Lalitaditya Muktapida of the Karkota dynasty, within a large colonnaded courtyard.

mount-ochi.s: Mount Ochi is the highest mountain of southern Euboea in Greece, rising above the town of Karystos. Near its summit stands the best-known of the 'dragon houses', a building of massive stone slabs of uncertain date and purpose.

mukalla.s: Mukalla is a port city on the Arabian Sea coast of eastern Yemen and the main seaport of the Hadramawt. In the 18th and 19th centuries it was ruled by the Kasadi family and then by the Qu'aiti sultans, who made it their capital under British protection.

mir-sayyid-ali-hamadani.s: Mir Sayyid Ali Hamadani was a Persian Sufi of the Kubrawiya order who visited Kashmir in the 1370s and 1380s with many followers. He is credited with spreading Islam in the valley and with introducing Persian crafts such as shawl-weaving.

mirza-muhammad-haidar-dughlat.s: Mirza Muhammad Haidar Dughlat was a Central Asian prince, soldier and historian, a cousin of the Mughal emperor Babur. He conquered Kashmir in 1540 and ruled it, nominally for the Mughal Humayun, until he was killed in 1551.

mohammad-afzal-khan.s: Mohammad Afzal Khan was the eldest son of Dost Mohammad Khan and emir of Afghanistan from 1865 to 1867. As governor in the north he conquered Kunduz and other Uzbek principalities for his father in the 1850s.

mehsana-district.s: Mehsana district is a district of northern Gujarat, India, with its headquarters at Mehsana. It was formed largely from the Kadi division of Baroda State and neighbouring small princely states, which merged into Bombay Province in 1948–1949.

muhammadu-korau.s: Muhammadu Korau is remembered in tradition as the first Muslim king of Katsina, one of the Hausa kingdoms of northern Nigeria, and is usually dated to the second half of the 15th century. Tradition also makes Korau a wrestler who killed Sanau, last ruler of the earlier Durbawa…

maikal-range.s: The Maikal Range is a forested range of hills in central India, on the border of Madhya Pradesh and Chhattisgarh, forming the eastern arm of the Satpura system. Its plateau of Amarkantak is the source of the Narmada and Son rivers.

marad.s: Marad was an ancient Sumerian city in central Mesopotamia, west of Nippur, identified with the mound of Tell Wanna wa Sadum in Iraq. Its patron god was Lugal-Marada.

maragtas.s: The Maragtas is a book published in 1907 by Pedro Monteclaro in Iloilo, setting out a legendary history of Panay drawn from oral tradition. It tells of ten datus from Borneo who bought land from the Ati and founded settlements on the island.

marikudo.s: Marikudo is the Ati chief of Panay in the Maragtas legend of the Visayas in the Philippines. In the story he sold the lowlands of the island to ten datus from Borneo, led by Datu Puti, for a golden salakot and a long gold necklace, and moved with his people into the hills.

madaoua.s: Madaoua is a town in the Tahoua Region of southern Niger, near the Nigerian border. It lies on the northern edge of the Hausa lands, in a zone where farmers and Tuareg herders such as the Kel Gres met and traded.

mwai-kibaki.s: Mwai Kibaki was president of Kenya from 2002 to 2013. An economist, he served as finance minister under Jomo Kenyatta and vice-president under Daniel arap Moi before leading the opposition.

manghit-dynasty.s: The Manghits were an Uzbek tribe whose chiefs ruled Bukhara from the mid-18th century until 1920. Muhammad Rahim, who held the office of atalik, took effective power under Nader Shah's protection, and in 1785 his relative Shah Murad founded the Emirate of Bukhara, the dynasty…

mehrab-khan.s: Mehrab Khan was the Khan of Kalat, ruler of the Baloch and Brahui tribal confederacy of Balochistan, from 1817 to 1839. During the First Anglo-Afghan War the British accused him of obstructing their army's march through the Bolan Pass, and on 13 November 1839 a British force…

mikhail-skobelev.s: Mikhail Skobelev was a Russian general famous for his campaigns in Central Asia and the Balkans. He crushed the Kokand rising of 1875–76 and became the first governor of the Fergana Oblast, then won fame at Plevna and Shipka-Sheinovo in the Russo-Turkish War of 1877–78.

maku.s: Maku is a town in West Azerbaijan province in the far north-west of Iran, built in a narrow gorge beneath an overhanging cliff near the borders with Turkey and Nakhchivan and close to Mount Ararat. From the mid-18th century to the 1920s it was ruled by hereditary khans of the…

mansi.s: The Mansi, formerly called Voguls, are a Finno-Ugric people of western Siberia and the eastern slopes of the northern Urals, living mainly in the Khanty-Mansi Autonomous Okrug. Hunters, fishers and herders, they paid fur tribute to the Khanate of Sibir and came under Russian…

motronynskyi-monastery.s: The Motronynskyi Holy Trinity Monastery is an Orthodox monastery in the Kholodny Yar forest near Chyhyryn in Cherkasy Oblast, central Ukraine. Its abbot Melkhisedek Znachko-Yavorsky supported the haidamaks of the Koliivshchyna rising of 1768, who according to tradition…

mutsu-munemitsu.s: Mutsu Munemitsu was a Japanese statesman from the Kii domain who served as foreign minister from 1892 to 1896. He negotiated the Anglo-Japanese Treaty of Commerce and Navigation of 1894, which ended British extraterritoriality in Japan, and with Itō Hirobumi concluded the…
