mokvi-cathedral.s: Mokvi Cathedral is a medieval church in the Ochamchire district of Abkhazia, built in the 950s or 960s by Leon III, king of the Abkhazians, as the seat of a bishopric. A large cross-domed building, it was also a centre of learning, where the illuminated manuscript known as the…

mac-lochlainn-dynasty.s: The Mac Lochlainn were a branch of the Cenél nEógain that held the kingship of Ailech for much of the 11th and 12th centuries. Domnall Ua Lochlainn and his grandson Muirchertach Mac Lochlainn claimed the high kingship of Ireland.

macmahons-of-oriel.s: The MacMahons, Mac Mathghamhna in Irish, were the ruling family of the lordship of Oriel, the remnant of the kingdom of Airgialla in what is now County Monaghan, from the 13th to the late 16th century. After the execution of Hugh Roe MacMahon in 1590 the English divided their…

mellifont-abbey.s: Mellifont Abbey, in County Louth, was the first Cistercian monastery in Ireland, founded in 1142 by Saint Malachy with monks from Clairvaux, under the patronage of Donnchad Ua Cerbaill, king of Airgialla. It became the mother house of many Irish Cistercian abbeys.

mono-river.s: The Mono is a river of West Africa which flows south through Togo and, in its lower course, forms part of the border between Togo and Benin before reaching the Gulf of Guinea. Tado, the traditional homeland of the Aja peoples, lies near it, and the Nangbéto Dam on its course…

medinet-habu.s: Medinet Habu is an archaeological site on the west bank of the Nile at Thebes, modern Luxor, in Egypt, dominated by the mortuary temple of Ramesses III, built in the early 12th century BCE. Its walls carry reliefs and inscriptions of the king's wars, including the best-known…

mrauk-u.s: Mrauk U is a town in Rakhine State, western Myanmar, that was the capital of the Arakanese kingdom from 1430 to 1785. Founded by Min Saw Mon after he regained his throne with help from the Bengal Sultanate, it grew rich on trade across the Bay of Bengal and was visited by…

mamikonian-dynasty.s: The Mamikonian family was one of the most powerful noble houses of ancient and early medieval Armenia, holding the hereditary office of commander-in-chief (sparapet) under the Arsacid kings. Its members led the Armenian defence of Christianity against Sasanian Persia, most…

mesrop-mashtots.s: Mesrop Mashtots was an Armenian monk and scholar who created the Armenian alphabet around 405 with the support of King Vramshapuh and the Catholicos Sahak. With his pupils he translated the Bible and other Christian texts, beginning a golden age of Armenian literature.

moree.s: Moree is a fishing town on the coast of Ghana's Central Region, a few kilometres east of Cape Coast. It was the port of the Fante kingdom of Asebu, whose rulers invited the Dutch to trade there, and in 1612 the Dutch built Fort Nassau at Moree, their first fortified post on…

monte-naranco.s: Monte Naranco is a hill overlooking Oviedo in Asturias, northern Spain. On its slopes King Ramiro I of Asturias built a royal complex in the 840s, of which two buildings survive: the palace hall later converted into the church of Santa María del Naranco, dedicated in 848, and…

mahishmati.s: Mahishmati was an ancient city on the Narmada river in central India, the southern capital of the kingdom of Avanti and later the seat of the Kalachuris of Mahishmati. It appears in the Sanskrit epics and Puranas and is usually identified with Maheshwar in Madhya Pradesh,…

mads-lange.s: Mads Lange was a Danish trader who ran a large trading post at Kuta in southern Bali from the late 1830s under the protection of the raja of Badung. He exported rice, coconut oil and other goods, supplied passing ships and acted as a go-between in the Dutch campaigns against…

massenya.s: Massenya is a town in south-western Chad, south-east of Lake Chad and N'Djamena. It was the capital of the Sultanate of Baguirmi from the 16th century, a walled trading and slave-raiding centre.

maximilian-von-montgelas.s: Maximilian von Montgelas was a Bavarian statesman who, as chief minister of Maximilian IV Joseph, later King Maximilian I, from 1799 to 1817, created the modern Bavarian state. Allied with Napoleon, he greatly enlarged Bavaria's territory and saw it become a kingdom in 1806,…

maupiti.s: Maupiti is the westernmost high island of the Leeward Society Islands in French Polynesia, a small volcanic island surrounded by a lagoon and low coral islets, about 40 kilometres west of Bora Bora. In the 18th century it was conquered by the chiefs of Bora Bora.

monasterboice.s: Monasterboice is a ruined early medieval monastery in County Louth, Ireland, north of Drogheda, founded according to tradition by St Buite in the late 5th century. It is best known for its high crosses, above all Muiredach's Cross of the 10th century, one of the finest in…

mutesa-i-of-buganda.s: Mutesa I was kabaka of Buganda from 1856 to 1884. He strengthened royal power over the chiefs and opened his court to Arab and Swahili traders, adopting some Islamic practices.

mbarara.s: Mbarara is the largest city of south-western Uganda and the historic headquarters of the Kingdom of Ankole. The British set up their district administration there around 1900, and it became the centre of Ankole district and a market town for the region's cattle-keeping and…

mamankam-festival.s: The Mamankam was a great festival held every twelve years on the banks of the Bharathappuzha at Thirunavaya in Kerala. In the later Middle Ages the Zamorin of Calicut took control of it and presided as its protector, while warriors sent by the rival ruler of Valluvanad tried…

mount-erciyes.s: Mount Erciyes, the ancient Mount Argaeus, is a dormant volcano south of Kayseri in central Anatolia, Turkey, and at 3,917 metres the highest mountain in the region. The kings of Cappadocia ruled from Mazaca at its foot, and the mountain appeared on the city's coins.

meshan.s: Meshan was a province of the Sasanian Empire at the head of the Persian Gulf, in present-day southern Iraq, corresponding to the earlier kingdom of Characene, also called Mesene. Ardashir I conquered it around 222 CE, and Sasanian princes sometimes governed it with the title…

minchancaman.s: Minchancaman was the last independent ruler of Chimor, the kingdom of the north coast of Peru centred on Chan Chan. Under him Chimor reached its greatest extent, as far north as Tumbes.

mithridates-i-callinicus.s: Mithridates I Callinicus was king of Commagene, in south-eastern Anatolia, from about 109 to 70 BCE. He married Laodice, daughter of the Seleucid king Antiochus VIII, uniting Persian and Macedonian royal lines, a double heritage that his son and successor Antiochus I Theos…

mount-nemrut.s: Mount Nemrut is a 2,134-metre mountain in south-eastern Turkey, near Adıyaman, crowned by the tomb sanctuary of Antiochus I Theos of Commagene, built in the 1st century BCE. Colossal seated statues of the king and of gods combining Greek and Persian features flank an…

madikeri.s: Madikeri, formerly Mercara, is a hill town in Karnataka, India, and the headquarters of Kodagu district. Founded as the capital of the Haleri rajas of Coorg in the late 17th century, it has a fort rebuilt by Tipu Sultan and the domed tombs of the rajas.

magas-of-cyrene.s: Magas was ruler of Cyrene, a son of Ptolemy I's queen Berenice I by an earlier marriage. Made governor of Cyrene around 300 BCE, he later declared himself king and in the 270s BCE, allied with the Seleucids, marched on Egypt against his half-brother Ptolemy II, until a Libyan…

muskerry.s: Muskerry is a region of central County Cork, Ireland, west of the city of Cork, preserved in the baronies of East and West Muskerry. From the 14th century it was ruled by the MacCarthys of Muskerry, a branch of the MacCarthy kings of Desmond, who built Blarney Castle and were…

mandalay.s: Mandalay is the second-largest city of Myanmar, on the east bank of the Irrawaddy in Upper Burma. It was founded by King Mindon in 1857 as the royal capital of the Konbaung dynasty and remained so until the British annexation of 1885.

macregol-gospels.s: The Macregol Gospels, or Book of MacRegol, is an illuminated Irish gospel book of about 800, written by Mac Regol, abbot of Birr, who died in 822. Decorated in the Insular style with evangelist portraits and elaborate initials, it was later glossed in Old English and is now in…

magna-carta.s: Magna Carta is the charter of liberties that rebellious barons forced King John of England to accept at Runnymede in June 1215. It limited royal power, protected the rights of the barons and the church, and promised lawful judgement to free men.

molossians.s: The Molossians were the leading tribe of ancient Epirus, in north-western Greece, around Dodona and the Ioannina basin. Ruled by the Aeacid kings, who claimed descent from Achilles, they united the Epirote tribes under their leadership and produced Olympias and Pyrrhus.

mellitus.s: Mellitus was a member of the Gregorian mission sent to England in 601, who became the first bishop of London in 604 under King Sæberht of Essex. Expelled when Sæberht's pagan sons took power around 616, he later returned and was archbishop of Canterbury from 619 until his…

middlesex.s: Middlesex is a historic county of England, north and west of the City of London, between the Thames and the Lea. Its name means 'the Middle Saxons', and in the early Middle Ages it formed part of the kingdom of Essex before passing under Mercian control.

mutara-ii-rwogera.s: Mutara II Rwogera was mwami, or king, of Rwanda in the first half of the 19th century. His reign saw the conquest of the eastern kingdom of Gisaka around 1852, which added a large territory to Rwanda.

meurig-ap-tewdrig.s: Meurig ap Tewdrig was a king of Glywysing and Gwent in south-east Wales, probably in the 6th or 7th century. The charters of the Book of Llandaff record his grants to the church, and his descendants ruled both kingdoms for generations.

monmouthshire.s: Monmouthshire is a county in south-east Wales, bordering England along the River Wye. It was created in 1536 under the Laws in Wales Acts from marcher lordships that had grown out of the Norman conquest of the old Welsh kingdom of Gwent.

milot.s: Milot is a town in northern Haiti, about 20 kilometres south of Cap-Haïtien. Henri Christophe built his royal palace of Sans-Souci there from 1810, and the Citadelle Laferrière stands on the mountain above it.

maeva.s: Maeva is a village on the island of Huahine in the Society Islands, beside the lagoon of Lake Fauna Nui. It was the seat of the island's chiefly families, and its shores hold one of the largest groups of marae, stone temple platforms, in French Polynesia, many of them…

maiao.s: Maiao is a small, low island in the Windward group of the Society Islands, about 80 kilometres west of Moorea, enclosing two lagoons. In the 18th and 19th centuries it was ruled with Huahine by the same royal line.

magyarisation.s: Magyarisation was the policy of spreading the Hungarian language and identity among the non-Hungarian peoples of the Kingdom of Hungary, pursued especially after the Compromise of 1867. Measures such as the Apponyi school laws of 1907 required teaching in Hungarian, and many…

mirian-iii-of-iberia.s: Mirian III was king of Iberia, or Kartli, in eastern Georgia in the early 4th century and the first Christian ruler of the country. Georgian tradition, which echoes an account by the church historian Rufinus, holds that he and his wife Nana were converted through Saint Nino in…

mtskheta.s: Mtskheta is a small town north of Tbilisi in Georgia, where the Aragvi meets the Kura. It was the capital of the ancient kingdom of Iberia, or Kartli, until about the late 5th or 6th century, and the centre of its conversion to Christianity.

modakeke.s: Modakeke is a town in Osun State in south-western Nigeria, adjoining Ile-Ife. It was founded in the 19th century by Oyo Yoruba refugees settled at Ife during the wars that followed the collapse of the Oyo Empire.

malembo.s: Malembo was a port on the Atlantic coast of Cabinda, in present-day Angola, in the old kingdom of Kakongo. In the 18th century it was one of the busiest slave-trading harbours of the Loango Coast, much used by French and English ships, and in the 19th century it traded in palm…

mahanadi.s: The Mahanadi is a major river of east-central India, about 850 kilometres long, rising in Chhattisgarh and flowing through Odisha to the Bay of Bengal. Its fertile delta around Cuttack was a heartland of ancient Kalinga and of later Odia kingdoms, and many small princely…

mcmahon-hussein-correspondence.s: The McMahon–Hussein Correspondence was an exchange of letters in 1915–1916 between Sir Henry McMahon, British High Commissioner in Egypt, and Hussein bin Ali, Sharif of Mecca. Britain promised to recognise Arab independence in a broad region in return for an Arab revolt…

mushegh-of-kars.s: Mushegh was the first king of Kars and a younger brother of Ashot III of Bagratid Armenia. In 963 Ashot granted him the district of Vanand with the fortress of Kars, and he ruled it as a subordinate Bagratid kingdom until his death in 984, founding a line that lasted until 1065.

msiri.s: Msiri was a Nyamwezi trader from western Tanzania who founded the Yeke kingdom in Katanga in the second half of the 19th century. Arriving around 1856, he built a state at Bunkeya based on trade in copper, ivory and slaves, at the expense of the Kingdom of Kazembe and the Luba.

mutomboko.s: The Mutomboko is an annual ceremony of the Lunda people of the Luapula valley in Zambia, held each July at Mwansabombwe, the seat of the Mwata Kazembe. It commemorates the Lunda migration from the kingdom of the Mwata Yamvo and the conquest of the Luapula valley in the 18th…

medine-mali.s: Médine is a village on the Senegal River near Kayes in western Mali, just below the Felou Falls. In 1855 Louis Faidherbe built a French fort there, which in 1857 withstood a three-month siege by El Hadj Umar Tall's army until relieved, a turning point in French expansion up…

maadd.s: Ma'add was a confederation of tribes of central and western Arabia in late antiquity. South Arabian inscriptions of the 4th to 6th centuries record Himyarite campaigns against Ma'add, and the Himyarite kings set the Kindite house over them to control the interior.

muallaqat.s: The Mu'allaqat, or Suspended Odes, are a collection of seven (in some versions ten) long pre-Islamic Arabic poems regarded as the finest of early Arabic poetry. Tradition says they were hung on the Kaaba in Mecca, though the story is doubtful.

melqart.s: Melqart was the chief god of the Phoenician city of Tyre, whose name means 'king of the city'. Worshipped as protector of the city and its colonies, he had an annual festival of awakening, and his cult spread to Cyprus, Carthage and Gades in Spain.

mahmud-barzanji.s: Sheikh Mahmud Barzanji was a Kurdish leader from Sulaymaniyah in northern Iraq and a sheikh of the Qadiri Sufi order. Appointed governor by the British in 1918, he soon rebelled and was exiled, but returned in 1922 and proclaimed himself king of the Kingdom of Kurdistan.

mulavarman.s: Mulavarman was a king of Kutai in eastern Borneo around the late 4th or early 5th century, the grandson of Kudungga. Seven stone pillars (yupa) found at Muara Kaman record in Sanskrit, in a southern Indian Pallava script, his gifts of thousands of cattle to Brahmins and his…

muara-kaman.s: Muara Kaman is a village on the Mahakam River in East Kalimantan, Indonesia, where seven inscribed stone pillars (yupa) of King Mulavarman of Kutai were found. Dating from around 400, they are the oldest known inscriptions in Indonesia, and the area is regarded as the centre…

muammar-gaddafi.s: Muammar Gaddafi was the ruler of Libya from 1969 to 2011. A young army officer, he led the coup of 1 September 1969 that overthrew King Idris and set up a revolutionary republic, later called the Jamahiriya, based on the ideas of his Green Book.

maria-vladimirovna-staritskaya.s: Maria Vladimirovna Staritskaya was a Russian princess, daughter of Prince Vladimir of Staritsa and a relative of Tsar Ivan IV. In 1573 she married Duke Magnus of Holstein, whom Ivan had made king of Livonia as his vassal.

mbanza-loango.s: Mbanza Loango, also called Buali, was the capital of the Kingdom of Loango on the coast of the present-day Republic of the Congo, near Loango Bay. European visitors from the 17th century described a large town of royal enclosures and markets where the Maloango held court.

maloango.s: Maloango, or Ma Loango, was the title of the king of Loango on the Atlantic coast north of the Congo River. The holder was a sacred ruler chosen from princes of the royal matrilineage, surrounded by taboos and assisted by officials in charge of trade, war and the coast.

mary-i-of-england.s: Mary I was queen of England and Ireland from 1553 to 1558, the daughter of Henry VIII and Catherine of Aragon. She restored Catholicism, married Philip II of Spain in 1554 and had about 280 Protestants burned for heresy.

menes.s: Menes was the king whom later Egyptian tradition and Greek historians credited with uniting Upper and Lower Egypt and founding the First Dynasty around 3100 BCE. Manetho and Herodotus said he founded Memphis.

mbona.s: Mbona is a rain cult of the lower Shire valley in southern Malawi, centred on a shrine at Khulubvi. According to tradition Mbona was a rain-maker killed by a chief and later venerated as a spirit who controls rain and fertility.

manganja.s: The Manganja, or Mang'anja, are a Chewa-related people of the Shire valley and highlands of southern Malawi. From the 16th century they lived under the Lundu, a branch of the ruling Phiri clan of the Maravi, and traded ivory and iron goods.

mermnad-dynasty.s: The Mermnad dynasty ruled the Kingdom of Lydia from Sardis from about 680 BCE until the Persian conquest around 547 BCE. Its kings, Gyges, Ardys, Sadyattes, Alyattes and Croesus, subdued most of the Greek cities of Ionia, fought the Cimmerians and the Medes, and issued the…

minaic-language.s: Minaic was the Ancient South Arabian language of the Kingdom of Ma'in in the al-Jawf region of Yemen, written in the South Arabian script. It is known from inscriptions of roughly the 8th to the 1st century BCE, found in Yemen and at Minaean trading posts as far as Dedan in…

mir-qasim.s: Mir Qasim was Nawab of Bengal from 1760 to 1763, installed by the East India Company in place of his father-in-law Mir Jafar. He moved his capital to Munger, reorganised his army and abolished internal duties, which brought him into conflict with Company traders.

manua-islands.s: The Manuʻa Islands are a group of three volcanic islands, Taʻu, Ofu and Olosega, at the eastern end of the Samoan archipelago, about 100 kilometres east of Tutuila. Seat of the ancient title of Tuʻi Manuʻa, they were ceded to the United States in 1904 and are part of American…

manica-mozambique.s: Manica, formerly Macequece, is a town in western Mozambique near the border with Zimbabwe. It grew from Masekesa, a Portuguese gold-trading fair in the Manyika highlands.

mutasa.s: Mutasa is the hereditary title of the rulers of Manyika, a Shona kingdom in the highlands on the border of present-day Zimbabwe and Mozambique. From the 16th century the Mutasa controlled alluvial gold and trade routes to the coast, dealing with the Portuguese at the fair of…

mapungubwe-hill.s: Mapungubwe Hill is a flat-topped sandstone hill in the Limpopo valley of northern South Africa, near the confluence with the Shashe. Around 1220 the ruling elite moved onto its summit, apart from commoners below, and royal graves there contained gold objects including the…

malawi.s: Malawi is a landlocked country in south-eastern Africa, lying along the western shore of Lake Malawi. Its name recalls the Maravi confederacy of the 16th and 17th centuries.

mauri.s: The Mauri were the ancient Berber people of north-western Africa, in what is now northern Morocco and western Algeria, from whom the names Mauretania and Moors derive. United under kings by the late 3rd century BCE, they became Roman allies and then subjects after their…

moulouya-river.s: The Moulouya is a river of north-eastern Morocco, about 520 kilometres long, that rises in the Middle Atlas and flows north into the Mediterranean near the Algerian border. In antiquity, as the Mulucha, it formed the border between the kingdoms of Mauretania and Numidia, and…

martin-de-goiti.s: Martín de Goiti was a Basque conquistador who served under Miguel López de Legazpi in the Spanish conquest of the Philippines. In 1570 he led an expedition to Manila that clashed with Rajah Sulayman and burned the town, and in 1571 he defeated a Tagalog and Kapampangan fleet…

merionethshire.s: Merionethshire, or Merioneth, was a historic county of north-west Wales, created by the Statute of Rhuddlan in 1284 after the English conquest of Gwynedd. It took its name from the early kingdom of Meirionnydd and had Dolgellau and Harlech as its main towns.

mande-peoples.s: The Mande peoples are a family of ethnic groups of West Africa who speak Mande languages, among them the Malinke, Bambara, Soninke, Dyula and Mende. Their heartland, the Manden on the upper Niger, was the core of the Mali Empire founded by Sundiata Keita in the 13th century.

mael-sechnaill-mac-maele-ruanaid.s: Máel Sechnaill mac Máele Ruanaid was king of Mide and, from 846, high king of Ireland, of the Clann Cholmáin. He fought the Vikings, drowning their leader Turgesius in 845, and he was the first high king to obtain the submission of most Irish provinces, including Munster.

metohija.s: Metohija is the western part of Kosovo, a fertile basin drained by the White Drin that includes the towns of Peć, Prizren and Gjakova. Its name comes from the Greek word for church estates, recalling the lands of medieval Serbian monasteries such as the Patriarchate of Peć.

meic-uilleim.s: The Meic Uilleim, or MacWilliams, were descendants of William fitz Duncan, a grandson of Malcolm III, who claimed the Scottish throne. From the 1180s they raised repeated revolts in Moray and Ross against the kings William the Lion and Alexander II.

malcolm-iii-of-scotland.s: Malcolm III, called Canmore, was king of Scots from 1058 to 1093. He killed Macbeth in 1057 and Lulach in 1058, and married first Ingibiorg and then the English princess Margaret, whose sons founded the line of later Scottish kings.

macdermot.s: The MacDermots, Irish Mac Diarmada, were a Gaelic family who ruled Moylurg in north County Roscommon from the 12th century, as a branch of the Síl Muiredaig and marshals of the O'Connor kings of Connacht. They ruled from the Rock of Lough Cé and patronised Boyle Abbey and…

muirchertach-ua-briain.s: Muirchertach Ua Briain was king of Munster and high king of Ireland with opposition, a great-grandson of Brian Boru. Ruling from 1086, he made Limerick a royal centre, gave the Rock of Cashel to the Church in 1101 and sponsored the reforming Synod of Cashel.

mudejar-revolt-of-1264-1266.s: The Mudéjar revolt of 1264–1266 was an uprising of Muslims living under Castilian rule in Andalusia and Murcia, supported by the Nasrid emir of Granada. It briefly restored Muslim control of Murcia.

masaniello.s: Masaniello, born Tommaso Aniello, was a Neapolitan fisherman who led the revolt of Naples against Spanish rule and a new tax on fruit in July 1647. For about ten days he dominated the city and negotiated with the viceroy, but he grew erratic and was murdered on 16 July 1647.

mbundu.s: The Mbundu, or Ambundu, are a Bantu-speaking people of north-central Angola who speak Kimbundu. Their chiefdoms between the Kwanza and Lucala rivers formed the kingdom of Ndongo, whose ruler bore the title ngola, the origin of the name Angola.

mahendra-of-nepal.s: Mahendra was King of Nepal from 1955 until his death in 1972. In December 1960 he dismissed the elected government of B.

muluki-ain.s: The Muluki Ain is the national legal code of Nepal issued in 1854 under the Rana prime minister Jang Bahadur Rana. It codified civil and criminal law and placed every group in the kingdom within a single caste hierarchy, from the 'sacred-thread-wearing' high castes through the…

magdalensberg.s: The Magdalensberg is a mountain in Carinthia, Austria, whose summit and slopes hold the remains of a large Celtic and early Roman settlement. From the 1st century BCE it was a trading centre where Italian merchants bought Noric iron, and it probably served as the capital of…

monkwearmouth-jarrow-abbey.s: Monkwearmouth–Jarrow Abbey was a twin monastery in Northumbria, founded by Benedict Biscop at Wearmouth in 674 and at Jarrow around 681–82. Biscop brought books, masons and glaziers from Gaul and Rome, and the house became a leading centre of learning.

magnus-vi-of-norway.s: Magnus VI, called the Lawmender, was King of Norway from 1263 to 1280. He gave Norway a single national law code, the Landslov of 1274, and a town law in 1276, replacing the regional laws.

martti-rautanen.s: Martti Rautanen was a Finnish Lutheran missionary who worked among the Ovambo of northern Namibia from 1870 until his death in 1926. Based at Olukonda in Ondonga, where he was known as Nakambale, he translated the Bible and other texts into Oshindonga, founded the first…

minab.s: Minab is a city in Hormozgan Province in southern Iran, on the Minab River near the Strait of Hormuz. It lies near the site of Old Hormuz, the mainland port and capital of the kingdom of Hormuz until around 1300, when raids drove its king to move to the island of Jarun.

mogho-naaba-wobgo.s: Mogho Naaba Wobgo, born Boukary Koutou, was king of the Mossi kingdom of Ouagadougou from about 1890. He resisted French expansion, and when French forces took Ouagadougou in 1896 he fled and continued resistance from exile in the Gold Coast, where he died in 1904.

macedonia-roman-province.s: Macedonia was a province of the Roman Republic and Empire, created in 146 BCE after Rome had defeated the last Macedonian kings and suppressed the revolt of Andriscus. Governed from Thessalonica, it covered most of the old kingdom of Macedon, Paeonia and parts of Epirus and…

midas.s: Midas was a king of Phrygia in the late 8th century BCE, ruling from Gordion. Assyrian records call him Mita of Mushki and show him as a rival and later a correspondent of Sargon II.

mieszko-ii-lambert.s: Mieszko II Lambert was King of Poland from 1025 to 1031 and again ruled from 1032 until his death in 1034, son of Bolesław I the Brave. His reign saw attacks by the Holy Roman Empire and Kievan Rus, revolts by his brothers, the loss of Lusatia and the royal crown, and the…

mithridates-i-of-pontus.s: Mithridates I Ktistes, 'the Founder', was the first king of Pontus. A noble of Persian descent from the family that ruled Kios on the Sea of Marmara, he escaped the wars of Alexander's successors around 302 BCE and established himself in north-eastern Anatolia.

madog-ap-maredudd.s: Madog ap Maredudd was the last king of the whole of Powys, ruling from 1132 until his death in 1160. Allied with Henry II of England against Owain Gwynedd, he extended Powys to the east and was praised by the court poets.

magnus-maximus.s: Magnus Maximus was a Roman general of Spanish origin who, as commander in Britain, was proclaimed emperor by his troops in 383. He crossed to Gaul, where the emperor Gratian was killed, and ruled Britain, Gaul and Spain from Trier until he invaded Italy and was defeated and…

mathrafal.s: Mathrafal is a site near Meifod in Montgomeryshire, mid-Wales, traditionally the chief court of the kings and princes of Powys from the 9th century. A ringwork and bailey castle survives there, probably built in the late 12th or early 13th century.

markos-monastery.s: Marko's Monastery is a Serbian Orthodox monastery of Saint Demetrius in the village of Markova Sušica near Skopje, North Macedonia. Its church was begun in 1345 by Vukašin and completed around 1376–77 by his son Prince Marko, whose portraits appear among its frescoes.

michael-ventris.s: Michael Ventris was an English architect and amateur linguist who deciphered Linear B, the script of the Mycenaean palaces. In 1952, working from the tablets found at Pylos and Knossos, he showed that it recorded an early form of Greek, and with John Chadwick he published…

mahanaga.s: Mahanaga was, according to the Mahavamsa, a brother of King Devanampiya Tissa of Anuradhapura who in the 3rd century BCE fled south after an attempt on his life and founded the kingdom of Ruhuna. He is credited with establishing Mahagama, later Tissamaharama, as its capital.

marib.s: Marib is a town in central Yemen on the edge of the Ramlat al-Sabatayn desert, capital of Marib Governorate. In antiquity it was the capital of the kingdom of Saba, sustained by the great Marib Dam and the incense trade, and it has major ruins including the Awwam and Bar'an…

malietoa-tanumafili-i.s: Malietoa Tanumafili I was a Samoan paramount chief, son of Malietoa Laupepa. After his father's death in 1898 he was declared king, but his succession was disputed by Mataʻafa Iosefo, and the ensuing war and foreign intervention led to the abolition of the kingship by the…

mulinuu.s: Mulinuʻu is a low peninsula on the western side of Apia harbour on Upolu, Samoa. Samoan chiefs set up their central government there in 1873, and it remained a seat of royal and rival Samoan governments during the conflicts of the late 19th century.

macedonian-front.s: The Macedonian front, also called the Salonika front, was a theatre of the First World War in northern Greece and southern Serbia. Allied forces landed at Salonika in October 1915 and, joined by the rebuilt Serbian army, held a line against Bulgarian and German troops for…

mileseva-monastery.s: Mileševa is a Serbian Orthodox monastery near Prijepolje in south-western Serbia, founded by King Stefan Vladislav in the 1230s. Its frescoes include the celebrated White Angel at the tomb of Christ.

magdala.s: Magdala, or Amba Mekdela, is a mountain fortress in the Wollo highlands of northern Ethiopia. Emperor Tewodros II made it his stronghold and kept political prisoners there, including the young Menelik of Shewa, who escaped in 1865.

monreale-cathedral.s: Monreale Cathedral is a church in the hills above Palermo in Sicily, founded by King William II in 1174 together with a Benedictine abbey. Its interior is covered with vast gold-ground mosaics of Old and New Testament scenes, and its cloister has more than 200 carved columns.

mayadunne.s: Mayadunne was king of Sitawaka in Sri Lanka from 1521 to 1581. One of the princes who divided the Kingdom of Kotte after the Vijayabahu Kollaya, he waged almost constant war against his brother Bhuvanaikabahu VII and the Portuguese who supported Kotte.

morphou.s: Morphou is a town in north-western Cyprus, near the bay of the same name, in a fertile plain known for citrus growing. The ancient city-kingdom of Soloi lay on the bay to the west, near the copper mines of Skouriotissa.

mount-batukaru.s: Mount Batukaru is a volcano in western Bali, Indonesia, and the second-highest peak on the island, at about 2,276 metres. Its slopes feed the rice terraces of Tabanan, including those of Jatiluwih, part of the subak irrigation landscape listed as a World Heritage Site.

moorea.s: Moorea is a volcanic island in the Society Islands of French Polynesia, about 17 kilometres north-west of Tahiti. In the late 18th and early 19th centuries it was closely bound up with Tahitian politics, and Pōmare II took refuge there before regaining Tahiti in 1815.

mahavamsa.s: The Mahavamsa, the "Great Chronicle", is a Pali chronicle of Sri Lanka composed at the Mahavihara monastery in Anuradhapura, traditionally by the monk Mahanama, around the 5th or 6th century CE. It narrates the island's history from the legendary arrival of Prince Vijaya to…

mannar.s: Mannar is a town on Mannar Island off the north-west coast of Sri Lanka, linked to the mainland by a causeway. It lies at the start of Adam's Bridge, the chain of shoals towards India, and the nearby ancient port of Mantai was a major centre of trade in the first millennium CE.

masties.s: Masties was a Berber ruler in the Aurès mountains in the late 5th or early 6th century, known only from a Latin inscription found at Arris. In it he claims to have been duke for 67 years and emperor for 10, and never to have broken faith with either the Romans or the Moors.

magnis.s: Magnis was a small walled Roman town at Kenchester, west of Hereford in England, on the road along the Welsh border. Excavations have traced its defences and buildings of the 2nd to 4th centuries.

merewalh.s: Merewalh was the first known king of the Magonsaete, in the borderlands west of the Severn, in the mid 7th century. Later tradition made him a son of Penda of Mercia, though this is uncertain.

mildburh.s: Mildburh was a daughter of King Merewalh of the Magonsaete and the first abbess of the double monastery of Wenlock in Shropshire, founded around 680. Venerated as a saint, she was credited with miracles, and the rediscovery of her relics by the Cluniac monks of Wenlock in 1101…

much-wenlock.s: Much Wenlock is a market town in Shropshire, England, which grew around a monastery founded about 680 with Mildburh as its abbess. Refounded as a Cluniac priory in the late 11th century, Wenlock Priory became one of the richest religious houses in the region.

middle-angles.s: The Middle Angles were a group of Anglian peoples in the east Midlands of England, around the Fens and the Nene and Welland valleys. Around 653 Penda of Mercia made his son Peada their ruler, and Peada's baptism brought the first Christian mission to Mercian territory.

masuna.s: Masuna was a Berber king in western Algeria, named in an inscription of 508 at Altava as king of the peoples of the Moors and Romans. He is probably the Massonas whom Procopius describes as an ally of the Byzantine general Solomon against other Berber rulers in 535.

max-havelaar.s: Max Havelaar is a novel published in 1860 by Multatuli, the pen name of the former colonial official Eduard Douwes Dekker. Drawing on his service in Lebak on Java, it attacks the exploitation of Javanese peasants under the Dutch cultivation system and the local rulers who…

multatuli.s: Multatuli was the pen name of Eduard Douwes Dekker, a Dutch writer who served as a colonial official in the Dutch East Indies. After resigning as assistant resident of Lebak on Java in 1856, he wrote the novel Max Havelaar (1860), denouncing colonial abuses.

minerva.s: Minerva was the Roman goddess of wisdom, crafts and strategic war, identified with the Greek Athena. With Jupiter and Juno she formed the Capitoline Triad worshipped on the Capitol in Rome.

martin-of-braga.s: Martin of Braga was a monk from Pannonia who settled in Gallaecia in the 550s, founded the monastery of Dumio and became archbishop of Braga. He is credited with converting the Suebi from Arianism to Catholicism and presided over the Second Council of Braga in 572.

miro-king-of-the-suebi.s: Miro was king of the Suebi in Gallaecia from 570 to 583. A Catholic ruler, he supported the church reforms of Martin of Braga and the Second Council of Braga in 572.

makoko-iloo-i.s: Iloo I was the Makoko, or king, of the Tio (Teke) kingdom north of Malebo Pool in the late 19th century. On 10 September 1880 he signed a treaty with the French explorer Pierre Savorgnan de Brazza placing his lands under French protection and ceding the site where Brazzaville…

malebo-pool.s: Malebo Pool, formerly Stanley Pool, is a wide, lake-like stretch of the Congo River about 35 kilometres long, just above the rapids that block navigation to the sea. Kinshasa lies on its southern shore and Brazzaville on its northern, making it the meeting point of river…

maguire-dynasty.s: The Maguires, Mág Uidhir, were the ruling family of Fermanagh in Ireland from the late 13th century to the early 17th, with their seat at Enniskillen. Often under O'Neill overlordship, they controlled the Lough Erne waterways.

minet-el-beida.s: Minet el-Beida is a bay on the Syrian coast north of Latakia that served as the harbour of ancient Ugarit, about a kilometre from the city. In 1928 a farmer ploughing there broke into a Late Bronze Age tomb, leading to the excavations that uncovered Ugarit and its archives.

mano-people.s: The Mano are a Mande-speaking people of north-central Liberia and the neighbouring forest region of Guinea, living mainly in Nimba County. Traditionally rice farmers, they are known for their masks and for the Poro society, which shaped male initiation and authority.

menua.s: Menua was king of Urartu from about 810 to 786 BCE, the son of Ishpuini. He enlarged the kingdom by campaigns to the north, west and towards Lake Urmia and left many inscriptions recording his wars and buildings.

mayombe.s: Mayombe is a region of low mountains and dense rainforest along the Atlantic coast of west-central Africa, stretching across the Cabinda enclave of Angola, the Kongo Central province of the Democratic Republic of the Congo and the Republic of the Congo. It is the home of the…

mbandzeni.s: Mbandzeni was king of the Swazi from 1875 until his death in 1889. During his reign he granted large numbers of concessions to white speculators and settlers, covering grazing and farming land, minerals, customs and even the right to run public services, in return for payments.

minos.s: Minos is a legendary king of Crete in Greek mythology, son of Zeus and Europa, said to have ruled from Knossos. Greek writers remembered him as a lawgiver and as the first ruler to command the sea.

minotaur.s: The Minotaur is a creature of Greek mythology with the head of a bull and the body of a man, born to Pasiphaë, the wife of King Minos of Crete, and a bull. Minos kept it in the Labyrinth at Knossos and fed it with young men and women sent from Athens, until Theseus killed it.

mindon-min.s: Mindon Min was king of Burma from 1853 to 1878, the second-last ruler of the Konbaung dynasty. He took the throne during the Second Anglo-Burmese War and sought to preserve the remaining kingdom through reform and diplomacy with the British.

manendragarh.s: Manendragarh is a town in northern Chhattisgarh, India, near the border with Madhya Pradesh, in the area of the former princely state of Korea, or Koriya. It grew with the development of the nearby coalfields and the railway in the 20th century, and since 2022 it has been the…

micronesia.s: Micronesia is a region of the western Pacific Ocean made up of thousands of small islands, including the Mariana, Caroline, Marshall and Gilbert Islands and Nauru. Its name, from the Greek for "small islands", came into use in the 19th century.

mashobra.s: Mashobra is a hill resort about 12 kilometres north-east of Shimla in Himachal Pradesh, India, set among forests of oak and pine at more than 2,000 metres. In the colonial period it lay among the small Simla Hill States and became a summer retreat for British officials.

makari.s: Makari is a town in the Far North Region of Cameroon, on the plains south of Lake Chad near the Nigerian border. One of the old Kotoko city-states, it was ringed by thick earthen walls and ruled by a sultan who paid tribute to Bornu, and it remains the seat of a traditional…

miyamoto-musashi.s: Miyamoto Musashi was a Japanese swordsman, strategist and artist, famed for fighting some sixty duels without defeat, including his contest with Sasaki Kojiro in 1612. He developed the two-sword style known as Niten Ichi-ryu.

mathura.s: Mathura is a city on the Yamuna in Uttar Pradesh, India, revered by Hindus as the birthplace of Krishna. In antiquity it was the capital of the Surasena kingdom, then a seat of the Indo-Scythian Northern Satraps and the southern capital of the Kushan Empire, when its workshops…

maresme.s: The Maresme is a comarca, or county, on the coast of Catalonia, Spain, north-east of Barcelona, with its capital at Mataró. It occupies a narrow strip between the sea and the coastal ranges, from Montgat to the mouth of the Tordera river.

mbum-people.s: The Mbum are a people of the Adamawa Plateau in northern Cameroon, with smaller groups in Chad and the Central African Republic, who speak an Adamawa language. Before the Fulani conquest in the early 19th century they held the area of Ngaoundéré.

mie-prefecture.s: Mie Prefecture is a prefecture of Japan in the Kinki region of central Honshu, on Ise Bay, with its capital at Tsu. It was formed in 1876 from the old provinces of Ise, Shima, Iga and part of Kii, after the abolition of the domains in 1871.

maki-izumi.s: Maki Izumi was a Shinto priest of the Suitengu shrine at Kurume and a leading imperial loyalist of the late Edo period. He promoted the restoration of direct imperial rule and the expulsion of foreigners, and allied himself with the radicals of the Choshu domain.

mandume-ya-ndemufayo.s: Mandume ya Ndemufayo was the last independent king of the Kwanyama, an Ovambo people living across the border of southern Angola and northern Namibia, reigning from 1911. He resisted Portuguese expansion, but after the Portuguese victory at Mongua in 1915 he withdrew into…

maranao-people.s: The Maranao are a Muslim people of the Philippines whose homeland is the region around Lake Lanao on Mindanao; their name means 'people of the lake'. They accepted Islam from the 16th century and organised themselves into many small sultanates that long resisted Spanish and…

marburg.s: Marburg is a university town on the Lahn river in Hesse, Germany. It grew around a castle of the landgraves of Thuringia and later of Hesse, and the Church of St Elizabeth, built over the tomb of Elizabeth of Hungary, made it a pilgrimage centre.

marburg-colloquy.s: The Marburg Colloquy was a meeting held at Marburg Castle in October 1529, called by Philip I of Hesse to unite the German and Swiss Reformers in a common Protestant alliance. Martin Luther, Philip Melanchthon, Huldrych Zwingli and Johannes Oecolampadius agreed on most…

mersa-gawasis.s: Mersa Gawasis is an archaeological site on the Red Sea coast of Egypt, south of Safaga, where a harbour was used by Middle Kingdom expeditions to Punt and other lands. Excavations since 2001 have found man-made caves with ship timbers, coiled ropes, cargo boxes and…

mahasenagupta.s: Mahasenagupta was a king of the Later Gupta dynasty of Magadha and Malwa in the late 6th century. The Aphsad inscription credits him with a victory over Susthitavarman of Kamarupa on the banks of the Lauhitya, the Brahmaputra.

madhavagupta.s: Madhavagupta was a prince of the Later Gupta dynasty, son of Mahasenagupta, who grew up at the Pushyabhuti court of Thanesar as a companion of the future emperor Harsha. He remained a close ally of Harsha and ruled in Magadha under his overlordship.

maravarman-sundara-pandya-i.s: Maravarman Sundara Pandya I was a king of the Later Pandya dynasty who began the revival of Pandya power in south India. Around 1219 he invaded the Chola kingdom, sacked Thanjavur and Uraiyur and forced the Chola king Kulottunga III to submit.

meurthe-et-moselle.s: Meurthe-et-Moselle is a department of north-eastern France in the Grand Est region, with its prefecture at Nancy. It was created in 1871 from the parts of the former Meurthe and Moselle departments that France kept after ceding Alsace and part of Lorraine to Germany at the end…

meuse.s: The Meuse (Dutch: Maas) is a river of western Europe, about 925 km long, which rises on the Langres plateau in north-eastern France and flows through Belgium and the Netherlands to the North Sea. Since Roman times it has been both a trade route and a frontier, and the Treaty…

marmarica.s: Marmarica is the ancient name for the coastal plateau and desert between the Nile Delta and Cyrenaica, in modern north-western Egypt and eastern Libya. It was home to Libyan pastoral peoples whom Greek and Roman writers called the Marmaridae.

meryey.s: Meryey, son of Did, was a chief of the Libu who around 1208 BCE led a coalition of Libyans and Sea Peoples, including the Ekwesh, Shekelesh, Lukka, Sherden and Teresh, into the western Nile Delta. The pharaoh Merneptah defeated them at Perire, as recorded at Karnak and on the…

manadeva-i.s: Manadeva I was a king of the Licchavi dynasty of Nepal, the first ruler of the Kathmandu Valley known from dated contemporary inscriptions. His pillar inscription of 464 CE at Changu Narayan records campaigns to the east and west that extended his kingdom.

marsala.s: Marsala is a port town at the western tip of Sicily. It stands on the site of Lilybaeum, founded by Carthage after the fall of Motya in 397 BCE, and its present name comes from the Arabic Marsa Allah or Marsa Ali, 'port of God' or 'port of Ali'.

miraflores-lima.s: Miraflores is a district of Lima, Peru, on cliffs above the Pacific, and one of the city's main residential, commercial and tourist areas. In January 1881, during the War of the Pacific, it was the site of the Battle of Miraflores, after which Chilean forces occupied Lima.

maselekwane-modjadji-i.s: Maselekwane Modjadji I was the first Rain Queen of the Lobedu people in what is now Limpopo, South Africa, coming to power around 1800. According to tradition she was a daughter of the king, and her accession began a line of queens believed to control the rain, to whom distant…

medma.s: Medma was an ancient Greek city on the Tyrrhenian coast of Calabria, southern Italy, at modern Rosarno. Founded by Locri Epizephyrii in the 6th century BCE, it was, with Hipponion, one of Locri's settlements on the western sea, and its sanctuaries have yielded many terracotta…

mirza-ghalib.s: Mirza Ghalib was the leading Urdu and Persian poet of the late Mughal era, best known for his ghazals. Born in Agra, he lived most of his life in Delhi, married into the family of the nawabs of Loharu, and served as poet to the last Mughal emperor, Bahadur Shah Zafar.

macdonnells-of-antrim.s: The MacDonnells of Antrim are a branch of Clan Donald of the Hebrides who settled the Glens of Antrim in north-east Ireland from the late 14th century, after a marriage with the Bissett heiress. In the 16th century, under leaders such as Sorley Boy MacDonnell, they fought the…

mount-carmel.s: Mount Carmel is a coastal mountain range in northern Israel, rising above the city of Haifa and the Mediterranean. Long held sacred, it is linked in the Hebrew Bible with the prophet Elijah.

maria-komnene-queen-of-jerusalem.s: Maria Komnene was a Byzantine princess, great-niece of Emperor Manuel I, who married King Amalric I of Jerusalem in 1167. She was the mother of Queen Isabella I of Jerusalem.

manx-language.s: Manx is a Goidelic Celtic language of the Isle of Man, closely related to Irish and Scottish Gaelic. Written from the early 17th century in a spelling based on English, it was the everyday language of most islanders until the 19th century, when English displaced it.

margaret-of-york.s: Margaret of York was a sister of the English kings Edward IV and Richard III who married Charles the Bold, Duke of Burgundy, in 1468. After his death she supported her stepdaughter Mary of Burgundy and her step-grandson Philip the Fair, and held court at Mechelen, where she…

matteo-i-visconti.s: Matteo I Visconti was lord of Milan and the real founder of the Visconti state. Great-nephew of Archbishop Ottone Visconti, he was named imperial vicar in 1294, was driven out by the della Torre in 1302 and returned with the support of Emperor Henry VII in 1311.

maria-de-molina.s: María de Molina was Queen of Castile as the wife of Sancho IV and twice served as regent. After Sancho's death in 1295 she defended the throne of her young son Ferdinand IV against rival claimants and rebellious nobles, and after Ferdinand's death in 1312 she was regent again…

montreal.s: Montreal is the largest city of Quebec, Canada, on an island in the St Lawrence River. Founded as Ville-Marie in 1642 by French Catholic settlers, it became the centre of the New France fur trade and surrendered to the British in 1760.

malbork-castle.s: Malbork Castle, German Marienburg, is a vast brick fortress on the Nogat river in northern Poland, built by the Teutonic Order from the late 13th century. From 1309 it was the seat of the Grand Master and capital of the Order's state in Prussia.

mirabel-castle.s: Mirabel was a crusader castle on the edge of the coastal plain east of Jaffa, at the site now known as Migdal Afek in Israel. Built in the 12th century near the springs of the Yarkon river, it guarded the road from Jaffa to Jerusalem and was associated with the lordship of…

mauren.s: Mauren is a municipality in the Unterland of Liechtenstein, near the Austrian border. A farming village for most of its history, it belonged to the Lordship of Schellenberg, which the princes of Liechtenstein bought in 1699 and united with the County of Vaduz in 1719 to form…

mykonos.s: Mykonos is a small island of the Cyclades in the Aegean Sea, Greece. After the Fourth Crusade it was taken around 1207 by the Venetian Ghisi family and later passed to Venice, before falling to the Ottomans in 1537 during the raids of Hayreddin Barbarossa.

malchow.s: Malchow is a small town in Mecklenburg, north-eastern Germany, built partly on an island in the Malchower See in the Mecklenburg Lake District. It received town rights in 1235 under the lords of Werle, and a Cistercian nunnery established there in the late 13th century later…

merneptah.s: Merneptah was the fourth king of the 19th Dynasty of Egypt, son and successor of Ramesses II. In his fifth year he defeated a Libyan invasion, joined by contingents of the Sea Peoples, at Perire in the western Delta.

merida-spain.s: Mérida is a city on the Guadiana river in western Spain, capital of the autonomous community of Extremadura. Founded in 25 BCE as Emerita Augusta for veterans of Augustus' wars, it became the capital of Lusitania and keeps one of the largest groups of Roman monuments in Spain.

merida-yucatan.s: Mérida is the capital of the Mexican state of Yucatán. Francisco de Montejo the Younger founded it in 1542 on the site of the Maya city of T'hó, reusing stone from its pyramids.

myra.s: Myra was a city of ancient Lycia, near modern Demre in southern Turkey, and one of the six largest members of the Lycian League. It is known for its rock-cut tombs and Roman theatre, and in the 4th century its bishop was Saint Nicholas, whose church still stands there.

ma-xiguang.s: Ma Xiguang was ruler of Chu, a Ten Kingdoms state in Hunan, from 947 to 950. A son of the founder Ma Yin, he was chosen over his elder brother Ma Xi'e, who rebelled with support from the Southern Tang.

ma-xie.s: Ma Xi'e was ruler of Chu, a Ten Kingdoms state in Hunan, from 950 to 951. An elder son of the founder Ma Yin, he was passed over in favour of his brother Ma Xiguang in 947, rebelled from Langzhou and seized Changsha at the end of 950.

meenakshi-of-madurai.s: Meenakshi was the last ruler of the Madurai Nayak dynasty, governing as queen from the early 1730s after the death of her husband Vijaya Ranga Chokkanatha. Disputes over the succession drew in the Nawab of the Carnatic, whose officer Chanda Sahib seized Tiruchirappalli and…

meenakshi-temple.s: The Meenakshi Temple (Meenakshi Amman Temple) is a Hindu temple complex in the centre of Madurai, Tamil Nadu, dedicated to the goddess Meenakshi and her consort Sundareswarar, a form of Shiva. Its present buildings, with fourteen towering painted gopurams, were largely rebuilt…

madhura-vijayam.s: Madhura Vijayam ('The Conquest of Madurai') is a Sanskrit poem written in the 14th century by Gangadevi, wife of the Vijayanagara prince Kumara Kampana. It recounts his campaigns in the Tamil country, his defeat of the Sambuvaraya rulers and the overthrow of the Madurai…

mabar.s: Ma'bar ('the crossing') was the name Arab and Persian writers gave to the Coromandel Coast of south-eastern India, especially the Pandya lands around Madurai. Marco Polo visited it in the late 13th century and described its pearl fishery.

myot-hill.s: Myot Hill is a small hill near Denny, south of Stirling in central Scotland, crowned by the remains of a hillfort. Like Dumyat, its name is thought to derive from the Maeatae, a people of the Forth valley who fought the Romans in the late 2nd and early 3rd centuries.

macedonia-region.s: Macedonia is a historical region of the central Balkans, centred on the Vardar and Aliakmon valleys and the plain around Thessaloniki. It takes its name from the ancient kingdom of Macedon and later formed a Roman province, a contested borderland between Byzantium, Bulgaria…

maka-satrapy.s: Maka was a province of the Achaemenid Persian Empire, listed in inscriptions of Darius I from the late 6th century BCE and usually located on both shores of the Strait of Hormuz, in modern Oman and the Makran coast of Iran. Its name is thought to continue the ancient Magan of…

manium.s: Manium was a ruler of Magan, the copper land of south-eastern Arabia, known only from inscriptions of Naram-Sin of Akkad, who reigned in the 23rd century BCE. Naram-Sin claimed to have defeated him, quarried diorite in his mountains and carried it back to Mesopotamia to make…

menarandra-river.s: The Menarandra is a river of southern Madagascar, flowing south-west across the arid plateau to the sea. It roughly marked the boundary between the Mahafaly to the west and the Antandroy to the east, and the Mahafaly kingdoms of the 17th to 19th centuries lay between it and…

mehri-language.s: Mehri is a Modern South Arabian language spoken by the Mahra people of eastern Yemen and western Oman, and by migrants in the Gulf states. It is a Semitic language but not a form of Arabic, being descended from languages spoken in southern Arabia before the spread of Arabic.

mindoro.s: Mindoro is the seventh-largest island of the Philippines, lying south-west of Luzon across the Verde Island Passage. Many scholars identify it with Ma-i, a trading country that Chinese records describe from the 10th century, and its coasts traded with Chinese merchants long…

majeerteen.s: The Majeerteen are a Somali clan of the Darod family, living mainly in the north-east of Somalia, in Puntland. In the 18th and 19th centuries their leaders ruled the Majeerteen Sultanate and the Sultanate of Hobyo, which accepted Italian protection and were conquered by Italy…

muzaffar-shah-of-malacca.s: Muzaffar Shah was sultan of Malacca from about 1445 to 1459, the first of its rulers to use the title sultan. He made Islam the state religion, and with his bendahara Tun Perak he repelled Siamese attacks and extended Malacca's power over the Malay Peninsula.

muzaffar-shah-i-of-perak.s: Muzaffar Shah I was the first sultan of Perak, reigning from about 1528 to 1549. The eldest son of Mahmud Shah, the last sultan of Malacca, he was passed over for the succession in Johor and invited to rule Perak, founding the dynasty that still reigns there.

mahathir-mohamad.s: Mahathir Mohamad is a Malaysian politician who was prime minister from 1981 to 2003 and again from 2018 to 2020. His first long tenure brought rapid industrialisation and large infrastructure projects, but also curbs on the judiciary and the rulers' powers and the jailing of…

malerkotla.s: Malerkotla is a town in Punjab, India, the seat of the former princely state of the same name ruled by Afghan nawabs. It is the only Muslim-majority town in Indian Punjab, a status linked to the tradition that its nawab Sher Muhammad Khan protested in 1705 against the…

mahavira.s: Mahavira, born Vardhamana, was the 24th and last tirthankara of Jainism, a contemporary of the Buddha in the 6th or 5th century BCE. Born into a ruling clan near Vaishali in Bihar, he renounced his household at about thirty and, after years of austerity, taught a path of…

mandu.s: Mandu is a ruined fortress city on a plateau of the Vindhya range in Madhya Pradesh, India. The sultans of Malwa made it their capital from the early 15th century and adorned it with palaces, mosques and tombs, including Hoshang Shah's marble tomb, the Jahaz Mahal and the Jama…

mam-people.s: The Mam are a Maya people of the western highlands of Guatemala, mainly in Huehuetenango and San Marcos, and of neighbouring Chiapas in Mexico. Before the Spanish conquest their kingdom had its capital at Zaculeu, which fell to Gonzalo de Alvarado in 1525.

mamprusi.s: The Mamprusi are a people of northern Ghana and northern Togo who speak Mampruli, a Gur language of the Mole-Dagbani group. Their kingdom, Mamprugu, ruled by the Nayiri from Nalerigu, is regarded as the senior of the related Mole-Dagbani states, including Dagbon and the Mossi…

mole-dagbani.s: The Mole-Dagbani are a group of related peoples of northern Ghana and Burkina Faso, including the Mamprusi, Dagomba, Nanumba and Mossi, who speak closely related Gur languages. Their traditions trace their ruling houses to the chief Na Gbewaa and his descendants, who from…

mamun-academy.s: The Ma'mun Academy was a circle of scholars gathered at Gurganj, capital of Khwarazm, by the Ma'munid Khwarazmshahs Ali and Ma'mun II in the early 11th century. Its members included al-Biruni, Ibn Sina, the mathematician Abu Nasr Mansur and the physician Abu Sahl al-Masihi.

manavadar.s: Manavadar is a town in Junagadh district of Gujarat, India. It was the capital of a small princely state ruled by a branch of the Babi family, the Pathan dynasty of Junagadh, under the Kathiawar Agency.

mora-cameroon.s: Mora is a town in the Far North Region of Cameroon, near the border with Nigeria at the foot of the Mandara Mountains. It became the capital of the Mandara (Wandala) kingdom in its later history, and the sultan of Mandara still resides there as a traditional ruler.

military-industrial-complex.s: The military-industrial complex is the network of armed forces, arms manufacturers and political interests that grows up around a permanent defence establishment. The term was popularised by President Dwight D.

march-on-washington.s: The March on Washington for Jobs and Freedom, held on 28 August 1963, was one of the largest political demonstrations in American history: some 250,000 people gathered at the Lincoln Memorial to demand civil and economic rights for African Americans. Organised by a coalition…

muhammad.s: Muhammad was the prophet of Islam, born in Mecca around 570 and active as a merchant before, according to Islamic tradition, receiving the revelations gathered in the Quran from about 610. Persecution drove him and his followers to Medina in 622, the hijra from which the…

munza.s: Munza was a king of the Mangbetu in the Uele region of north-eastern Congo. The German explorer Georg Schweinfurth visited his court in 1870 and described its great hall, music, ironwork and ivory in vivid detail.

mangkunegara-i.s: Mangkunegara I, born Raden Mas Said and known as Pangeran Sambernyawa, was a Javanese prince of the house of Mataram who fought the Dutch East India Company and the royal courts for about sixteen years. By the Treaty of Salatiga in 1757 he received an apanage in Surakarta and…

manabi-province.s: Manabí is a province on the central Pacific coast of Ecuador, with Portoviejo as its capital and Manta as its main port. It was the heartland of the Manteño culture before the Spanish conquest, and it is known for fishing, farming and the weaving of toquilla straw hats.

manta-ecuador.s: Manta is a port city in Manabí province on the Pacific coast of Ecuador. Near the site of the Manteño port of Jocay, it is now one of the main tuna-fishing and canning centres in the world.

marajo.s: Marajó is a large island in the mouth of the Amazon river, in the state of Pará, Brazil, covering about 40,000 square kilometres of savanna, swamp and forest. Between about 400 and 1400 CE it was home to the Marajoara culture, which built large earthen mounds and made…

merseburg.s: Merseburg is a town on the Saale river in Saxony-Anhalt, Germany. It was a royal palace of the Ottonian kings, and Otto I founded a bishopric there in 968; Bishop Thietmar wrote his famous chronicle there, and the cathedral library holds the Merseburg Charms.

mieszko-i.s: Mieszko I was the first historically documented ruler of Poland, of the Piast dynasty, ruling from around 960 until 992. He married the Bohemian princess Dobrawa and was baptised in 966, an event seen as the beginning of Polish Christianity.

montferrat.s: Montferrat (Monferrato) is a hilly region of southern Piedmont, Italy, between the Po and the Ligurian Apennines. It was ruled by the Aleramici and then the Palaiologos marquises, passed to the Gonzaga of Mantua in 1536 and went to Savoy in the early 18th century.

mont-cenis.s: Mont Cenis is a pass at about 2,080 metres in the western Alps, linking the Maurienne valley in Savoy with the Susa valley in Piedmont. It was one of the main routes between France and Italy in the Middle Ages, controlled by the margraves of Turin and later the house of Savoy.

melk.s: Melk is a town on the Danube in Lower Austria, at the western end of the Wachau valley. Its castle was an early residence of the Babenberg margraves, who gave it to Benedictine monks in 1089.

mindel.s: The Mindel is a river in Bavarian Swabia, southern Germany, flowing north from the Alpine foothills to join the Danube near Gundremmingen. It gave its name to the Mindel glaciation, one of the Ice Age cold stages defined by Albrecht Penck and Eduard Brückner.

markgraflerland.s: The Markgräflerland is a region in the far south-west of Baden-Württemberg, Germany, between Freiburg and Basel and the Rhine and the Black Forest. Its name, 'margraves' land', recalls the lordships held there by the margraves of Hachberg-Sausenberg and Baden.

mur-river.s: The Mur (Mura) is a river about 450 kilometres long in central Europe. It rises in the Hohe Tauern in Austria, flows east through Styria past Graz, and then forms parts of the borders of Slovenia, Croatia and Hungary before joining the Drava.

milceni.s: The Milceni were a West Slavic tribe living around Bautzen in what is now Upper Lusatia, in eastern Germany. Their land, called Milsko, was conquered by the Germans in the 10th century and later contested between Poland, Meissen and Bohemia.

meknes.s: Meknes is a city in northern Morocco, founded as a Berber settlement in the 10th century. Sultan Moulay Ismail made it his capital from 1672 to 1727 and built a vast imperial city of palaces, granaries, stables and walls, entered through gates such as Bab Mansour.

marruvium.s: Marruvium was the chief town of the Marsi, on the eastern shore of the Fucine Lake in central Italy, at modern San Benedetto dei Marsi. After the Social War it became a Roman municipium.

mayyafariqin.s: Mayyafariqin, the Byzantine Martyropolis and modern Silvan in Diyarbakır province, Turkey, is a town in the upper Tigris basin. It was the capital of the Kurdish Marwanid dynasty in the 10th and 11th centuries, and later held by the Artuqids and the Ayyubids.

maseko-ngoni.s: The Maseko Ngoni are a branch of the Ngoni people whose ancestors left the Zulu region of south-eastern Africa in the 1820s during the upheavals of the Mfecane. Under Ngwana and then Mputa they crossed the Zambezi and moved as far north as southern Tanzania before turning…

mputa.s: Mputa, also called Mputa Maseko, was a leader of the Maseko Ngoni in the mid-nineteenth century. He led his people north to the Songea area of southern Tanzania, where they lived for some years before being defeated by rival Ngoni groups and driven south again.

mount-damavand.s: Mount Damavand is a dormant volcano in the Alborz range of northern Iran, about 5,610 metres high and the highest peak in Iran. It features widely in Persian myth and poetry: in the Shahnameh the tyrant Zahhak is chained in a cave on the mountain.

massachusetts-bay-company.s: The Massachusetts Bay Company was an English joint-stock company chartered by Charles I in 1629 to settle and trade in New England. Its Puritan leaders, headed by John Winthrop, took the charter with them to America in 1630, turning the company into the government of the…

massina.s: Massina, or Macina, is a region of the inner Niger delta in central Mali, a seasonally flooded plain around Mopti and Djenné. Long home to Fulbe herders as well as farmers and fishermen, it was ruled by Fulbe ardo chiefs under Bambara overlords until Seku Amadu's jihad of 1818…

mastia.s: Mastia was an Iberian town in south-eastern Spain, chief town of the Mastieni. It appears as Mastia Tarseion in the second treaty between Rome and Carthage, of 348 BCE, recorded by Polybius, marking the limit beyond which Romans might not trade or found cities.

mwembe.s: Mwembe was the town of the Yao chiefs called Mataka on the highlands east of Lake Malawi, in what is now Niassa province of northern Mozambique. It grew in the nineteenth century as the centre of a powerful chiefdom that traded slaves and ivory to the coast.

matsue.s: Matsue is a city in western Japan and the capital of Shimane Prefecture, between Lake Shinji and Lake Nakaumi. It grew up as a castle town after Horio Yoshiharu built Matsue Castle, completed in 1611, and was the seat of the Matsue domain, ruled by a branch of the Matsudaira…

matsumae-castle.s: Matsumae Castle, also called Fukuyama Castle, stands in the town of Matsumae in southern Hokkaido, Japan. Completed in 1854 to strengthen coastal defence, it was the last Japanese castle built in the traditional style.

matsumae-yoshihiro.s: Matsumae Yoshihiro was a Japanese lord of the Kakizaki family, which controlled southern Hokkaido, then called Ezo. Taking the family name Matsumae, he received a charter from Tokugawa Ieyasu in 1604 granting him the exclusive right to trade with the Ainu, which became the…

menashi-kunashir-rebellion.s: The Menashi–Kunashir rebellion was an uprising of the Ainu of Kunashir Island and the Menashi district of eastern Hokkaido in 1789. Provoked by harsh treatment from Japanese merchants running fisheries under the Matsumae domain, the Ainu killed about seventy Japanese.

mauretania-sitifensis.s: Mauretania Sitifensis was a Roman province in north-eastern Algeria, created under Diocletian around 300 CE by dividing off the eastern part of Mauretania Caesariensis. Its capital was Sitifis, modern Sétif, in a rich grain-growing upland.

mijikenda.s: The Mijikenda, meaning nine towns, are a group of nine related Bantu-speaking peoples of the Kenyan coastal hinterland, from the Tanzanian border north towards Malindi. Living traditionally in fortified hilltop villages called kaya, they traded ivory, grain and other produce…

muhammad-i-tapar.s: Muhammad I Tapar was sultan of the Seljuk Empire from 1105 to 1118, son of Malik-Shah I. After years of civil war with his brother Berkyaruq he ruled the western Seljuk lands from Isfahan, campaigning against the Nizari Ismailis and against Arab emirs in Iraq.

mount-merapi.s: Mount Merapi is an active volcano in Central Java, Indonesia, north of Yogyakarta, and one of the most active in the world. Its ash made the surrounding plains fertile and supported early Javanese kingdoms such as Medang, whose court moved to East Java in 929, possibly after…

media-region.s: Media was an ancient region of north-western Iran, centred on the Zagros mountains and the city of Ecbatana, modern Hamadan. Home of the Medes, it was the core of the Median kingdom of the seventh and sixth centuries BCE and then a rich satrapy of the Achaemenid Empire.

metz.s: Metz is a city in Lorraine, north-eastern France, where the Seille joins the Moselle. It began as Divodurum, the main town of the Mediomatrici, and under Rome was an important road junction later called Mettis after the people.

moselle.s: The Moselle is a river of north-eastern France, Luxembourg and western Germany, about 545 kilometres long. Rising in the Vosges, it flows past Metz, forms part of the border between Luxembourg and Germany and joins the Rhine at Koblenz.

mareb-river.s: The Mareb is a river of north-eastern Africa that rises in the Eritrean highlands south of Asmara, forms part of the border between Eritrea and Ethiopia and continues west into Sudan as the Gash, ending in an inland delta near Kassala. The lands north of it were long known as…

maurienne.s: The Maurienne is the valley of the Arc river in Savoy, south-eastern France, running from the Alpine passes near Mont Cenis down to the Isère. In antiquity it was home to the Medulli.

megarid.s: The Megarid was the small territory of the ancient Greek city of Megara, on the isthmus between Attica and the Corinthia. Its limited plain and the Geraneia mountains lay on the land route between central Greece and the Peloponnese, which made it a frequent battleground…

minangkabau-people.s: The Minangkabau are an Austronesian people of the highlands of West Sumatra, Indonesia, known for their matrilineal society, in which land and houses pass through the female line. Their highlands were a source of gold for the ports of the Strait of Malacca and the seat of the…

muaro-jambi.s: Muara Jambi is a large Buddhist temple complex on the Batang Hari river east of the city of Jambi in Sumatra, Indonesia, built mainly between the seventh and thirteenth centuries. Its brick temples, ponds and canals, spread over several square kilometres, make it one of the…

meaux.s: Meaux is a town on the Marne east of Paris, in the Île-de-France region of France. It began as Iatinum, the chief town of the Gallic Meldi, and became a bishopric in late antiquity.

melik-shahnazar-ii.s: Melik Shahnazar II was the Armenian melik of Varanda, one of the five melikdoms of Karabakh, in the mid-eighteenth century. In conflict with the other meliks, he allied with Panah Ali Khan, founder of the Karabakh Khanate, and helped him build the fortress of Shusha in the…

mystras.s: Mystras is a ruined medieval town on a spur of Mount Taygetus near Sparta in the Peloponnese, Greece. William II of Villehardouin built a castle there in 1249; ceded to Byzantium in 1262, it became the capital of the Despotate of the Morea and a centre of late Byzantine art…

mount-taygetus.s: Mount Taygetus is a mountain range in the southern Peloponnese, Greece, rising to about 2,400 metres and separating Laconia from Messenia. Ancient Sparta lay at its eastern foot, and the Spartan conquest of Messenia across the range shaped the city's history.

melian-dialogue.s: The Melian Dialogue is a passage in Thucydides' History of the Peloponnesian War recounting negotiations between Athenian envoys and the leaders of Melos in 416 BCE. The Athenians argue that the strong do what they can and the weak suffer what they must, while the Melians…

mangoky-river.s: The Mangoky is a river in south-western Madagascar, one of the longest on the island at over 500 kilometres. It rises in the central highlands and flows west to a delta on the Mozambique Channel.

maroserana-dynasty.s: The Maroserana were a royal dynasty of south-western Madagascar that rose in the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries. Its branches founded the Sakalava kingdoms of Menabe and Boina on the west coast, and related lines ruled the Mahafaly kingdoms of the south-west.

makhzan-al-asrar.s: Makhzan al-Asrar, The Treasury of Mysteries, is the first of the five long poems of the Persian poet Nizami Ganjavi, written in the 1160s or 1170s. A didactic work of about 2,250 couplets, it mixes moral and religious discourses with short illustrative stories.

milas.s: Milas is a town in Muğla province, south-western Turkey, on the site of ancient Mylasa, the capital of Caria under the Hecatomnid dynasty. In the late thirteenth century it was taken by Turkmen raiders and became a chief town of the Menteshe beylik, whose rulers built mosques…

mendes.s: Mendes was an ancient Egyptian city in the north-eastern Nile Delta, at present-day Tell el-Ruba. It was the cult centre of a ram god, the Ram of Mendes, and of the fish goddess Hatmehit.

manduria.s: Manduria is a town in the province of Taranto in Apulia, southern Italy. In antiquity it was a Messapian town with massive triple walls, and in 338 BCE the Spartan king Archidamus III, fighting for Taras, was killed in battle beneath them.

messapic-language.s: Messapic was an extinct Indo-European language of the Messapians of south-eastern Italy, in the Salento peninsula of Apulia. It is known from several hundred inscriptions written in an alphabet adapted from the Greek alphabet of Taras, dating mainly from the sixth to the first…

mount-ithome.s: Mount Ithome is a mountain of about 800 metres in Messenia, in the south-western Peloponnese of Greece. The Messenians used it as a fortress in their wars against Sparta, and after the great earthquake of about 464 BCE rebellious helots held out on it for years.

molyvos.s: Molyvos, officially Mithymna, is a small town on the northern coast of the Greek island of Lesbos, on the site of the ancient city of Methymna. Built on a hillside below a medieval castle that was held by the Genoese Gattilusi lords and then by the Ottomans, it is known for…

morena-political-party.s: Morena, the National Regeneration Movement, is a left-wing Mexican political party founded by Andrés Manuel López Obrador, first as a movement in 2011 and then as a registered party in 2014. It won the presidency, with López Obrador, and a majority in Congress in 2018, ending…

mikhail-speransky.s: Mikhail Speransky was a Russian statesman and reformer, the leading adviser of Emperor Alexander I until his fall and exile in 1812. As governor-general of Siberia from 1819 to 1821 he drew up the Siberian reforms of 1822, which among other things abolished the khanship of the…

miknasa.s: The Miknasa were a Berber tribal group of medieval North Africa. Sufri Kharijites among them founded Sijilmasa in the Tafilalt oasis in 757, and the Midrarid emirs who ruled it came from their ranks.

movses-kaghankatvatsi.s: Movses Kaghankatvatsi is the name traditionally given to the author of the History of the Country of Albania, the main narrative source for Caucasian Albania. Written in Armenian, the work was probably compiled in the 10th century from older material, and its authorship,…

mirambo.s: Mirambo was a Nyamwezi ruler in present-day western Tanzania who built a powerful state, known as Urambo, in the 1870s. The son of a minor chief, he formed an army of ruga-ruga warriors armed with guns and conquered neighbouring chiefdoms west of Tabora.

matsunaga-hisahide.s: Matsunaga Hisahide was a Japanese warlord of the Sengoku period who rose in the service of Miyoshi Nagayoshi to become one of the most powerful men in the Kinai. After Nagayoshi's death he fought the Miyoshi elders, and troops under his son took part in killing the shogun…

miyoshi-yoshitsugu.s: Miyoshi Yoshitsugu was the adopted heir of Miyoshi Nagayoshi and head of the Miyoshi clan after 1564. Dominated by the three Miyoshi elders and Matsunaga Hisahide, he was involved in the killing of the shogun Ashikaga Yoshiteru in 1565.

mesha.s: Mesha was king of Moab in the 9th century BCE, known from the Hebrew Bible and his own inscription, the Mesha Stele. The son of Chemosh-yatti, he ruled from Dibon and threw off the domination of the Kingdom of Israel after the reign of Ahab, recovering territory north of the…

mesha-stele.s: The Mesha Stele, or Moabite Stone, is a basalt slab inscribed around 840 BCE for King Mesha of Moab, found at Dhiban in Jordan in 1868 and now in the Louvre. Its text, in the Moabite language and alphabet, celebrates Mesha's revolt against the Kingdom of Israel, founded by…

mohawk-river.s: The Mohawk River is a river of New York State that flows east for about 240 kilometres to join the Hudson north of Albany. Its valley, the homeland of the Mohawk nation, was the only low-level route through the Appalachians and a main path of trade and war between the Great…

molly-brant.s: Molly Brant was a Mohawk leader of the 18th century, the consort of the British Indian superintendent Sir William Johnson and the elder sister of Joseph Brant. A respected clan matron, she used her influence to keep the Mohawk and much of the Iroquois Confederacy loyal to…

mogok.s: Mogok is a town in the hills of the Mandalay Region of Myanmar, north-east of Mandalay, famous for centuries as the world's main source of fine rubies, including the deep red 'pigeon's blood' stones, as well as sapphires and other gems. The mines were long controlled by…

mixtecs.s: The Mixtecs, who call themselves Ñuu Savi, 'people of the rain', are an indigenous people of western Oaxaca and neighbouring parts of Guerrero and Puebla in Mexico. Before the Spanish conquest they lived in many small kingdoms such as Tilantongo and Tututepec, whose histories…

morioka.s: Morioka is the capital of Iwate Prefecture in northern Honshu, Japan. It grew up as the castle town of the Nanbu clan, who moved their seat there at the end of the 16th century and built Morioka Castle in stages over several decades, and it was the centre of the Morioka domain…

mount-athos.s: Mount Athos is a mountain and peninsula in northern Greece, the easternmost of the three prongs of Chalcidice, and the site of an Orthodox monastic community governed as a self-administering part of Greece. Hermits lived there from at least the 9th century, and the first large…

miskito.s: The Miskito are an indigenous people of the Caribbean coast of Nicaragua and Honduras, whose ancestry mixes Amerindian, African and European origins. From the 17th century they allied with English traders and buccaneers, obtaining firearms that let them dominate neighbouring…

motya-charioteer.s: The Motya Charioteer is a marble statue of a young man in a long, finely pleated tunic, found in 1979 on the island of Motya off western Sicily. Carved by a Greek sculptor in about 470 to 450 BCE, it is one of the finest surviving works of the early Classical style.

mountain-autonomous-soviet-socialist-rep.s: The Mountain Autonomous Soviet Socialist Republic was an autonomous republic of the Russian SFSR in the North Caucasus, created in January 1921 with its capital at Vladikavkaz. It united Chechen, Ingush, Ossetian, Kabardian, Balkar and Karachay districts.

maronites.s: The Maronites are Eastern Catholic Christians of the Syriac tradition, named after the 5th-century monk Saint Maron and centred on Mount Lebanon. Their church entered full communion with Rome in the Crusader period.

mutare.s: Mutare, called Umtali until 1982, is a city in eastern Zimbabwe near the border with Mozambique. Founded in the 1890s and moved to its present site to meet the railway from Beira, which reached it in 1898, it became the gateway between the Rhodesian interior and the coast.

mtamvuna-river.s: The Mtamvuna is a river of South Africa that flows into the Indian Ocean and forms part of the boundary between the provinces of KwaZulu-Natal and the Eastern Cape. In the 19th century it marked the north-eastern edge of Pondoland, separating the Mpondo kingdom from Natal.

mthatha-river.s: The Mthatha is a river of the Eastern Cape in South Africa, flowing south-east past the city of Mthatha into the Indian Ocean. It long formed the south-western boundary of the lands of the Mpondo, separating them from the Thembu and Xhosa peoples.

mfengu.s: The Mfengu are a Xhosa-speaking people of the Eastern Cape in South Africa, formed largely from refugees who fled into Xhosa lands from the wars of the 1820s in Natal. Many allied with the Cape Colony, which settled them on land taken from the Xhosa from 1835 and used them as…
