mayflower-compact.s: The Mayflower Compact was an agreement signed by 41 men aboard the Mayflower off Cape Cod on 11 November 1620 (Old Style), before the settlers went ashore. Lacking a valid patent for New England, they bound themselves into a 'civil body politic' to make just laws for the…

mandor-affair.s: The Mandor affair was a series of mass killings carried out by the Japanese occupation forces in West Kalimantan in 1943 and 1944. Claiming to have uncovered a plot, the Japanese arrested and executed many of the region's leaders, including the sultan of Pontianak, Syarif…

mempawah.s: Mempawah is a coastal town in West Kalimantan, Indonesia, north of Pontianak, and the seat of a regency of the same name. It was the centre of a Malay sultanate linked by marriage to Bugis and Arab families.

mpla.n: People's Movement for the Liberation of Angola
mpla.s: The People's Movement for the Liberation of Angola (MPLA) is an Angolan political party founded in the 1950s, which fought Portuguese rule from 1961 under Agostinho Neto. Backed by the Soviet Union and Cuban troops, it took Luanda and declared Angola's independence in November…

maputo.s: Maputo, known until 1976 as Lourenço Marques, is the capital and largest city of Mozambique, on Delagoa Bay in the far south of the country. A Portuguese trading post grew into a town that replaced Mozambique Island as the colonial capital in 1898, helped by the railway to the…

maelor.s: Maelor was a medieval district of north-east Wales, divided into Maelor Gymraeg, or Welsh Maelor, around Wrexham and Maelor Saesneg, or English Maelor, east of the Dee. It formed part of Powys Fadog, whose prince Gruffydd Maelor took his name from it.

mandore.s: Mandore, anciently Mandavyapura, is a historic town a few kilometres north of Jodhpur in Rajasthan, India. It was the seat of the Pratiharas of Mandavyapura from about the 6th century and was taken by the Rathores around 1400 as their capital, until Rao Jodha founded Jodhpur…

markus-sittikus-von-hohenems.s: Markus Sittikus von Hohenems was prince-archbishop of Salzburg from 1612 to 1619. He continued the rebuilding of Salzburg in Italian style begun by Wolf Dietrich von Raitenau, starting the new cathedral designed by Santino Solari and building the palace and trick fountains of…

moutier-grandval-abbey.s: Moutier-Grandval Abbey was a monastery founded around 640 at Moutier in the Jura mountains of modern Switzerland. In 999 King Rudolf III of Burgundy gave it to the bishop of Basel, forming the core of the prince-bishopric's lands in the Jura.

magdeburg.s: Magdeburg is a city on the Elbe and the capital of Saxony-Anhalt, Germany. Otto I made it a centre of his rule and raised it to an archbishopric in 968, and its town law, Magdeburg law, was adopted by hundreds of towns across central and eastern Europe.

meersburg.s: Meersburg is a small town on the north shore of Lake Constance in Baden-Württemberg, Germany. After the city of Constance adopted the Reformation in the 1520s, the prince-bishops of Constance moved their residence there, later building a baroque New Palace beside the medieval…

merseburg-charms.s: The Merseburg Charms are two magic spells in Old High German, written down in the 9th or 10th century in a manuscript of the cathedral library of Merseburg. One frees captives, the other heals a horse's injured foot by invoking the gods Wodan, Frija and others.

marsal.s: Marsal is a village in the Seille valley in Lorraine, north-eastern France. Its salt springs were worked from prehistoric times, and in the Middle Ages they brought revenue to the bishops of Metz.

meinwerk.s: Meinwerk was bishop of Paderborn from 1009 to 1036, a Saxon noble and kinsman of Emperor Henry II. Using his family wealth and imperial grants, he rebuilt the cathedral, founded the Abdinghof monastery and built the Bartholomew Chapel, making Paderborn a major ecclesiastical…

matthaus-schiner.s: Matthäus Schiner was a Swiss cardinal and statesman, bishop of Sion from 1499. An ally of Pope Julius II against France, he raised Swiss troops for the Holy League and led them in the Italian Wars until their defeat at Marignano in 1515.

mahajirstvo.s: The Mahajirstvo is the name given to the mass emigration and deportation of Muslim peoples of the north-western Caucasus, including the Abkhaz and Circassians, to the Ottoman Empire after the Russian conquest. In Abkhazia it followed the abolition of the principality in 1864…

monemvasia.s: Monemvasia is a fortified town on a rocky island off the south-eastern coast of the Peloponnese, joined to the mainland by a causeway. Founded in the 6th century, it was a strong Byzantine port that fell to William II of Villehardouin in 1248 and was returned to Byzantium in…

mat-river.s: The Mat is a river in north-central Albania, about 115 kilometres long, flowing west through a mountainous valley to the Adriatic north of Lezhë. The surrounding district, also called Mat, was a stronghold of clans and noble families such as the Kastrioti in the late Middle Ages.

muzaka-family.s: The Muzaka were an Albanian noble family of the Myzeqe plain and Berat. In the 14th century Andrea II Muzaka received the Byzantine title of despot, and the family ruled Berat until the Ottoman conquest of 1417.

monastery-of-saint-john-vladimir.s: The Monastery of Saint John Vladimir (Shën Gjon Vladimir) is an Orthodox monastery near Elbasan in central Albania. It was built in 1381 by Karl Thopia, ruler of the Principality of Albania, and dedicated to Jovan Vladimir, an 11th-century prince of Duklja venerated as a…

mulde.s: The Mulde is a river in eastern Germany, formed by the junction of the Zwickauer Mulde and the Freiberger Mulde in Saxony. It flows north through Saxony and Saxony-Anhalt, past Grimma and Eilenburg, and joins the Elbe at Dessau.

myzeqe.s: Myzeqe is the largest plain of Albania, along the Adriatic coast in the south-west of the country between the Shkumbin and Vjosa rivers, around Fier and Lushnjë. Once largely marshland, it was the base of the medieval Muzaka family, whose name it is thought to share.

maximilien-de-bethune-duke-of-sully.n: Maximilien de Béthune, Duke of Sully
maximilien-de-bethune-duke-of-sully.s: Maximilien de Béthune, Duke of Sully, was the chief minister of Henry IV of France. A Protestant who had fought beside Henry in the Wars of Religion, he became superintendent of finances in 1598 and restored the royal treasury, repaid debts, and built roads, canals and…

mamia-v-gurieli.s: Mamia V Gurieli was Prince of Guria in western Georgia from 1797 until his death in 1826. Caught between the Kingdom of Imereti, the Ottoman Empire and advancing Russia, he accepted a Russian protectorate in 1810 while keeping control of internal affairs.

mamia-iii-gurieli.s: Mamia III Gurieli was Prince of Guria in western Georgia from 1689 until his death in 1714. Taking advantage of the dynastic wars of the neighbouring Kingdom of Imereti, he seized its throne several times between 1701 and 1713.

malka-river.s: The Malka is a river of the North Caucasus in Russia, about 216 km long, rising on the northern slopes of Mount Elbrus and flowing east and north-east through Kabardino-Balkaria to join the Terek near Prokhladny. Its valley and that of its tributary the Baksan formed the…

mstislav-i-of-kiev.s: Mstislav I, called the Great, was Grand Prince of Kiev from 1125 to 1132, the eldest son of Vladimir Monomakh and Gytha of Wessex. Long prince of Novgorod before that, he kept the princes of Rus' under Kiev's authority and campaigned against the Cumans, Polotsk and the Chuds.

mindelheim.s: Mindelheim is a town in Swabia, Bavaria, on the Mindel river. It belonged to the Frundsberg family, whose best-known member, the mercenary commander Georg von Frundsberg, was born there, and later to Bavaria.

maramures.s: Maramureș is a historical region in the north-eastern Carpathians, on the upper Tisza, today divided between Romania and Ukraine. In the Middle Ages it was a Hungarian county in which Romanian nobles kept local autonomy; two of them, Dragoș and Bogdan, crossed the mountains in…

monte-carlo.s: Monte Carlo is a district of Monaco on the Spélugues plateau east of the harbour. Prince Charles III founded its casino in 1863 to restore the principality's finances after the loss of Menton and Roquebrune, and the quarter, named after him in 1866, grew into a resort of the…

mirko-petrovic-njegos.s: Mirko Petrović-Njegoš was a Montenegrin military commander and poet, elder brother of Prince Danilo I and father of Prince, later King, Nikola I. Known as the 'Sword of Montenegro', he defeated the Ottomans at Grahovac in 1858 and fought in the war of 1862.

mozhaysk.s: Mozhaysk is a town in Moscow Oblast, Russia, on the upper Moskva river about 110 km west of Moscow. Taken by Moscow from Smolensk in 1303, it was the centre of an appanage principality until 1454 and a fortress guarding the western approach to the capital.

mstislavl.s: Mstislavl is a small town in Mogilev Region, eastern Belarus, on the Vikhra river in the Sozh basin. Founded by the 12th century in the Smolensk lands, it was the seat of a Lithuanian appanage principality and later of the Mstislavl Voivodeship of the Polish–Lithuanian…

muroma.s: The Muroma were a Finnic people of the middle Oka basin, mentioned in the Primary Chronicle among the peoples paying tribute to the Rus'. The town of Murom took its name from them.

murom.s: Murom is a city in Vladimir Oblast, Russia, on the left bank of the Oka. Mentioned in the Primary Chronicle under 862, it was the seat of a principality held by princes of the Chernigov line, and it is associated with the saints Peter and Fevronia and the epic hero Ilya Muromets.

minsk.s: Minsk is the capital and largest city of Belarus, on the Svislach river. First recorded in 1067, when the sons of Yaroslav the Wise sacked it in their war with Vseslav of Polotsk, it became the seat of a principality and passed to the Grand Duchy of Lithuania in the 14th century.

mutimir-of-serbia.s: Mutimir was Prince of Serbia in the second half of the 9th century, a member of the Vlastimirović dynasty and son of Vlastimir. He defeated a Bulgarian invasion and drove out his brothers.

malmedy.s: Malmedy is a town in the province of Liège in eastern Belgium. It grew around the abbey founded by Saint Remaclus in the 7th century, twin of the abbey at Stavelot, with which it formed an ecclesiastical principality.

mus.s: Muş, also spelled Mush, is a city in eastern Turkey, capital of Muş Province, on a fertile plain west of Lake Van. It was the centre of the historic Armenian district of Taron, held by the Mamikonian and later Bagratid princes, with the great monastery of Surb Karapet nearby.

maria-of-mangup.s: Maria of Mangup was a princess of the Orthodox principality of Theodoro in the Crimea who married Stephen the Great of Moldavia in 1472. The marriage linked Moldavia with the last Byzantine-ruled state in the Crimea, and Stephen supported her family's claims there.

mehmed-iv.s: Mehmed IV was Ottoman sultan from 1648 to 1687, coming to the throne aged six. Real power passed to the Köprülü grand viziers, who restored order and won Crete and Podolia.

mukachevo.s: Mukachevo, in Hungarian Munkács, is a city in Zakarpattia in western Ukraine. Its hilltop Palanok Castle belonged to the Rákóczi family, and Ilona Zrínyi defended it against the Habsburgs from 1685 to 1688.

machynlleth.s: Machynlleth is a market town in Powys, Wales, in the Dyfi valley. In 1404 Owain Glyndŵr held a parliament there, where he is said to have been crowned Prince of Wales in the presence of envoys from France, Castile and Scotland.

mai-thuc-loan.s: Mai Thúc Loan was the leader of a large uprising in 722 against Tang Chinese rule in Annan, in what is now northern Vietnam. Proclaiming himself emperor, known as the Black Emperor, he gathered a large army and allied with neighbouring peoples, but a Tang army crushed the revolt.

merrimack-river.s: The Merrimack River rises in New Hampshire and flows about 190 km south and then east through Massachusetts to the Atlantic at Newburyport. Early colonial grants used it as a boundary, and its valley was home to Pennacook and other Abenaki communities.

mason-dixon-line.s: The Mason–Dixon line is a boundary surveyed between 1763 and 1767 by Charles Mason and Jeremiah Dixon to settle a long dispute between the proprietors of Maryland and Pennsylvania. It fixed the borders between Pennsylvania, Maryland and Delaware, and in the 19th century it…

maryland-toleration-act.s: The Maryland Toleration Act, passed by the colony's assembly in April 1649, guaranteed freedom of worship to Christians who believed in the Trinity. Promoted by the Catholic proprietor Cecil Calvert, it protected the Catholic minority among a growing Protestant population,…

mary-ii-of-england.s: Mary II was queen of England, Scotland and Ireland from 1689 to 1694, reigning jointly with her husband William III of Orange. The Protestant elder daughter of James II, she was offered the throne with William after the Glorious Revolution, and they accepted the Bill of Rights.

massachusetts-government-act.s: The Massachusetts Government Act was one of the Intolerable Acts passed by the British Parliament in 1774 in response to the Boston Tea Party. It annulled key parts of the colony's charter of 1691, making the council appointed by the Crown and restricting town meetings.

maracaibo.s: Maracaibo is the second-largest city of Venezuela, on the strait linking Lake Maracaibo to the Gulf of Venezuela. Refounded in 1574, it was the capital of a Spanish province of the same name, which joined the Captaincy General of Venezuela in 1777 and stayed royalist early in…

margarita-island.s: Margarita Island is the largest island of Venezuela, in the Caribbean north-east of the mainland, and with nearby islands forms the state of Nueva Esparta. Sighted by Columbus in 1498, it was valued for its pearl fisheries in the 16th century.

manitoba-act.s: The Manitoba Act, passed by the Parliament of Canada in May 1870, created the province of Manitoba from part of Rupert's Land after the Red River Resistance. Negotiated with delegates of Louis Riel's provisional government, it provided for French and English as official…

monnet-plan.s: The Monnet Plan was France's first plan for reconstruction and modernisation, drawn up by Jean Monnet's planning commission and adopted in 1946. It directed investment to basic industries such as coal, steel, electricity, cement, farm machinery and transport, and was partly…

molokans.s: The Molokans are a Russian Spiritual Christian sect that emerged in the 18th century and rejects the Orthodox Church's priesthood, icons and sacraments. Persecuted in the Russian Empire, many were resettled in the 19th century in Transcaucasia, including the Mughan steppe and…

michoacan.s: Michoacán is a state of western Mexico, stretching from the Pacific coast to the volcanic highlands, with its capital at Morelia. It was the heartland of the Purépecha state, which resisted the Aztecs and submitted to the Spanish between 1522 and 1530.

mazyar.s: Mazyar was the last prince of the Qarinvand dynasty of Tabaristan, in the mountains south of the Caspian Sea. He converted to Islam under the caliph al-Ma'mun and governed Tabaristan, but in 839 he rebelled against al-Mu'tasim and the Tahirid governors of Khurasan.

meshchera.s: The Meshchera were a Finnic people of the forests along the middle Oka river in central Russia, mentioned in medieval Russian sources. Their lands came under Ryazan and Moscow, and they were gradually absorbed by Russian settlers and by the Tatars of the Qasim Khanate, centred…

mount-tai.s: Mount Tai is a mountain in Shandong, eastern China, rising to about 1,530 metres, the most revered of China's five sacred peaks. Emperors from Qin Shi Huang and Emperor Wu of Han onward performed the feng and shan sacrifices there to announce their mandate to heaven, and its…

meng-tian.s: Meng Tian was a general of the Qin dynasty. After helping to conquer Qi in 221 BCE, he led a large army against the Xiongnu in the Ordos region, linked older walls into a northern frontier line often seen as the first Great Wall, and built the Straight Road north from the…

musov.s: Mušov is a former village in southern Moravia, Czech Republic, now flooded by the Nové Mlýny reservoirs, whose surroundings hold important remains of the Roman period. On the nearby hill of Burgstall Roman forces built a fortified base during the Marcomannic Wars of the 2nd…

motagua-river.s: The Motagua is the longest river of Guatemala, flowing about 486 kilometres from the western highlands to the Gulf of Honduras on the Caribbean. Its middle valley held the main sources of jadeite in Mesoamerica, and the Classic Maya city of Quiriguá rose on its lower course,…

mhlathuze-river.s: The Mhlathuze is a river in northern KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa, flowing east to the Indian Ocean near Richards Bay. In the late 18th and early 19th centuries the lands along it and the Mfolozi rivers were home to the Mthethwa, Qwabe and early Zulu chiefdoms, whose rivalries…

magellans-cross.s: Magellan's Cross is a Christian cross planted by the expedition of Ferdinand Magellan in Cebu, Philippines, in April 1521, at the baptism of Rajah Humabon and his people. It stands in a small chapel next to the Basilica of the Santo Niño in Cebu City and is said to enclose…

maravar.s: The Maravar are a Tamil community of southern Tamil Nadu, India, historically a warrior caste of the dry Ramnad and Sivaganga region. Their chiefs, the Sethupathis of Ramnad, guarded the pilgrim route to Rameswaram and ruled a kingdom from the 17th century, and Maravar chiefs…

mangareva.s: Mangareva is the largest of the Gambier Islands in the far south-east of French Polynesia. Its Polynesian people were linked by voyaging with Pitcairn and Henderson islands, and it may have been a stepping stone for the settlers of Rapa Nui.

marquesas-islands.s: The Marquesas Islands are a group of rugged volcanic islands in the north-east of French Polynesia, among the earliest settled in eastern Polynesia and a likely source of settlers for Hawaii and Rapa Nui. Visited by the Spanish navigator Álvaro de Mendaña in 1595, they were…

mongkut.s: Mongkut, King Rama IV of Siam, reigned from 1851 to 1868. Before his accession he spent 27 years as a Buddhist monk, founding the reformist Thammayut order and studying Latin, English and Western science.

mont-terrible.s: Mont-Terrible was a French department created on 23 March 1793 from the territory of the Rauracian Republic, the former northern lands of the Prince-Bishopric of Basel in the Jura. Named after a mountain near its capital Porrentruy, it was too small to survive and was merged…

miles-macdonell.s: Miles Macdonell was a Scottish-born soldier and colonial administrator who served as the first governor of the Red River Colony from 1812. His Pemmican Proclamation of 1814, banning the export of pemmican from the colony's lands, angered the North West Company and the Métis…

maly-trostenets.s: Maly Trostenets was a Nazi extermination site near Minsk in occupied Belarus, in use from 1942 to 1944. Jews from Minsk and others deported from Germany, Austria and Czechoslovakia, as well as Soviet prisoners and partisans, were shot there, mostly in the Blagovshchina forest,…

madeira-mamore-railway.s: The Madeira-Mamoré Railway was a line of about 366 km built from 1907 to 1912 through the Amazon rainforest of Rondônia, Brazil, to bypass the rapids of the Madeira and Mamoré rivers. Brazil promised it to Bolivia in the Treaty of Petrópolis of 1903 to give Bolivian rubber an…

march-of-ancona.s: The March of Ancona was a frontier province in central Italy on the Adriatic coast, roughly the modern region of Marche. It took shape under the Holy Roman Empire in the 11th and 12th centuries and was recovered by the papacy under Innocent III, after which the Papal States…

melchior-ndadaye.s: Melchior Ndadaye was the first democratically elected president of Burundi and its first Hutu head of state. Leader of the FRODEBU party, he won the election of June 1993 and took office in July.

matsu-islands.s: The Matsu Islands are an archipelago off the coast of Fujian in mainland China, governed by the Republic of China (Taiwan) as Lienchiang County. Held by Nationalist forces after 1949, they were heavily fortified and shelled during the Taiwan Strait crises.

medellin.s: Medellín is Colombia's second-largest city and the capital of Antioquia department, in the Aburrá Valley of the Andes. It grew in the 20th century as a centre of the coffee trade and the textile industry.

medellin-cartel.s: The Medellín Cartel was a Colombian drug-trafficking network based in Medellín that dominated the cocaine trade to the United States in the 1980s. Led by Pablo Escobar with partners such as the Ochoa brothers and Carlos Lehder, it waged a campaign of bombings and…

minor-c-keith.s: Minor Cooper Keith was an American businessman who built the railway from Costa Rica's Central Valley to the Caribbean coast between 1871 and 1890. He planted bananas along the line to provide freight, and in 1899 his banana business merged into the United Fruit Company.

mariel-boatlift.s: The Mariel boatlift was the mass emigration of about 125,000 Cubans from the port of Mariel to Florida between April and October 1980. It began after thousands of Cubans sought asylum at the Peruvian embassy in Havana, and Fidel Castro allowed those who wished to leave to go,…

maximo-gomez.s: Máximo Gómez was a Dominican-born general who became the commander of Cuba's independence armies. He fought throughout the Ten Years' War of 1868–1878 and, as general-in-chief in the war of 1895, led the invasion of western Cuba with Antonio Maceo, using guerrilla tactics and…

mohamed-morsi.s: Mohamed Morsi was an Egyptian engineer and Muslim Brotherhood politician who became Egypt's first freely elected president in June 2012. His year in office was marked by economic difficulties and a decree expanding his powers that provoked mass protests.

manuel-zelaya.s: Manuel Zelaya is a Honduran politician of the Liberal Party who was President of Honduras from 2006 until 28 June 2009, when the army removed him and flew him to Costa Rica. The coup followed his push for a poll on a constituent assembly and his closer ties with Hugo Chávez's…

mustafa-barzani.s: Mustafa Barzani was a Kurdish nationalist leader who led the Kurdish movement in Iraq for much of the 20th century. He commanded the army of the short-lived Republic of Mahabad in Iran in 1946, then led his followers to the Soviet Union, returning to Iraq in 1958.

mahabad.s: Mahabad is a city in West Azerbaijan province in north-western Iran, south of Lake Urmia, with a mainly Kurdish population. Formerly called Saujbulagh, it took the name Mahabad in the 1930s.

maryland-county.s: Maryland County is the south-easternmost county of Liberia, on the border with Côte d'Ivoire, with its capital at Harper. It covers the territory of the former Republic of Maryland, founded by African American settlers at Cape Palmas, which was annexed to Liberia in 1857 after…

maryland-state-colonization-society.s: The Maryland State Colonization Society was a branch of the American colonisation movement that from 1831 organised the emigration of free Black Americans from Maryland to Africa, with funds from the state legislature. In 1834 it founded a colony at Cape Palmas in West Africa,…

mirdita.s: Mirdita is a mountainous region of northern Albania, home to a Catholic Gheg clan of the same name, with its centre at Rrëshen. Under Ottoman rule it enjoyed wide autonomy under hereditary chiefs, the kapedans of the Gjonmarkaj family.

managua.s: Managua is the capital and largest city of Nicaragua, on the southern shore of Lake Managua. A small town between the rival cities of León and Granada, it was chosen as the capital in 1852 as a compromise.

marin-drzic.s: Marin Držić was a Renaissance playwright and poet from the Republic of Ragusa (Dubrovnik), regarded as the greatest Croatian writer of comedies. His best-known play, Dundo Maroje (c.

monte-titano.s: Monte Titano is a limestone mountain in San Marino, rising to 739 metres, on whose ridge stand the City of San Marino and the republic's Three Towers. According to tradition Saint Marinus founded a Christian community there in 301.

montalcino.s: Montalcino is a hill town in the province of Siena in southern Tuscany, Italy. After Siena fell to imperial and Florentine forces in 1555, Sienese exiles kept the republic alive there under French protection until 1559, when it passed to Cosimo I de' Medici.

mirabeau-b-lamar.s: Mirabeau B. Lamar was a Georgia-born politician and soldier who was the second President of the Republic of Texas, from 1838 to 1841.

mariano-arista.s: Mariano Arista was a Mexican general and politician who was President of Mexico from 1851 to 1853. In 1840 he defeated the federalist rebels of the Republic of the Rio Grande.

martin-miguel-de-guemes.s: Martín Miguel de Güemes was an Argentine military leader and governor of Salta from 1815 to 1821. With gaucho guerrilla forces he defended the northern frontier of the United Provinces of the Río de la Plata against repeated royalist invasions from Upper Peru, allowing José de…

manuel-crescencio-rejon.s: Manuel Crescencio Rejón was a Mexican jurist and politician from Yucatán. He drafted much of Yucatán's constitution of 1841, which introduced the writ of amparo, a citizen's legal protection against unconstitutional acts by the authorities.

miguel-barbachano.s: Miguel Barbachano y Tarrazo was a politician from Mérida who served several times as governor of Yucatán between 1841 and 1853. His rivalry with Santiago Méndez of Campeche dominated the peninsula's politics.

miguel-primo-de-rivera.s: Miguel Primo de Rivera was a Spanish general who seized power in a coup in September 1923 and ruled as dictator with the backing of King Alfonso XIII until January 1930. His regime ended the Rif War in Morocco with French help and invested in public works, but lost support…

malolos.s: Malolos is a city in Bulacan province, north of Manila in the Philippines. In 1898 it became the seat of Emilio Aguinaldo's revolutionary government; the Malolos Congress met at its Barasoain Church and drafted a constitution, and the First Philippine Republic was inaugurated…

maqoma.s: Maqoma was a Rharhabe Xhosa chief, the eldest son of Ngqika, and one of the most capable commanders of the Cape frontier wars. Expelled from the Kat River valley in 1829, he led Xhosa forces in the wars of 1834–1836 and 1850–1853.

minamoto-no-yoritomo.s: Minamoto no Yoritomo was the founder and first shogun of the Kamakura shogunate. Leading the Minamoto clan to victory over the Taira in the Genpei War of 1180–1185, he set up a warrior government at Kamakura, appointed military governors and stewards across Japan and destroyed…

mathurin-leonard-duphot.s: Mathurin-Léonard Duphot was a French general of the Revolutionary Wars who served under Napoleon in Italy. In December 1797 he was shot by papal troops during a riot outside the French embassy in Rome.

malbork.s: Malbork (German Marienburg) is a town on the Nogat River in northern Poland, built around the castle of the Teutonic Order, its headquarters from 1309 to 1457. The castle is the largest brick Gothic fortress in the world and a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

manitoba.s: Manitoba is a province of central Canada, with Winnipeg as its capital. It was created in 1870 from part of Rupert's Land after the Red River Resistance led by Louis Riel, whose provisional government negotiated its entry into Confederation, and was enlarged northwards to…

metis.s: The Métis are an Indigenous people of Canada and the northern United States who arose from the unions of fur traders, mostly French and Scottish, with First Nations women. Centred on the Red River valley, they developed a distinct culture, the Michif language and the buffalo…

millau.s: Millau is a town in the Aveyron department of southern France, on the Tarn River. In Roman times the nearby workshops of La Graufesenque made red-gloss pottery exported across the empire, and the town later became a centre of glove-making.

matsuda-michiyuki.s: Matsuda Michiyuki was a Japanese official of the Meiji government who carried out the annexation of the Ryukyu Kingdom, an event known as the Ryukyu Disposition. In 1879 he arrived at Shuri with police and troops, abolished the Ryukyu domain and established Okinawa Prefecture,…

manius-curius-dentatus.s: Manius Curius Dentatus was a Roman general and statesman of plebeian origin. As consul in 290 BCE he ended the Third Samnite War and conquered the Sabines, and in 275 BCE he defeated Pyrrhus of Epirus near Beneventum.

muhammad-ibn-wasif.s: Muhammad ibn Wasif was a secretary at the court of the Saffarid ruler Ya'qub ibn al-Layth in Sistan in the late 9th century. According to the Tarikh-i Sistan, when Ya'qub complained that he could not understand poems praising him in Arabic, Muhammad composed verses in Persian…

mendut.s: Mendut is a 9th-century Buddhist temple in Central Java, Indonesia, about three kilometres east of Borobudur, built under the Sailendra dynasty. Its chamber holds three large stone statues: a seated Buddha flanked by the bodhisattvas Avalokiteshvara and Vajrapani.

milton-cato.s: Milton Cato was a Vincentian lawyer and politician who led Saint Vincent and the Grenadines to independence. A founder of the Saint Vincent Labour Party in 1955, he served as chief minister and premier and became the country's first prime minister at independence in October 1979.

mino-province.s: Mino Province was an old province of central Japan, corresponding to the southern part of modern Gifu Prefecture. Its rich farmland and its position on the routes between eastern Japan and Kyoto made it valuable; it was ruled by the Toki family as governors, seized by Saito…

mongke-temur-son-of-hulagu.s: Möngke Temür was a Mongol prince of the Ilkhanate, a son of Hulagu Khan. He married Abish Khatun, the last Salghurid ruler of Fars, which brought the province under closer Ilkhanid control.

merovech.s: Merovech was a semi-legendary king of the Salian Franks in the mid-5th century, from whom the Merovingian dynasty took its name. Gregory of Tours says only that some held him to be of the family of Chlodio and that he was the father of Childeric I.

mughith-al-din-tughrilshah.s: Mughith al-Din Tughrilshah was a prince of the Seljuk Sultanate of Rum and a son of Kilij Arslan II. In 1202 his brother Süleymanshah II gave him Erzurum, taken from the Saltukids, and he ruled it as a largely independent principality until his death.

miraj.s: Miraj is a town in Sangli district of Maharashtra, India, close to the Krishna river. Its fort was held by the Bijapur Sultanate and later by the Marathas, and in the 18th century it became the seat of the Patwardhan family, generals of the Peshwas.

massufa.s: The Massufa were a Sanhaja Berber tribe of the western Sahara, closely related to the Lamtuna and among the early supporters of the Almoravid movement in the 11th century. They controlled much of the caravan traffic across the desert, including the salt mines of Taghaza and…

mahisagar-district.s: Mahisagar district is a district of eastern Gujarat, India, created in 2013 from parts of the Panchmahal and Kheda districts, with its headquarters at Lunavada. It is named after the Mahi river, which flows through it.

manisa.s: Manisa is a city in western Turkey, at the foot of Mount Sipylus above the Gediz plain, north-east of Izmir. Known in antiquity as Magnesia ad Sipylum, it gave its name to the battle of 190 BCE in which Rome defeated Antiochus III.

mito-ibaraki.s: Mito is a city in eastern Japan and the capital of Ibaraki Prefecture. The Satake moved their seat there in the 1590s, and from 1609 it was the castle town of the Mito Domain, ruled by a senior branch of the Tokugawa family.

mohammed-bin-salman.s: Mohammed bin Salman is the crown prince of Saudi Arabia, a son of King Salman, and since 2022 also its prime minister. Appointed crown prince in 2017, he concentrated power in his own hands, launched the Vision 2030 programme to diversify the economy away from oil and relaxed…

masjid-al-haram.s: The Masjid al-Haram, the Grand Mosque of Mecca, is the holiest site of Islam, surrounding the Kaaba towards which Muslims pray. It is the centre of the hajj pilgrimage, and Saudi rulers have enlarged it repeatedly since the 1950s to hold millions of worshippers.

marklo.s: Marklo was the meeting place of the general assembly of the pagan Saxons, said to have been held each year on the Weser in northern Germany. The 9th-century Life of Saint Lebuin describes delegates of nobles, freemen and half-free from every district gathering there to decide…

marduk-kabit-ahheshu.s: Marduk-kabit-ahheshu was the founder of the Second Dynasty of Isin, which ruled Babylonia from about 1157 BCE. He established his line at Isin as Elamite invasions brought down the Kassite dynasty, his reign overlapping with that of the last Kassite king.

marduk-nadin-ahhe.s: Marduk-nadin-ahhe was a king of Babylon of the Second Dynasty of Isin, reigning from about 1099 to 1082 BCE, and a brother of Nebuchadnezzar I. He raided Assyria and carried off statues of gods from Ekallatum, but the Assyrian king Tiglath-Pileser I struck back, raiding…

muridun.s: The Muridun, 'disciples', were the followers of the Sufi teacher Ibn Qasi in the Algarve in south-western al-Andalus. In 1144 they rose against Almoravid rule, seizing Mértola, Silves and other towns, and Ibn Qasi ruled Mértola as imam.

monte-barbaro.s: Monte Barbaro is a hill in north-western Sicily, near Calatafimi, on which stand the ruins of the ancient city of Segesta, chief settlement of the Elymians. Its summit holds the remains of the city's agora, houses and a Greek theatre facing the sea, while the unfinished Doric…

manapa-tarhunta.s: Manapa-Tarhunta was a king of the Seha River Land in western Anatolia in the late 14th and early 13th centuries BCE. Having sided with Arzawa against the Hittites, he was spared by Mursili II, who confirmed him as a vassal king by treaty.

muhammad-ii-seljuk-sultan-of-iraq.s: Muhammad II, son of Mahmud II, was Seljuk sultan of Iraq and western Iran from 1153 to 1159. Seeking to restore Seljuk authority over the Abbasid caliphs, he besieged Baghdad in 1157, but the siege failed.

muhammad-ii-of-granada.s: Muhammad II was the second Nasrid sultan of Granada, reigning from 1273 to 1302. He organised the emirate's administration and defended it by playing Castile, Aragon and the Marinids of Morocco against one another.

mezotne-hillfort.s: Mežotne hillfort is an earthwork fortress on the bank of the Lielupe in southern Latvia. It was one of the chief strongholds of the Semigallians, surrounded by a settlement and burial grounds, and German crusaders captured it in the early 13th century.

micanopy.s: Micanopy was a principal chief of the Seminole in Florida. He was among the leaders of the Second Seminole War, taking part in the attack on Major Dade's column in December 1835.

miyagi-prefecture.s: Miyagi Prefecture is a prefecture in the Tōhoku region of north-eastern Honshu, Japan, with its capital at Sendai. It was formed after the abolition of the domains in 1871, largely from the lands of the Sendai Domain.

maxima-sequanorum.s: Maxima Sequanorum was a late Roman province created around 300 CE, covering the former land of the Sequani in the Jura and western Switzerland. Its capital was Vesontio, now Besançon.

manuchihr-ibn-shavur.s: Manuchihr ibn Shavur was the first Shaddadid emir of Ani, to whom the Seljuk sultan Malik Shah granted the city in 1072. He built the mosque that still stands there, one of the earliest Turkish-era mosques in Anatolia.

merowe-sudan.s: Merowe is a town on the Nile in northern Sudan, near the fourth cataract and the ancient sites of Napata and Jebel Barkal. It lay in the land of the Shaigiya tribes.

makhachkala.s: Makhachkala is the capital of the Republic of Dagestan in Russia, on the western shore of the Caspian Sea. It grew from the Russian fortress of Petrovskoye, founded in 1844 near the old shamkhal seat of Tarki, and was renamed in 1921 after the revolutionary Makhach Dakhadayev.

may-thirtieth-movement.s: The May Thirtieth Movement was a wave of anti-imperialist strikes and protests in China that followed the shooting of demonstrators by the International Settlement's police on Nanjing Road, Shanghai, on 30 May 1925. Strikes and boycotts of British and Japanese goods spread to…

massa-tuscany.s: Massa is a city in north-western Tuscany, Italy, at the foot of the Apuan Alps near the Ligurian coast. From the 15th century it was ruled by the Malaspina and later the Cybo-Malaspina families, whose small state with neighbouring Carrara became a duchy and passed to the Duchy…

moussa-ag-amastan.s: Moussa ag Amastan was amenokal, or paramount chief, of the Kel Ahaggar Tuareg of the central Sahara from 1905 until his death in 1920. After French forces defeated the Tuareg at Tit in 1902 he submitted to French rule and became a close friend of the hermit Charles de Foucauld…

mount-ebal.s: Mount Ebal is a mountain north of Nablus in the West Bank, facing Mount Gerizim across the valley of ancient Shechem. In the Hebrew Bible it is where Moses commanded the Israelites to build an altar and pronounce curses, while blessings were spoken from Gerizim.

masfut.s: Masfut is an inland exclave of the emirate of Ajman in the Hajar Mountains of the United Arab Emirates, near the border with Oman and the Dubai enclave of Hatta. A small farming town of date gardens and falaj irrigation, it is one of two detached territories, with Manama, that…

manama.s: Manama is the capital and largest city of Bahrain, on the north-east coast of Bahrain Island. Mentioned in Islamic chronicles from the 14th century, it grew as the islands' main port for pearling, trade and later the British political agency.

muhammad-bin-thani.s: Muhammad bin Thani was the leader of Doha and the first ruler of Qatar recognised by Britain. After a destructive war with Bahrain and Abu Dhabi, he signed an agreement with the British envoy Lewis Pelly in 1868 that treated him as the peninsula's leader and separated Qatar…

malavikagnimitram.s: Malavikagnimitram is a Sanskrit play by Kalidasa, probably the earliest of his three surviving dramas. Set at the court of the Shunga king Agnimitra in Vidisha, it is a court comedy about the king's love for Malavika, a maid of the queen who proves to be a princess.

morgantina.s: Morgantina is an ancient city in central Sicily near Aidone, occupied by Sicels and then Greeks from the Bronze Age to the Roman period. Captured by Ducetius in the 5th century BCE, it flourished under Hieron II of Syracuse and was sacked by Rome in 211 BCE.

manlius-valens.s: Gaius Manlius Valens was a Roman commander who, as legate of a legion in Britain in 52, was defeated by the Silures of south Wales soon after the death of the governor Ostorius Scapula, as Tacitus records. He later held commands in the civil wars of 69 and was consul in 96 at…

mandarin-chinese.s: Mandarin Chinese is the largest group of Chinese dialects, spoken across northern and south-western China, and the basis of Standard Chinese, the official language of the People's Republic of China and Taiwan. Standard Mandarin, based on the Beijing dialect, is one of…

madura.s: Madura is an island off the north-east coast of Java, in Indonesia's East Java province, separated from Java by the narrow Madura Strait. Drier and less fertile than Java, it is known for salt production, cattle raising and bull races, and its people, the Madurese, speak their…

mukteshvara-temple-bhubaneswar.s: The Mukteshvara Temple is a small 10th-century Hindu temple dedicated to Shiva in Bhubaneswar, Odisha, built under the Somavamshi dynasty. Admired as a gem of Odishan architecture, it marks the transition to the mature Kalinga style and is known for its carved arched gateway…

meissen.s: Meissen is a town on the Elbe in Saxony, Germany, north-west of Dresden. It grew around a castle founded by King Henry the Fowler in 929 among the Slavic Sorbs, became the seat of a bishopric in 968 and of the margraves of Meissen, from whose Wettin line the Electorate of…

markos-botsaris.s: Markos Botsaris (c. 1788–1823) was a Souliote leader and hero of the Greek War of Independence.

mariana-islands.s: The Mariana Islands are a chain of fifteen volcanic islands in the western Pacific, including Guam, Saipan, Tinian and Rota. Settled by the ancestors of the Chamorro about 3,500 years ago, they were colonised by Spain from 1668.

malta.s: Malta is an island country in the central Mediterranean, south of Sicily, made up of Malta, Gozo and smaller islands. Its harbours drew Phoenicians, Romans, Arabs, who took it in 870, and Normans; from 1530 it was the base of the Knights Hospitaller, who withstood the Ottoman…

mikhail-gorbachev.s: Mikhail Gorbachev (1931–2022) was the last leader of the Soviet Union, general secretary of the Communist Party from 1985 and president from 1990 to 1991. His policies of glasnost, or openness, and perestroika, or restructuring, loosened censorship and central control, while…

mers-el-kebir.s: Mers El Kébir is a port town on the Algerian coast a few kilometres west of Oran, with one of the best natural harbours of North Africa. Spain held it from 1505, with Oran, until 1708 and again from 1732 to 1792.

mostaganem.s: Mostaganem is a port city on the Mediterranean coast of western Algeria, east of Oran. In 1558 the Count of Alcaudete, Spanish governor of Oran, led an army against it and was defeated and killed by the forces of Algiers, one of Spain's worst setbacks in North Africa.

melilla.s: Melilla is a Spanish autonomous city on the Mediterranean coast of north-east Morocco. Founded by the Phoenicians as Rusadir, it was occupied by the Umayyad Caliphate of Córdoba in 927, and Castilian forces took it in 1497.

matagorda-bay.s: Matagorda Bay is a large bay on the Gulf coast of Texas, sheltered by Matagorda Island and Matagorda Peninsula. In 1685 La Salle's French expedition landed there and built Fort Saint Louis nearby, and his ship La Belle sank in the bay, where archaeologists recovered it in the…

marquis-lie-of-zhao.s: Marquis Lie of Zhao, personal name Zhao Ji, was ruler of the Zhao clan territory when King Weilie of Zhou formally recognised Zhao, Wei and Han as states in 403 BCE. The recognition of the three families that had partitioned the State of Jin is traditionally taken as the start…

mencius.s: Mencius (Mengzi) was a Confucian philosopher of the 4th century BCE, born in the State of Zou in Shandong. He travelled among the courts of Qi, Wei and Teng urging rulers to govern through benevolence, and taught that human nature is innately good.

mankurwane.s: Mankurwane was chief of the Tlhaping, a Tswana people, at Taung in the second half of the 19th century. In 1882 he fought the Korana chief David Massouw over land west of the Transvaal, both sides recruiting white mercenaries who were later paid in farms.

makua.s: The Makua are a Bantu people of northern Mozambique and southern Tanzania, the largest ethnic group of Mozambique. Organised in many chiefdoms in the interior, they traded and fought with the Swahili coastal sultanates such as Angoche, and were drawn into the ivory and slave…

moheli.s: Mohéli, or Mwali, is the smallest of the four main islands of the Comoros, between Grande Comore and Anjouan. Long claimed by the sultans of Anjouan, it was seized around 1830 by the Malagasy prince Ramanetaka, whose family ruled it as sultans until it became a French…

mutsamudu.s: Mutsamudu is the capital of the island of Anjouan in the Comoros and the country's second-largest town. Founded in the 15th century, it became the seat of the Anjouan sultans, with a stone medina, palaces and a citadel built in the late 18th century above its harbour.

murzuq.s: Murzuq is an oasis town in the Fezzan region of south-western Libya. From the 16th century it was the capital of the Awlad Muhammad sultans of Fezzan and a major station on the caravan route between Tripoli, Bornu and the Lake Chad region.

moroni.s: Moroni is the capital and largest city of the Comoros, on the west coast of Grande Comore. A Shirazi-founded coastal town of the Bambao sultanate, it replaced Dzaoudzi on Mayotte as capital of the French territory of the Comoros in the early 1960s and became capital of the…

muhsin-ibn-fadl.s: Muhsin ibn Fadl al-Abdali was sultan of Lahej in southern Arabia from 1827 to 1847. In January 1839 a British East India Company force under Captain Stafford Haines captured Aden from him after disputes over a plundered ship, creating the Aden Settlement.

mesud-ii.s: Mesud II was the last sultan of the Seljuk Sultanate of Rum, reigning intermittently from 1284 until his death around 1308. He ruled as a vassal of the Mongol Ilkhanate, which installed and deposed him, and held little real power as Anatolia fragmented among Turkmen beyliks.

moro-people.s: The Moro people are the Muslim peoples of Mindanao, the Sulu archipelago and Palawan in the southern Philippines, among them the Tausug, Maguindanao and Maranao. The name was given by the Spanish, who fought them in the long Moro wars from the 16th to the 19th century.

mahakaccana.s: Mahakaccana was one of the leading disciples of the Buddha, praised in the Pali texts as foremost in explaining briefly stated teachings in detail. A native of Ujjain, he is said to have spread Buddhism in Avanti, and in the Madhura Sutta he teaches King Avantiputra of…

megasthenes.s: Megasthenes was a Greek historian and diplomat sent by the Seleucid king Seleucus I as envoy to the court of Chandragupta Maurya at Pataliputra around 300 BCE. His Indica, known only from quotations by later writers such as Arrian, Strabo and Diodorus, described Indian…

maryland.s: Maryland is a state of the eastern United States on Chesapeake Bay. Founded in 1634 as an English proprietary colony of the Calvert family, Lords Baltimore, it offered a refuge for Catholics and grew rich on tobacco worked by indentured servants and enslaved Africans.

mbabane.s: Mbabane is the capital and one of the largest cities of Eswatini, in the highveld of the north-west. It grew from a trading post near the royal residence of King Mbandzeni and was chosen in 1902 as the administrative centre of the British protectorate of Swaziland.

milo-of-croton.s: Milo of Croton was the most famous wrestler of ancient Greece, winning at the Olympic Games six times in the later 6th century BCE, as well as many victories at the other panhellenic games. Ancient writers tell many stories of his strength and link him with Pythagoras, who…

muhammad-ibn-tahir.s: Muhammad ibn Tahir was the last Tahirid governor of Khurasan, ruling from Nishapur from 862 to 873 on behalf of the Abbasid caliphs. Under him the dynasty lost control of Tabaristan to the Zaydi Alids and faced rising disorder in Sistan.

martos.s: Martos is a town in the province of Jaén, Andalusia, Spain, below the rock known as the Peña de Martos; it was the Roman colony of Tucci. Its castle was handed to Ferdinand III of Castile by al-Bayyasi in the 1220s and then given to the Order of Calatrava, which held it as a…

medina-elvira.s: Medina Elvira (Madinat Ilbira) was a city of al-Andalus near modern Atarfe, north-west of Granada, and the capital of the Elvira district under the Umayyads. It grew near Roman Iliberri, where the Council of Elvira met in the early 4th century.

molina-de-aragon.s: Molina de Aragón is a town on the Gallo river in the province of Guadalajara, Spain, dominated by one of the largest castles in the country. A Muslim border lordship in the 11th century, it was taken by Alfonso I of Aragon around 1129 and became the semi-independent Lordship…

moron-de-la-frontera.s: Morón de la Frontera is a town in the province of Seville, Andalusia, Spain, south-east of the city of Seville. A Berber clan, the Banu Dammar, ruled it as a small taifa in the early 11th century until al-Mutadid of Seville annexed it.

mirpur-khas.s: Mirpur Khas is a city in Sindh, Pakistan, east of Hyderabad. Founded in 1806 by Mir Ali Murad Talpur, it was the seat of a branch of the Talpur dynasty until the British conquest of 1843.

mavia.s: Mavia was a queen of the Arab Tanukhids in the later 4th century CE who led a revolt against Rome in the 370s. Her forces ravaged Palestine and Phoenicia and defeated Roman troops, until the emperor Valens accepted her demand that an Arab hermit named Moses be made bishop of…

mar-piccolo.s: The Mar Piccolo is a shallow inner sea at Taranto in Apulia, southern Italy, linked by narrow channels to the outer bay, the Mar Grande. It gave ancient Taras and later Taranto one of the best harbours of southern Italy and has long been used for shellfish farming.

marta-river.s: The Marta is a river of northern Lazio, Italy, flowing about 50 km from Lake Bolsena, its only outlet, to the Tyrrhenian Sea south of Tarquinia. Its valley was a route between the Etruscan cities of the interior and the coast, and the city of Tarquinii stood on a plateau above…

maputaland.s: Maputaland is a region of north-eastern KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa, between the Lubombo Mountains and the Indian Ocean, bordering Mozambique and Eswatini. It formed the southern part of the Tembe kingdom until the Anglo-Portuguese boundary of the 1890s divided the kingdom,…

map-of-teozacoalco.s: The Map of Teozacoalco is a painted map of 1580 from the Mixtec town of Teozacoalco in Oaxaca, Mexico, made for the Relaciones Geográficas ordered by Philip II of Spain. It combines a map of the town's lands with genealogies of its rulers.

mozdok.s: Mozdok is a town in North Ossetia–Alania, Russia, on the Terek River. It was founded as a Russian fortress in 1763, and its construction on land claimed by the Kabardians helped provoke the long Russian–Circassian conflict.

manuha.s: Manuha was the last king of the Mon kingdom of Thaton in Lower Burma. According to the Burmese chronicles, he refused King Anawrahta of Pagan's request for Buddhist scriptures, and in 1057 Anawrahta took Thaton and carried him, his court, monks and craftsmen to Pagan.

mentuhotep-i.s: Mentuhotep I was a nomarch of Thebes in Upper Egypt in the late 22nd century BCE and the founder of the Eleventh Dynasty. He probably ruled only as a local governor, but later kings honoured him as an ancestor with royal titles.

montu.s: Montu was an ancient Egyptian god of war, worshipped in the Theban region and shown with a falcon's head crowned by a sun disc and two plumes. His cult centres included Armant, Medamud and Tod, and he rose to prominence under the Eleventh Dynasty, whose kings took the name…

mpondo.s: The Mpondo are a Xhosa-speaking Nguni people of the north-eastern Eastern Cape, South Africa, in the region historically called Pondoland, between the Mthatha and Mtamvuna rivers. Their kingdom kept its independence until it was annexed to the Cape Colony in 1894.

mirabal-sisters.s: The Mirabal sisters, Patria, Minerva and María Teresa Mirabal, were Dominican political activists who opposed the dictatorship of Rafael Trujillo. Members of the clandestine 14 June Movement, they were murdered on Trujillo's orders on 25 November 1960, and their deaths…

mario-soares.s: Mário Soares was a Portuguese politician who founded the Socialist Party in exile in 1973 and helped steer Portugal to democracy after the Carnation Revolution of 1974. He was prime minister from 1976 to 1978 and from 1983 to 1985, when he negotiated Portugal's entry into the…

manuel-piar.s: Manuel Piar was a general of the Venezuelan war of independence, born in Curaçao. He led the patriot campaign in Guayana, winning the Battle of San Félix in 1817 and helping to secure Angostura as a base.

mazaces.s: Mazaces was the last Persian satrap of Egypt under Darius III. Appointed after his predecessor Sabaces fell at the Battle of Issus in 333 BCE, he had no army able to resist Alexander the Great and surrendered the country to him without a fight in 332 BCE, handing over Memphis…

maha-sura-singhanat.s: Maha Sura Singhanat, born Bunma and known in the Thonburi period as Chao Phraya Surasi, was a Siamese general and the younger brother of Rama I. With his brother he led Taksin's campaigns against Lan Na, Cambodia and Laos, including the capture of Vientiane in 1779.

mcmahon-line.s: The McMahon Line is the boundary between Tibet and British India drawn by the British negotiator Henry McMahon and agreed with Tibetan representatives at the Simla Convention of 1914. It follows the crest of the eastern Himalayas for about 890 kilometres.

mikael-sehul.s: Mikael Sehul was a Tigrayan lord who dominated the Ethiopian Empire in the late 18th century. Having built a strong regional state in Tigray that controlled the trade route to Massawa, he marched on Gondar, had Emperor Iyoas I killed in 1769 and installed and removed emperors…

moquegua.s: Moquegua is a city and region in southern Peru, in a warm valley on the western slope of the Andes. In the Middle Horizon the valley was a meeting ground of two Andean states, with Tiwanaku colonies on the valley floor and the Wari stronghold of Cerro Baúl above it, and later…

moquihuix.s: Moquihuix was the tlatoani of Tlatelolco, the twin city of Tenochtitlan, from about 1460 to 1473. He was married to a sister of the Tenochca ruler Axayacatl, and quarrels between the two cities led to open war in 1473.

maxixcatzin.s: Maxixcatzin was the ruler of Ocotelolco, the most powerful of the four altepetl that made up the Nahua state of Tlaxcala, at the time of the Spanish arrival. After the Tlaxcalans fought Cortés in 1519, he argued for alliance with the Spanish and supported them after their…

man-mandir-palace.s: The Man Mandir Palace stands inside Gwalior Fort in Madhya Pradesh, India, and was built by the Tomara king Man Singh Tomar between about 1486 and 1516. Its outer walls are decorated with bands of blue, green and yellow glazed tiles showing ducks, elephants, tigers and…

maulana-abul-kalam-azad-arabic-persian-r.n: Maulana Abul Kalam Azad Arabic Persian Research Institute
maulana-abul-kalam-azad-arabic-persian-r.s: The Maulana Abul Kalam Azad Arabic Persian Research Institute is a manuscript library and research centre at Tonk in Rajasthan, India, established by the state government in 1978. Its collection grew from the library of the Nawabs of Tonk and holds thousands of Arabic, Persian…

muhammad-ali-khan-of-tonk.s: Muhammad Ali Khan was the Nawab of Tonk, a princely state of Rajputana in India, from 1864 to 1867. In 1867 men acting for him killed members of the family of the Thakur of Lawa, a dependent chief, and the British government deposed him and sent him into exile at Benares.

milners-kindergarten.s: Milner's Kindergarten was the name given to a group of young Oxford-educated administrators recruited by Alfred Milner, British High Commissioner in South Africa, to rebuild the Transvaal and Orange River colonies after the Second Boer War. Members such as Lionel Curtis,…

moesia.s: Moesia was a Roman province south of the lower Danube, covering parts of modern Serbia, North Macedonia, Bulgaria and Romania, named after the Thracian Moesi. Conquered after the campaigns of Marcus Licinius Crassus in 29 BCE and organised early in the 1st century CE, it was…

morava-river.s: The Morava, called the March in German, is a river of central Europe that rises in the north of the Czech Republic and flows south about 350 kilometres through Moravia, to which it gives its name, before joining the Danube near Bratislava. Its lower course forms the borders…

mandubracius.s: Mandubracius was a prince of the Trinovantes in south-eastern Britain whose father had been killed by Cassivellaunus. He fled to Julius Caesar in Gaul and returned with Caesar's second invasion of Britain in 54 BCE.

msallata.s: Msallata is a town in the hills of north-western Libya, inland from Khoms and south-east of Tripoli. In November 1918, after the Ottoman defeat in the First World War, Tripolitanian notables gathered there and proclaimed the Tripolitanian Republic, one of the first republics…

maha-manikya.s: Maha Manikya was a ruler of Tripura in the early 15th century, usually seen as the first historically attested king of the Manikya dynasty. The Rajmala places him in a long line of legendary predecessors, but historians regard him as the first ruler confirmed by other…

manikya-dynasty.s: The Manikya dynasty ruled the kingdom of Tripura in north-eastern India from about the early 15th century until 1949, one of the longest-lasting royal lines of South Asia. Its kings claimed descent from the lunar dynasty of Hindu tradition, and their history is told in the…

mula-murcia.s: Mula is a town in the Region of Murcia in south-eastern Spain, lying on the Mula river west of the city of Murcia. It is named among the seven towns that Theodemir kept under his rule in the treaty he made with the Muslim conquerors in 713.

maui.s: Maui is the second-largest island of Hawaii, formed by two volcanoes joined by an isthmus, with the summit of Haleakalā in the east. Its chiefs, united under Piʻilani around 1500, became a leading power under Kahekili II in the late 18th century.

mua-tonga.s: Muʻa is a town on the shore of the lagoon of Tongatapu, the main island of Tonga. From about the 12th or 13th century its district of Lapaha was the seat of the Tuʻi Tonga, the sacred kings, and the centre of a chiefdom whose influence reached across western Polynesia.

mosque-of-ibn-tulun.s: The Mosque of Ibn Tulun is a congregational mosque in Cairo, built by Ahmad ibn Tulun for his new capital, al-Qata'i, and completed in 879. Built of brick and decorated with carved stucco, it has a vast courtyard surrounded by arcades and a minaret with an external spiral…

maastricht.s: Maastricht is a city on the Meuse in the far south of the Netherlands and the capital of the province of Limburg. It grew from a Roman river crossing and became a centre of the cult of Saint Servatius, whose relics lie in the Basilica of Saint Servatius.

martin-of-tours.s: Martin of Tours was a Roman soldier turned monk and bishop of Tours from 371 until his death in 397. Born in Pannonia, he is remembered for sharing his cloak with a beggar at Amiens, and he founded the monasteries of Ligugé and Marmoutier.

mamilia-gens.s: The Mamilia gens was a family of Tusculum in Latium that later became part of the Roman nobility. Its legendary leader Octavius Mamilius was the son-in-law of Tarquinius Superbus and is said to have led the Latins against Rome at Lake Regillus around 496 BCE.

mixteca-costa.s: The Mixteca Costa is the coastal lowland region of the Mixtec homeland, on the Pacific side of the states of Oaxaca and Guerrero in southern Mexico. Hot and fertile, it produced cotton, cacao and salt and had access to marine resources.

moesia-inferior.s: Moesia Inferior was a Roman province on the lower Danube, covering present-day northern Bulgaria and the Dobruja region of Romania. It was created around 86 CE, when Domitian divided Moesia, and defended the Danube frontier with legions at Novae, Durostorum and Troesmis.

maharana.s: Maharana, 'great rana', was the royal title of the rulers of Mewar, whose capital was Chittor and from 1559 Udaipur, and of a few other Rajput states such as Porbandar. The rulers of Mewar bore it for centuries as a mark of their claim to precedence among the Rajput princes.

macmurrough-dynasty.s: The MacMurroughs, in Irish Meic Murchada, were the leading family of the Uí Chennselaig and kings of Leinster from the 11th century, named after Murchad, son of Diarmait mac Máel na mBó. Diarmait Mac Murchada brought Anglo-Norman knights into Ireland in 1169.

maedoc-of-ferns.s: Máedóc of Ferns, also known as Aidan or Mogue, was an Irish saint who founded the monastery of Ferns in County Wexford around 600. Under the patronage of the Uí Chennselaig kings, Ferns became the chief church of southern Leinster and later the seat of a diocese.

mathgamain-mac-cennetig.s: Mathgamain mac Cennétig was king of the Dál Cais and, from about 970, king of Munster, the elder brother of Brian Boru. With Brian he defeated the Norse of Limerick at Sulcoit in 967 and sacked their town, and he took Cashel from the Eóganachta.

mikhail-artemyevich-muravyov.s: Mikhail Muravyov was a Russian army officer and Left Socialist Revolutionary who commanded Red forces after the October Revolution. In January and February 1918 he led the Bolshevik advance on Kyiv, shelling the city and carrying out mass executions after its capture.

manfredo-fanti.s: Manfredo Fanti was an Italian general of the Risorgimento, born in the Duchy of Modena. Exiled after the revolt of 1831, he fought in Spain's Carlist War and then served the Kingdom of Sardinia.

mesannepadda.s: Mesannepadda was a king of Ur around 2500 BCE, named in the Sumerian King List as the founder of the First Dynasty of Ur. His name appears on contemporary objects, including a seal from the Royal Cemetery of Ur and a bead found at Mari, and he also bore the title king of Kish,…

meskalamdug.s: Meskalamdug was a ruler of Ur around 2600–2500 BCE, known from finds in the Royal Cemetery excavated by Leonard Woolley. A grave holding his name yielded a celebrated helmet beaten from a single sheet of gold in the form of a wig, now in the Iraq Museum.

medjerda.s: The Medjerda, the ancient Bagradas, is the longest river of Tunisia, rising in north-eastern Algeria and flowing about 450 km to the Gulf of Tunis. Its valley was the grain land of Carthage and of the Roman province of Africa.

manghud.s: The Manghud, or Mangit, were a Mongol tribe that became Turkic-speaking in the Golden Horde. Under the emir Edigu around 1400 they formed the core of the Nogai Horde, and other Mangit clans joined the Uzbek confederation of Abu'l-Khayr Khan.

ma-river.s: The Ma River is a river of northern Laos and north-central Vietnam, about 500 km long, flowing south-east through Thanh Hoa province to the Gulf of Tonkin. Its lower valley is one of the cradles of Vietnamese civilisation, home with the Red River delta to the Dong Son culture,…

makhado.s: Makhado was a king of the Venda in the Soutpansberg region of what is now Limpopo province, South Africa, from 1864 until his death in 1895. He led Venda resistance against the Boers of the Zoutpansberg, whose attacks in 1867 forced them to abandon the settlement of Schoemansdal.

mphephu.s: Mphephu was a king of the Venda in the Soutpansberg, successor of Makhado from 1895. He refused to submit to the South African Republic, which sent a large expedition against him in 1898; he fled north across the Limpopo, and Venda territory was annexed to the Transvaal.

morbihan.s: Morbihan is a department of Brittany in north-western France, with its prefecture at Vannes, named after the Gulf of Morbihan, Breton for 'little sea'. The gulf is an inland sea dotted with islands, opening to the Atlantic through a narrow channel.

marco-antonio-bragadin.s: Marco Antonio Bragadin was the Venetian governor of Famagusta in Cyprus during the Ottoman invasion of 1570–1571. He defended the city through a siege of almost a year until supplies ran out and surrendered on terms in August 1571.

methoni.s: Methoni is a small port town in Messenia, on the south-western tip of the Peloponnese in Greece, dominated by a great sea fortress. Held by Venice from about 1207 to 1500 as Modon, it was, with Coron, one of the 'eyes of the Republic' and a station for galleys and pilgrims on…

morean-war.s: The Morean War was the war of 1684–1699 between the Republic of Venice and the Ottoman Empire, part of the Great Turkish War. Venetian forces under Francesco Morosini conquered the Peloponnese (the Morea) between 1685 and 1687 and briefly took Athens, where a shell exploded…

merymose.s: Merymose was viceroy of Kush, the 'King's Son of Kush', under Amenhotep III in the early 14th century BCE. He governed Egyptian Nubia and led the army against the rebellious land of Ibhet in the king's fifth regnal year, as recorded in inscriptions.

montoire-sur-le-loir.s: Montoire-sur-le-Loir is a small town in the Loir-et-Cher department of central France. On 24 October 1940 Marshal Philippe Pétain met Adolf Hitler at its railway station, and the handshake between them became the symbol of the Vichy regime's policy of collaboration with Nazi…

mithila.s: Mithila is a region of the eastern Gangetic plain, between the Ganges and the Himalayan foothills, now divided between northern Bihar in India and the eastern Terai of Nepal. It was the land of the Vedic kingdom of Videha and later of the Karnat and Oiniwar dynasties, and it…

mysore.s: Mysore (Mysuru) is a city in southern Karnataka, India. According to tradition it became the seat of the Wodeyar dynasty in 1399, and the Wodeyars rose from local chiefs under Vijayanagara to rulers of the Kingdom of Mysore.

morlaas.s: Morlaàs is a small town north-east of Pau in the Pyrénées-Atlantiques department of south-western France. In the 11th and 12th centuries it was the capital of the viscounts of Béarn, whose mint there struck the widely circulated Morlaàs pennies, and its church of Sainte-Foy…

mont-ventoux.s: Mont Ventoux is a mountain in Provence, south-eastern France, rising to 1,910 metres north-east of Avignon, the highest peak in the region. Its bare limestone summit is visible from far across the Rhône valley.

maison-carree.s: The Maison Carrée is a Roman temple in Nîmes, southern France, built under Augustus and dedicated around the turn of the era to his grandsons and adopted heirs Gaius and Lucius Caesar. It is one of the best-preserved Roman temples anywhere, a model of classical architecture…

mastarna.s: Mastarna (Etruscan Macstrna) was an Etruscan warrior shown in the François Tomb at Vulci freeing Caelius Vibenna. The emperor Claudius, in a speech preserved on the Lyon Tablet, identified him with Servius Tullius, the sixth king of Rome, citing Etruscan sources that made him…

madockawando.s: Madockawando was a Penobscot sachem in what is now Maine, whose daughter married the French officer Jean-Vincent d'Abbadie de Saint-Castin. In King William's War he led attacks on English settlements, including the attack on Wells in 1692, while also negotiating with the…

mashpee-wampanoag-tribe.s: The Mashpee Wampanoag Tribe is a Native American tribe centred on the town of Mashpee on Cape Cod, Massachusetts. Mashpee was set aside in the 17th century as a self-governing community for Christian Native people and remained largely Wampanoag for centuries.

massasoit.s: Massasoit, also called Ousamequin, was the sachem, or paramount leader, of the Wampanoag in the early 17th century, ruling from Sowams in present-day Rhode Island. In March 1621 he made a treaty of mutual defence with the Pilgrims of Plymouth Colony, and that autumn he shared…

metacom.s: Metacom, also called Metacomet and known to the English as King Philip, was a sachem of the Wampanoag and a son of Massasoit. He succeeded his brother Wamsutta in 1662 and faced growing pressure from English settlers on Wampanoag land.

maasai-people.s: The Maasai are a Nilotic people of southern Kenya and northern Tanzania who speak Maa and traditionally live by herding cattle, organised in age sets of warriors and elders. In the 19th century they dominated much of the grazing land of the Rift Valley.

mumias.s: Mumias is a town in Kakamega County, western Kenya, near the Nzoia River. It grew around the court of the Wanga kingdom and takes its name from Nabongo Mumia, who welcomed British caravans there in the late 19th century, when it served as an early colonial station.

machchhu-river.s: The Machchhu is a river of the Saurashtra peninsula in Gujarat, western India, flowing north past Wankaner and Morbi towards the Little Rann of Kutch. The former princely states of Wankaner and Morvi grew up on its banks.

mohamoud-ali-shire.s: Mohamoud Ali Shire was sultan of the Warsangali in the Sanaag region of northern Somalia in the early 20th century. He supported the Dervish movement of Mohammed Abdullah Hassan against British rule, and in 1920, after the defeat of the Dervishes, the British exiled him to the…

mitakshara.s: The Mitakshara is a commentary on the Yajnavalkya Smriti, a Sanskrit text on Hindu law, written by the jurist Vijnaneshvara at the court of the Western Chalukya king Vikramaditya VI in the late 11th or early 12th century. It became the most influential authority on Hindu law…

miami-people.s: The Miami are an Algonquian-speaking Native American people who in the 18th century lived around the headwaters of the Maumee and Wabash rivers in present-day Indiana and Ohio, with a main town at Kekionga. Under leaders such as Little Turtle they formed part of the Western…

mandate-of-heaven.s: The Mandate of Heaven, tianming in Chinese, is the doctrine that Heaven grants the right to rule to a virtuous ruler and withdraws it from a wicked or incompetent one. It was formulated by the early Zhou to justify their overthrow of the Shang dynasty around 1046 BCE.

montego-bay.s: Montego Bay is a city on the north-west coast of Jamaica and the capital of the parish of St James. A centre of the sugar trade in the colonial period, it was at the heart of the 1831–1832 Christmas Rebellion of enslaved people led by Samuel Sharpe.

mbashe-river.s: The Mbashe River, formerly called the Bashee, flows south-east through the Eastern Cape of South Africa to the Indian Ocean. In Xhosa tradition the land between the Mbashe and the Kei was the core of the territory where the royal Tshawe lineage asserted supremacy over other…

morelos.s: Morelos is a small state of central Mexico south of Mexico City, with Cuernavaca as its capital. Its warm valleys were settled by Nahua peoples and contain the hilltop city of Xochicalco, and in colonial times it became a sugar-growing region.

makimuku.s: Makimuku is an archaeological site in Sakurai, Nara Prefecture, Japan, at the foot of Mount Miwa. In the early 3rd century it grew into a large planned settlement with a major building complex and some of the earliest keyhole-shaped tombs, including Hashihaka.

mirza-abu-bakr-dughlat.s: Mirza Abu Bakr Dughlat (died c. 1514) was an amir of the Dughlat clan who built an independent realm in Kashgar, Yarkand and Khotan in the late 15th century, nominally within Moghulistan.

moses.s: Moses is the central prophet of Judaism and an important figure in Christianity and Islam. According to the Hebrew Bible he led the Israelites out of slavery in Egypt and received the law, including the Ten Commandments, from God at Mount Sinai, and the first five books of the…

muhammad-ibn-yahya-hamid-al-din.s: Muhammad ibn Yahya Hamid al-Din, who ruled as Imam al-Mansur Muhammad, was the Zaydi imam of Yemen from 1890 to 1904 and the founder of the Hamid al-Din dynasty. He led repeated risings against Ottoman rule in the highlands, including sieges of Sanaa, and his resistance was…

minusinsk-basin.s: The Minusinsk Basin is a lowland on the upper Yenisei River in southern Siberia, ringed by the Sayan and Kuznetsk Alatau mountains, today in Khakassia and Krasnoyarsk Krai, Russia. Its fertile steppe was a centre of Bronze and Iron Age cultures such as the Afanasievo, Karasuk…

michua.s: Michuá was a zaque, ruler of the northern Muisca of Hunza in the Colombian highlands, in the late 15th century. According to Muisca tradition he fought the zipa Saguamanchica of Bacatá, and both rulers were killed in the Battle of Chocontá around 1490.

miroslav-of-hum.s: Miroslav (died c. 1199) was prince of Hum (Zachlumia), on the southern Adriatic coast, from the 1160s and a brother of the Serbian grand prince Stefan Nemanja.

miroslav-gospel.s: The Miroslav Gospel is an illuminated Cyrillic gospel book written around 1180–1190 for Prince Miroslav of Hum, brother of Stefan Nemanja. Richly decorated with initials combining Byzantine and Romanesque motifs, it is one of the oldest surviving documents in the Serbian…

messina.s: Messina is a port city in north-eastern Sicily, Italy, on the strait that separates the island from the mainland. Founded by Greeks in the 8th century BCE as Zancle and renamed Messana, it was seized by the Mamertines, whose appeal to Rome triggered the First Punic War in 264…

mylae.s: Mylae was an ancient Greek city on the north coast of Sicily, founded by settlers from Zancle in the 8th century BCE on the site of modern Milazzo. Off its coast in 260 BCE the Roman fleet, using the boarding bridge known as the corvus, won its first great naval victory over…

mala-khortytsia.s: Mala Khortytsia is a small island in the Dnieper river at Zaporizhzhia, Ukraine, west of the larger island of Khortytsia. Around 1552 Prince Dmytro Vyshnevetsky built a wooden fortress there, whose remains have been excavated, and it is often seen as the site of the first…

mixe.s: The Mixe, who call themselves Ayuuk, are an Indigenous people of the mountains of north-eastern Oaxaca, Mexico, speaking a language of the Mixe-Zoque family. From their rugged homeland around Zempoaltépetl they resisted the Zapotecs and the Aztecs and were only slowly brought…

muslim-ibn-quraysh.s: Muslim ibn Quraysh, called Sharaf al-Dawla, was the Uqaylid emir of Mosul from 1061 to 1085 and one of the leading Arab princes of Iraq and Syria under Seljuk overlordship. He took Aleppo in 1080 and held Harran and other towns of the Jazira.

mount-kailash.s: Mount Kailash is a peak of 6,638 metres in the Transhimalaya of Ngari, western Tibet. Sacred to Hindus as the abode of Shiva and also to Buddhists, Jains and followers of Bon, it is the goal of a pilgrimage circuit around its base, and its summit has never been climbed.

mahdia.s: Mahdia is a port city on the east coast of Tunisia, built on a narrow peninsula. Founded in 916 by the first Fatimid caliph, Abdallah al-Mahdi, it was the Fatimid capital until 948 and later the last stronghold of the Zirids after the Hilalian invasions.

mpande.s: Mpande kaSenzangakhona was king of the Zulu from 1840 to 1872, a half-brother of Shaka and Dingane. With Boer support he overthrew Dingane in 1840 and went on to reign longer than any other Zulu king, keeping peace with the British in Natal at the cost of the land south of the…

melmoth-osborn.s: Sir Melmoth Osborn was a British colonial official in Natal and Zululand. He served as British resident in Zululand after the Anglo-Zulu War and, when Britain annexed the territory in 1887, became its resident commissioner and chief magistrate, governing from Eshowe through…

medo-babylonian-conquest-of-the-assyrian.n: Medo-Babylonian conquest of the Assyrian Empire
medo-babylonian-conquest-of-the-assyrian.s: The Medo-Babylonian conquest of the Assyrian Empire was the war of 626–609 BCE in which Babylonia under Nabopolassar, joined from 615 BCE by the Medes under Cyaxares, destroyed the Neo-Assyrian Empire. Assur fell in 614 BCE and Nineveh was sacked in 612 BCE; the last Assyrian…

muslim-conquest-of-persia.s: The Muslim conquest of Persia was the conquest of the Sasanian Empire by the Rashidun Caliphate between 633 and the early 650s. Arab victories at al-Qadisiyyah (636) and Nahavand (642) opened Iraq and the Iranian plateau to the invaders, and the death of the last Sasanian…

mexican-war-of-independence.s: The Mexican War of Independence was the armed conflict of 1810–1821 that ended Spanish rule in New Spain. It began with Miguel Hidalgo's call to revolt at Dolores on 16 September 1810 and was carried on by José María Morelos and later by guerrilla leaders such as Vicente…

makassar-war.s: The Makassar War (1666–1669) was fought between the Dutch East India Company (VOC), allied with the Bugis prince Arung Palakka of Bone, and the Sultanate of Gowa in southern Sulawesi under Sultan Hasanuddin. The Treaty of Bongaya (1667) forced Gowa to cede territory and accept…

mongol-invasions-of-anatolia.s: The Mongol invasions of Anatolia were the campaigns by which the Mongol Empire subdued the Seljuk Sultanate of Rum in the mid-13th century. A Mongol army under Baiju defeated Sultan Kaykhusraw II at Köse Dağ in 1243, making the sultanate a tributary, and Baiju defeated the…

muslim-conquest-of-the-maghreb.s: The Muslim conquest of the Maghreb was the conquest of North Africa west of Egypt by the Rashidun and Umayyad caliphates between 647 and 709. Early raids were followed by the founding of Kairouan by Uqba ibn Nafi in about 670, while Berber resistance under Kusaila and the…

mughal-maratha-wars.s: The Mughal–Maratha Wars, also called the Deccan Wars, were fought from 1680 to 1707 between the Mughal Empire under Aurangzeb and the Maratha kingdom founded by Shivaji. Aurangzeb campaigned in the Deccan for over twenty years and had Shivaji's son Sambhaji executed in 1689,…

mongol-invasions-of-the-levant.s: The Mongol invasions of the Levant were the attacks on Syria and Palestine by the Mongol Empire and its successor, the Ilkhanate, from the 1240s to the early 14th century. Hülegü's army sacked Aleppo and took Damascus in 1260, but the Mamluks defeated the Mongols at Ain Jalut…

moro-rebellion.s: The Moro Rebellion was an armed conflict from 1899 to 1913 between the United States Army and the Muslim Moro peoples of Mindanao, the Sulu Archipelago and neighbouring islands in the southern Philippines. It went on after the main Philippine–American War ended in 1902, and…

mahdist-war.s: The Mahdist War was fought from 1881 to 1899 in Sudan between the followers of Muhammad Ahmad, who proclaimed himself the Mahdi, and the Egyptian government backed by Britain. The Mahdists took Khartoum in 1885, killing Charles Gordon, and built their own state, which an…

muscovite-lithuanian-wars.s: The Muscovite–Lithuanian Wars were a series of wars from 1487 to 1537 between the Grand Duchy of Moscow and the Grand Duchy of Lithuania, allied with Poland, over the Rus' lands between them. Moscow gained much territory, including Chernigov and Smolensk, taken in 1514 despite…

mad-war.s: The Mad War was a conflict of 1485–1488 between the French crown, governed by Anne of France during the minority of Charles VIII, and a coalition of nobles led by Louis of Orléans and Duke Francis II of Brittany. The royal victory at Saint-Aubin-du-Cormier in 1488 ended the…

muslim-conquest-of-transoxiana.s: The Muslim conquest of Transoxiana was the gradual conquest of the lands between the Oxus and Jaxartes rivers in Central Asia by the Umayyad and early Abbasid caliphates, from the 670s to the mid-8th century. Qutayba ibn Muslim took Bukhara and Samarkand between 705 and 715,…

mongol-invasion-of-europe.s: The Mongol invasion of Europe was the campaign of 1236–1242 in which Mongol armies under Batu Khan and Subutai conquered the Volga Bulgars and the principalities of Rus' and then invaded Poland and Hungary. They won at Legnica and Mohi in April 1241, but withdrew in 1242,…

mongol-invasion-of-kievan-rus.s: The Mongol invasion of Kievan Rus' began with a raid that defeated the Rus' princes at the Kalka River in 1223 and became a full conquest under Batu Khan in 1237–1240. Ryazan, Vladimir and many other cities were destroyed and Kyiv fell in December 1240; the Rus' principalities…

mongol-invasion-of-volga-bulgaria.s: The Mongol invasion of Volga Bulgaria was the series of campaigns from 1223 to 1236 against the Bulgar state on the middle Volga. After the Volga Bulgars ambushed a Mongol force returning from the Kalka in 1223, Batu Khan's great western campaign destroyed their cities,…

myanmar-civil-war-2021-present.s: The Myanmar civil war is the armed conflict that followed the military coup of February 2021, in which the army overthrew Aung San Suu Kyi's elected government. The People's Defence Forces of the opposition National Unity Government and long-established ethnic armed…

mongol-invasions-of-georgia.s: The Mongol invasions of Georgia began with raids by the generals Jebe and Subutai in 1220–1222, which defeated the Georgian armies of King George IV. A full invasion in the 1230s overran the kingdom, and in 1243 Queen Rusudan accepted Mongol overlordship.

mainz-diocesan-feud.s: The Mainz Diocesan Feud was a war of 1461–1462 over the archbishopric of Mainz between Diether von Isenburg and Adolf II of Nassau, whom the pope had appointed after deposing Diether. Diether's ally Frederick I of the Palatinate won the Battle of Seckenheim in 1462, but…

mughal-war-of-succession-1657-1661.s: The Mughal war of succession broke out when the emperor Shah Jahan fell ill in 1657 and his four sons fought for the throne. Aurangzeb, allied at first with Murad Bakhsh, defeated his brother Dara Shikoh at Samugarh in 1658, imprisoned his father and was crowned.

muscovite-lithuanian-war-1500-1503.s: The Muscovite–Lithuanian War of 1500–1503 was fought between Ivan III of Moscow and the Grand Duchy of Lithuania under Alexander Jagiellon, after border princes changed allegiance to Moscow. The Muscovites won a major victory at Vedrosha in 1500, while their Livonian allies…

mithridatic-wars.s: The Mithridatic Wars were three wars fought between the Roman Republic and Mithridates VI of Pontus from 89 to 63 BCE. Mithridates overran Roman Asia and Greece in 88 BCE but was driven back by Sulla, and later fought Murena, Lucullus and Pompey.
